title: So is it private or not?
text: I didn’t try the app just yet because I’m confused. App Store description and privacy-nutrition label says you do not collect data and data processing is done on device but the linked privacy policy says that you process the data in your offices or at the location of third-parties involved and that our data might be stored in a different country than ours. It also says that you may retain the data for as long as you need it. So which one is it? Do you collect and retain data or not? Legally, and I’m not a lawyer, if I was to complain about you collecting data you would refer me to your privacy policy even though your app description and privacy label says otherwise. In both case, you refer to your privacy policy for more details. So, you should probably revise your privacy policy.

title: Lack of most useful metric views or groups
text: I expected this app to fill the void Apple Fitness Trends and Summaries leaves to users. But Fitness View doesn’t seem to fulfill that gap either. One example: My running group and I would like to see a simple view that is easy to find the total running or hiking distance per time period with total elevation gain. As it is now elevation gain seems to be a unrepresented totaled metric.  Also not clear if “running + walking distance” includes “Hiking”.  Being able to pair multiple exercise metrics into a time range view would be great.  examples :  Running + Hiking Distance with Elevation gain over a week/month/year  Biking distance + elevation gain over week/month/year Biking + Running distance + elevation gain over week/month/year    Also, there is no group/team metric view, that is really disappointing one of the biggest missing data points with Apple Watch/Fitness is even when “Competing” it is only based on Ring closures as opposed to more goal/metric based numbers such as a group goals. For example a group goal to individually run 200 miles a month and see how everyone is doing in near real time. Or to bike 30K elevation gain in a month. As it is now that can only be done partially through Strava/Fitness and adding up each individual session manually.  App has potential but really just a slightly more in depth Apple fitness app.  Also the widgets never get created and my app always crashes (on latest iOS).  Happy to re-review after updates or speak to developers more.  Had high hopes for app even with premium version it disappoints still.

The other minor issue I encountered today is that the app auto-paused my workout when I stopped to pick up my dog’s poo. Pausing is fine, I just didn’t know it had happened. I didn’t realize it until 3-4 minutes later when I looked at my watch to check my heart rate. Not a deal breaker, I just would have liked a discernible alert on my watch. (And if the app noticed I paused walking, why couldn’t it detect when I started moving again?) Overall, I really enjoy the app, its Apple Watch abilities, and its integration with the Activity app. Definitely worth $9.99/year.

gist: best health reader app, great 2.0 features
title: This is now the best “reader” app for health data
text: The app now exceeds the functionality of its predecessor, along with having a much nicer UI and more pleasant UX.  There might still be a few calculation or typographical quirks, but the new 2.0 update has a number of great additional features , weekly and monthly goals being a couple of my favorites.  I can recommend this app to anyone without reservation and am very impressed by Funn Media’s focus determination for taking this app from where it was initially to the gem that it is right now. [Update - 21 Sep] Getting there… Dark Mode and some calculations I just checked have been fixed with v1.1.1. Added a star and will keep checking for other improvements. Original Review - Still not ready… A reviewer from two months ago mentioned how Dark Mode was messed up. I actually waited to write this review until the most recent update (v1.1), thinking an update would be released around the same time as iOS 15. Once I saw that Dark Mode had not been fixed , it only looks right on the Settings tab. To be honest, I really do not know what to make of this app. Full transparency, I have lifetime subscriptions to three other apps from Funnmedia (the developer). Two of those other apps I use daily. I like what Funnmedia is trying to do. They actually used to have an app called HealthView that did/does almost exactly the same thing as this FitnessView app, but HealthView is now “owned” by Reflectly. Although the UI is a little dated, HealthView showed/shows way more metrics than FitnessView , some of which are important (e.g., Net Calories , which is a calculation and not actually something that is in the iOS Health app; Total Fat , not just Saturated Fat). Hopefully, Funnmedia will add all of the metrics/calculations from HealthView. At least include more metrics that make sense. Why is there only Saturated Fat and not Total Fat? Net Calories is way more meaningful than Nike Fuel. (Nike doesn’t even use Nike Fuel anymore.) Then there is the issue of what the “Insights” actually mean. Let’s use Water, for example, I see an Hourly Avg. of 17.33 US oz and a Daily Avg. of 61.66 US oz. I have recorded 52 oz today. It is 11:45p right now. What are these numbers calculating? Those numbers are from the “Home” tab. On the “Stats” tab for today, the Hourly Avg. is 0.59 US oz. What is that? I have recorded 52 oz in a 24-hour day. That should be over 2 oz per hour, right? Water is not the only metric with issues like this. From a widgets standpoint, the “Activity” ring goal shows the same three metrics (move, exercise, stand) as the Activity app. However, move is kcal instead of cal (no big deal). Exercise does not have a label (min) at all, just numbers; and when you get to an hour, instead of showing 60 minutes, it shows 1:00. That means if your goal is 30 exercise minutes for a day and you earn 60 exercise minutes that day, your exercise progress is displayed as “1:00/30”. If you’re not going to make this better than the Health and Activity apps, at least make it the same , not worse. Remember, this app can only replace the user’s view of their own statistics. Users still have to use the iOS Activity app to see what their friends/family are doing. They shouldn’t have to figure out what they are looking at based on the app. For this to be an app that just “reads” information from the iOS Health app, there are really only two things on which to focus , 1) making accurate calculations; and 2) presenting the data in an easy to understand and aesthetically pleasing way. This app is not doing that yet , which is odd because Funnmedia just had an app that does almost the same thing. I am hopeful that they will address some of this stuff soon , even though there are still some issues with one of their other apps that I emailed them about over a year ago. I was told that all of them were added to their “future update”, but it has been 15 months now. To be clear, I am an overall fan of what Funnmedia is trying to do from an app standpoint, but I get the impression that there are other business issues getting in the way of the apps really offering the solid user experience that one might expect. I will gladly edit/update this review with each update that addresses some of the issues I mentioned.

text: Die FitnessView App ist ein sehr gelungenes Dashboard für Gesundheitsdaten. Besonders hervorzuheben ist die Widget-Funktion: Sie schließt genau die Lücken, die in der Apple Fitness App bestehen – und das im typischen, klaren Apple-Stil. Die Widgets sind frei belegbar und lassen sich individuell anpassen. Auch die bekannten Ringe können flexibel konfiguriert werden, was einen echten Mehrwert für die persönliche Übersicht bietet. Was die App zusätzlich besonders macht: Auch das Dashboard innerhalb der App ist komplett anpassbar. Diese Flexibilität zieht sich konsequent durch die gesamte App und sorgt dafür, dass man sich alles genau so einrichten kann, wie es am besten zum eigenen Alltag passt. Ich bin rundum zufrieden mit der App. Auch das Preismodell ist fair – vor allem, weil es regelmäßig gute Angebote gibt. And from my mental remembrance, I’ve walked at most six times on them in the last week, however it counts no amount. Additionally, the calories, I go on a NordicTrack treadmill in my house and when I take note of how many calories were burned, I also check on the app to see if it corresponds. However, it doesn’t even seem to count half the amount of calories burned. As a result, for these bits of information, I’ve taken out a half-star for each one, leaving 4 out of 5 stars. This is a good and very useful app, one that I absolutely love, however, it needs some slight fixing. The steps and tracked minutes of walking seem satisfactory, despite the slightly difference in walking; 50 steps and no change has been monitored, however, walking 50 more steps at a greater than the previous one adds in those steps. title: The best!
text: So positive and encouraging! I’ve used many pedometer apps over the years, finally landing on this one, but set it aside when I got my Apple Watch a few years ago. Rehabbing from three spinal fusions in the last two years, my PT encouraged me to track my steps , not just a daily goal, but a weekly one too. I remembered this app’s option to a) not lose a streak if one day was missed and b) set a weekly goal. It’s perfect for where I’m at: prioritizing my weekly goal means I can fall short of my daily goal once (or even twice) a week and still feel successful and proud of my progress (rather than like a failure for missing one day).  I appreciate how easy it is to see my complete history, going back over 10 years. I can track the months and years that I walked more/less and what was going on in my life/health. One unexpected insight I gleaned upon returning to this app is how drastically my step count dropped when I started serious weightlifting. As a personal trainer, I know that our bodies are built to ambulate. Apple Watch is less geared toward tracking steps as much as it is tracking activity. I want and need to track both for balanced and healthy mobility and functional fitness.  Right mow, I’m walking far more than I would without this app and have no plans to stop using it, even once my rehab is complete. Thank you!!

Apple, if you read reviews and if you’re seeking ways to make users truly fall in love with the fitness functionality capabilities of the Apple Watch, you should partner with this Developer. gist: requires write permission to all health data
title: Privacy
text: It is disappointing that the app will not work without granting permission to read and write all health data. It’s not clear why the app needs write access, but it will refuse to open if it isn’t given it. It would be much better if you could select what the app is allowed to view, and then the app will work with whatever data it has been given, rather than an all or nothing approach. Edit: thanks for the response. I understand Apple can only let you show the pop up once asking for permissions, but most apps get around this by not allowing you to do an action you haven’t allowed permission for. So in this case, not allowing you to start a workout recording and instead have a link to privacy tab in settings explaining that the app needs write access.  This is how every other app I have installed deals with privacy permissions, rather than not opening without all permissions checked. As an example, Instagram app works fine without camera permission, unless you try and take a photo in which case it is a splash screen with a link to privacy in settings.

gist: I do not want a freaking stand notification in the middle of the night, especially
title: Mostly I love it, but….
text: I really like the watch, and it is particularly the Activity app I value. It has really helped motivate me to get up and move, and seeing the payoff in health stats is really rewarding. A significant flaw, though, is the inability to tailor notifications more. I LIKE the stand notifications: they help me be mindful of time passing when I’m caught up in work or reading, so I will be sure to get up and move around throughout the day.  I do not want a freaking stand notification in the middle of the night, especially since the reason it goes off is that the watch has noted I am restless. The little alert is just enough to tip me from restlessly sleeping to “thanks for waking me ALL the way up, Apple!” But I wear the watch because it is the most considerate alarm option, sufficient to wake me at 5 am for work but let my husband sleep on. Q&A on the internet shows people have been saying this for 5 years. Fix it, Apple! Also, though less urgent, I DO like alerts telling me I’ve met my move, exercise, or stand goal for the day. I do like when the day is winding down being reminded if i have not met a goal. I do NOT like all the “badges.” I am not 6, I do not want a gold star or a “badge” and a “good job!” How hard would it be to let folks choose the notifications they want, instead of all notifications on or off?

gist: I decided to try the free trial of Fitness +, but I really didn’t think
title: Unexpectedly Wonderful
text: I purchased an Apple Watch to help me keep track of my activity for health reasons. I decided to try the free trial of Fitness +, but I really didn’t think I would use it. I was surprised by how much I love it.  Apple has put together a diverse, talented, and positive team. I look forward to spending part of my day with these folks. I love how they bring who they are into their workout, sharing culture, family stories, and music along with positive encouragement. I love that modifications are offered every time. I have a long way to go before I can match the trainers without mods, but I don’t feel bad about myself because of the easy and positive way they are offered.  I do have one small disappointment- I was very excited to see that Pilates was being added. However, it doesn’t seem to be classic Pilates. I’ve only done one class so far, but there was no Hundred, no roll ups, no focus on breathing… I’m not really sure what makes it possible to call this “Pilates.” I wish they were offering real Pilates classes.  Overall, though, this is a fantastic offering and it has really been helping me stay motivated to continue to meet my exercise goals.

The hike was strenuous and as my ski/hiking pole or mountaineering boots & skis broke through the snow, the App would ask me if I had fallen. And it did that dozens of times. gist: Fitness+ yoga content disliked; cancelled trial
title: Avoid if looking for yoga content
text: I’ve tried out the free trial to see if it has any interesting yoga content for me to mix up my practice, and cancelled it after a few days. I’m sure the workout tracking features are alright, but the content is definitely not for me. It’s all “OHMYGAAAAWD LET’S DO SOME CARDIO”, and little else that I’ve been able to find. It feels very obnoxious and like it caters exclusively to a cliché parody of Californians. It considers “yoga” to be one single amorphous thing, high-intensity flows performed by overenthusiastic Americans in overdecorated studios to Gen Z music (no wonder given Apple Music’s obsession with the same niche I suppose). No labelling or way of filtering by type of practice (there are a tremendously diverse set of kinds of yoga) or any useful descriptions of individual sessions (only a marketing preview for each video). I’ve tried a lot of yoga apps on the App Store, and honestly, not a single one is worse than this. Maybe the other kinds of workout are better?

They each have a style and you can end up wasting time with a workout or cooldown that just does not work for you. ** whatever the follow was appears to have been resolved ** The ugly… Deep breath. The link between AppleTV and apple watch is spindly and delicate. Connecting takes minutes not moments. Not the WiFi as I am streaming 4K to this AppleTV with no issues. And once connected they almost always stay connected but that initial connect is stubborn. If the watch and tv don’t want to play nice you can airplay from your phone but that means dragging the stream over WiFi and pushing it to Apple TV so if you get a blip you can get tossed out of your 30 minute run 26 minutes in while doing an all out push. Oops. This is very frustrating and sometimes overshadows the otherwise content being produced. text: As others gave said, the filters need a bit of work. And please make the workouts less preachy. I just want to train, not get lectured about representation etc. Interestingly, there are no ugly people represented. Integration with the Watch is ok. I don’t see how having the rings displayed on the screen suddenly transforms your workout when it’s literally on your wrist.  It’s also incredibly stereotypically AMERICAN. Everything is AWESOME to the MAX. I’m a fat cynical Irishman who feels no connection to some toned hunk/babe telling me to dig deep within myself for the final hill. That said, the trainers are very pleasant with lots of perfectly toothy smiles and singing/rapping along with the music. This may or may not be a plus - I find it utterly irritating sometimes, but tolerable other times. Often, I wish I could just play my own music in the background.  All in all, for the price, it’s decent enough - depending on what equipment you have at home, it’s a fraction of the cost of a gym membership. title: Good start!
text: I love that the workouts start automatically on my Apple Watch, that captions are an option (and some trainers use a little bit of ASL here and there), and that the trainers put out a welcoming and inclusive energy. What I’d like:  - More adjustments for people with disabilities (given that they’ve been cleared for exercise by a physician), especially anyone wheelchair-bound. These adjustments can be easy to do, and for some workouts, someone can give adjustment suggestions at the start. Giving workouts that have this option a specific tag would also help. - Morning yoga, stretch breaks - shorter workouts for when you need to move a bit but don’t have time for a full workout. These could go under the 5min tag in their respective categories or go under a “move break” type category all their own. - Meditation and stretch cross-overs (under the same 5minute tag I described above). You could even team up with the Ten Percent app for a mini mind-body challenge. This app has a lot of potential and as time passes, I am getting closer to cancelling my Peloton sub - but it’s not quite ready to replace it yet.

text: I am nearing the end of a 3 month trial of Apple Fitness+ and have loved it enough that I was planning to purchase a subscription, but with how it has been running over the past few weeks I definitely will not be. I especially love the dance workouts, but nearly every other one I have selected lately either hasn’t loaded so I have to find another one to do, or plays for 10-15 minutes and then crashes. When it crashes, there is no way to resume where I left off or to even fast forward to the point I left off at. This is SO frustrating!!! I work out in the mornings and don’t have time to deal with this and still get my workout in while getting to work on time. I’m super over it. I enjoyed the workouts when they’ve worked, but would never spend the money on an app subscription that only works half of the time.

gist: I want to like this app.
title: Inaccurate Tracking
text: I want to like this app. However, it very frequently frustrates me with inaccurate readings. For example, depending on which wrist I wear my watch on I will get completely different steps for the day. Another feature I found to be frustrating was that the stand hours often do not recognize that you were actually up, even when you were up and moving around; therefore not giving you the credit. Although it’s recorded your steps and movements. Even exercise times…why is this stand function sometimes not picking up?  I found that when I tried the trial version things appeared to be better for a few days…but after that I saw some of these same inconsistencies. For the amount you want to charge; improvement is needed. The search continues for a more accurate health and fitness app that is all in one. Just a shortfall to not have them together especially if you’re working with a professional in wellness; it would be so nice to have tools that were more cohesive and consistent.

gist: That said I only use it for yoga.

text: 1st- I think the Fitness section is designed nice and easy to use. Also, if you stand up for 1 minute or 30 minutes it automatically registers an hour. It CAN’T tell if you are awake or asleep. I was surprised when I re-read that. gist: Pushing a lawnmower registers, but not for all the time.
title: Fitness App
text: This app seems best suited to under 40s running round urban streets. It is not well adapted to many of the daily activities of older people. Heavy duty pick, shovel and wheelbarrow work over half days doesn’t register as exercise. Walking the dog may or may not be recognised. Pushing a lawnmower registers, but not for all the time. Strenuous axe work, chopping wood for heating, tends to provoke great alarm, and questions plural as to whether I’ve had a fall. On occasion it has had to be prevented from making emergency phone calls when there was no emergency, just a more than usually tough log. It’s all a bit frustrating and there’s no way to get rid of it or go to a more laidback persona.  This app would benefit from a capacity to work a personality change and a capacity to tell it once and once only that the impact it has just registered isn’t a dangerous fall.

gist: But my bigger gripe is with the search function.
title: Great workouts, app needs improvement
text: I have been doing the workouts with my Apple Watch for over 2 months (Pilates, hiit, strength, dance, yoga, meditation, walking). I really like the workouts. They are challenging (and accessible to beginners with the trainer on the side offering modifications). (I am a fit 50 year old) I like the trainers. There are people of all ages, shapes and nationalities. I like how it encourages me to finish a training with a cooldown that includes a meditation. I’d really like to see a series for women with pelvic floor exercises and other tailored work.  Minor irritants are the excessive (not sincere) smiling/happiness. But my bigger gripe is with the search function. It’s not well designed to help you find a workout: which Pilates works on your back - yoga balancing poses vs slow flows vs mat work - dance choreography vs dance exercises - which strength workout works your arms - which mindful cooldown works the part of your body you just worked on … etc And re the Rings: the targets are not easy to tailor. I’d love one for steps per day, one for general active or taking care of yourself  (walk, meditation) and one for real training.

gist: The base app that interacts with you periodically throughout the day is not terrible.
title: Leaves you wanting more…
text: The base app that interacts with you periodically throughout the day is not terrible. It does seem a little inaccurate, but it’s not not bad considering the price point for the watch it’s self.  The fitness + is definitely lacking. I can see it being useful if you are doing at home workouts with minimal equipment. It even seems to have a good amount of cardio based workouts. However, anyone who was hoping for bench/equipment based workouts is going to be disappointed.  I was personally hoping to find a list of workouts, or even a list of routines to choose from, for different muscle groups. It would have been nice to build your own routine, choose from existing routines, or even have a personalized one generated. Track your progress, in terms of how much weight you are putting up and reps, and have it more synchronized to your Apple Watch.  What you get is a list of categories - within those categories are lists of videos that you can click on and follow along with the trainer, and their pupils, in the traditional p90x fashion. Luckily, there is a filter so you could dwindle down the videos to what you’re looking for, but at first glance it’s just a list of videos you sift through to see what you want to try that day. It doesn’t appear to be routines, just different workouts to try, however, new content is added.  Summary: The free aspect of the “fitness” app isn’t terrible for what you’re paying for. However, I would wait until they expand fitness +, significantly, before trying this app out - especially if you are looking for bench/equipment based exercises. If you’re looking for high cardio workouts that require nothing but a mat and some dumbbells, this could work for you.

gist: I’ve always been enamored by dancers but never felt competent enough to join in.
title: Obsessed! Helped me get a 200 Day streak of exercise!
text: The powerhouse combo of the Apple Watch + Fitness+ has been a game changer for my fitness lifestyle.  Watch Love how the watch gives tangible goals for your level that progress with you. Love the dopamine rush when all of my rings close & it makes that little spinning firework. Love that I can congratulate and compete with friends! App Love the variety of workouts, especially dance! I’ve always been enamored by dancers but never felt competent enough to join in. These routines meet me where I am, are super fun, & provide a great quick burn. Also love the treadmill workouts! I’ve ALWAYS despised running, especially running “for no reason”… I reluctantly selected a treadmill workout one time at the gym for a quick 10-min warm up, and I’ve been obsessed ever since! It blows my mind that I can actually enjoy something that I’ve been convinced I’ve hated for the last 22 years.  My only WISH for the app is to have more detailed tracking. Now that I’m getting into running, I’d love it if it would show my previous paces/heart rates for each run I repeat. Same for other workouts (HIIT, cycling, strength, etc. would show heart rate & “lead the pack” placement). Now that this is a lifestyle, it would totally be fun to see if I’m progressing & to have a clear goal to challenge myself again each round.

text: Im Grunde genommen bekommt man mit Fitness+ nur Trainingsvideos, die es kostenlos und besser auch auf YouTube gibt. Nichts ist individuell. gist: My only substantial complaint about this app is that there are no playback controls beyond
title: Disappointed Daily User
text: My only substantial complaint about this app is that there are no playback controls beyond play and pause.  It’s frankly bewildering that users aren’t able to rewind/fast forward through workouts. I understand that the exercise sets are meant to be performed from start to finish in a carefully designed order, but sometimes an Internet connection is spotty, which can cause the video to pause itself to buffer for a moment. It doesn’t take long after that for the app to shut the video down, sending the user to the end-of-workout summary page with a “done” button. At this point, no mater where you are in the workout, the app seems to consider the workout completed with no option to pick up where you left off. After five months of near daily use, this has happened to me several times. It can happen halfway through a 30-minute workout and with no playback controls, you’re left to wait through the parts you’ve already done or do them all over again if you want to keep your heart rate up while you wait.  I often squeeze in a workout on my lunch break or in between meetings. So I just don’t have the luxury to stop and wait an extra 20 minutes to return to where I left off.  I love the trainers. I love the workouts. They’ve taught me an absolute ton about how to move my body properly during exercise, and I feel better and stronger for having these workouts (literally) in my back pocket.  But the lack of playback controls in the app make create a frequent and significant frustration. And according to the Apple Community Discussions Forum, I’m not alone in my frustrations.

gist: Fitness+ is great at one thing: making you want to buy an Apple Watch.
title: So disappointing
text: Fitness+ is great at one thing: making you want to buy an Apple Watch. From there it backslides. First: the tracking is pretty bad. I often get reminders to stand up WHILE I’M STANDING UP. Also, there is no discernible difference between the “Move” tracking and the “Activity” tracking. Admittedly, I don’t sit at a desk all day, so I guess that means I have an active lifestyle, but it must count going up a single flight of stairs as “activity.” Whether or not I close all my rings is a total crapshoot, even if I barely sit down all day.  But the real disappointment is the Fitness+ subscription workouts. The interface on the iPhone is unusable,so poorly designed. It is so bad it is simply not recognizable as an Apple product. Next, we can’t get it to play on our television, even though we subscribe to Apple+. And when I play it over my iPad, it will not pair with my watch, even though both are running fully updated software and Bluetooth is on. And lastly, for some bizarre reason, all the instructors are made to constantly wave their hands around when they are introducing their class, which is just comically bizarre. They must feel at least a little self-conscious about it because it is super unnatural looking. I try to laugh it off but you want to be able to take these people seriously. I thought it was just a workout thing but then it happened when I tried a meditation as well (which I immediately stopped and went back to longtime fave meditation app).  I definitely will not renew when my 3-month free trial period ends. Apple really missed out big time here.

gist: Apple has the power to make some chores not only more entertaining, but more inclusive.
title: Housework Workouts
text: Apple has the power to make some chores not only more entertaining, but more inclusive. I was doing some general cleaning in my house and was wondering if maybe I can select hoovering as a workout. I can’t now, but hopefully in the future Apple will make it available.  We already know from research done with hotel housekeepers that when they were told their work is part of a healthy lifestyle, not only did they lose weight but also enjoyed what they were doing more, which in turn resulted in an increased feeling of well-being.  Imagine your gym freak friend leaving your house a mess after a hang out. You can suggest that dish washing will burn a few calories and let them get going. Or your partner putting off some gardening because… reasons. If you’ve ever mowed the lawn or pulled weeds you know how demanding it is.  Think of busy people who sometimes don’t have time to exercise but look after full-of-energy children or clean the house of a sick parent. This is exercise. Ticking these exercise and movements goals is reinforcing and builds momentum.  Not to mention convincing more men that housework and raising children is also good for their health. This will help a lot of households, in my opinion.  🤞🤞

gist: I’ve tried Fitness+ and Echelon’s Reflect and both services suffer from the same key issue.
title: The problem with Fitness+ and similar services
text: I’ve tried Fitness+ and Echelon’s Reflect and both services suffer from the same key issue. When you’re working with people new to fitness form is honestly the most important thing as proper form can prevent injuries. I love old workout videos because they introduce an exercise, they take the time to break down the exercise including what good form looks like and common mistakes. This is done in slow motion with plenty of explanation and then they start the workout. Fitness+ is like hey beginners and right away starts a full-on workout and they’re like hey if you can do it pay attention to the people in the background who will be doing modified versions of the exercises. To date, I have yet to finish even the beginner exercises because it’s frustrating bordering on arrogant of you to assume that a beginner is just going to jump in and my favorite part - not even an option to rewind or jump back - if I want to check ok how was his or her form. That is a place where the Reflect and similar training services have a huge leg up - massive screens and in the case of the Reflect the height, size and brightness works out to where you can literally see yourself next to if not on the trainer so I can literally see if I’m squatting low enough - how does my form compare - the essential things that separate a quality workout from a quantity doing it just to feel good about closing my rings. Technique is a huge part of fitness yet no one wants to take the time to teach it properly.

title: Peut mieux faire
text: Quelques petites suggestions : -Pouvoir stopper un exercice en cour et revenir en arrière afin de pouvoir le répéter si on ne l’a pas bien réalisé du premier coup. -possibilité de trier les exercices par niveau: débutants, intermédiaires, confirmés ou facile, moyen difficile -proposer des exercices de renforcement , de pilate ou de gainage utilisant un ballon type swiss ball . Même si l’usage exclusif de l’anglais me permet de travailler cette langue, j’aimerais bien avoir la possibilité de choix entre une version française et une version anglaise. Cela pourrait aider lorsque je ne suis pas sur d’avoir tout compris! Enfin, comme l’a suggéré, un des critiques, l’engagement idéologique « politiquement correct », est souvent pénible. Une application sportive doit faire preuve d’une stricte neutralité politique. Les louanges et incantations  à toutes les minorités soi disant opprimées, n’y ont pas leur place. Elles peuvent aussi heurter la sensibilité de la majorité…au mépris des règles les plus élémentaires de la démocratie.

title: Super zum Wiedereinstieg und Weitermachen
text: Ich verstehe die schlechten Bewertungen hier größtenteils nicht. In Bezug auf das Fitness Programm kann ich nur 5 Sterne geben. Die Watch hat noch Potential und auch der Service. Habe schon einiges ausprobiert, um sportlich am Ball zu bleiben als berufstätig Anfang 50. Mit Apple Fitness klappt es endlich und ich genieße den internationalen und wirklich diversen Trainerpool. Meine Favoriten habe ich schnell gefunden, probiere gern auch immer wieder Neues aus. -Exzellente und versierte Trainer und Trainerinnen, die harmonieren -Humorvolle Anleitungen -Optionen/Modifikationen mit 3. Trainingsperson für Leistungsanpassungen sind sehr hilfreich -Das Englisch kann man sehr gut verstehen, wo nicht, ist das Video klar und man kann kurz zurückspulen und hat es beim nächsten Mal drauf -länge der Sessions mit max. 30Min super zum selber zusammenstellen mit Trainer- und Stilwechseln nach Tagesverfassung -sehr gute Musikabmischung sowie Videoaufnahmen und Lichtverhältnisse -inspirierende Looks durch Nike ohne zuviel ChiChi -Diversität (Körperbau, Alter, Ethnie) als Fitnessvorbild Perfekt für Menschen, die berufstätig sind und sich selber eigenverantwortlich die Gesundheit erhalten oder wieder herstellen wollen.

title: Geniales Programm

Besonders gut finde ich die Yoga-Angebote von Molly Fox und die Meditationen mit JoAnna. Danke an die beiden. Auch das übrige Team macht einen tollen Job und ist sehr empfehlenswert.

title: À travailler ?
text: L’idée et la mise à disposition de l’ensemble du suivi est sympa! Cependant avoir des cours dans sa langue maternelle est essentiel et je n’ai pas l’impression que Apple ai compris cette subtilité… comment méditer si l’on comprend rien à ce qui nous est dit ? Pour la partie renforcement/gainage, certes le visuel reste le support principal mais c’est en vocal que le coach donne les variantes des exercices pour les rendre plus ou moins intense en fonction des capacités… Je ne suis pas le premier à faire cette remontée et j’aimerais une réponse de la part de l’équipe de développeur pour m’assurer que nos retours soient réellement pris en compte… à quoi bon les faire sinon ?? Enfin, d’un point de vue « évolutions possibles », il serait intéressant de trouver des programmes type « reprise du sport », rééducation, préparation à des événements sportifs, etc. Et que ceux-ci interfèrent automatiquement avec la suite de logiciel Apple par exemple ajout au calendrier pour que l’entraînement soit régulier et progressif… Je suis en plein essai du mois gratuit, sans retour de l’équipe de développeurs je ne poursuivrais pas par un abonnement…

text: I want to start by saying I love the workouts and the trainers. Specifically Kyle, Kim and Greg. But the tech  ruins the experience.  The functionality of the whole set up is flawed. I specifically purchased a Apple Watch to use Fitness+. Using it with chrome cast and other non apple devices the workouts would pause for long periods and then eventually just drop out, leaving me with no option but to start the workout from the start. So I then got a Apple TV thinking this might help. Using the Apple TV is just a bunch of new problems. Often my watch won’t connect leaving me trying to get the workouts started sometimes taking up to 30 minutes just to get my watch recognised by the Apple TV, or even worse if your watch battery dies in the middle of a work out your done.  I normally love apple products but this is some really bad tech. And making it that you can only use the workouts but buying the watch makes no sense. Also I only do strength and core training. The watch ads no benefit to this type of workout. I do like my watch for other reasons but it in no way ads to the Apple fitness+ experience unless you are only counting calories.

gist: It’s such a small thing, but it feels like a reward,especially when it’s a special
title: Helpful, but…
text: I would really like it if notifications didn’t override the animation for closing rings. It’s such a small thing, but it feels like a reward,especially when it’s a special one, like my favorite watery rings,and gives me the extra motivation to get things done. But when I’m missing it more often than not because my watch thinks it’s more important to give me a notification that I’ve closed the rings or met a goal or something, it makes my ADHD brain less likely to put in the effort over time. Shouldn’t it be possible to be able to access that animation afterward, even if something interrupts? It’s just one of those small things that can actually mean a great deal. (And yes, I know there’s a feature that turns off the grouping of notifications, but for some reason it still does it anyway. Really annoying and demotivating.)

title: Mixed feelings on this App/service
text: I just got the Apple SE8 watch. With it was a trial to Fitness+.  My primary activity is Meditation, so that’s what I’m speaking to largely at the moment. I have to say that so far it feels like this is not a genuine effort for mindfulness/mental health practices.  My 3 major complaints:  1) Starting every episode with “…in the apple fitness+ studio in LA…”; this isn’t necessary for the purposes of the audience you’re targeting this activity to. We don’t want to hear “Apple” or promo/marketing narrations about anything while doing this. We already purchase your products and attempt your subscription services like Fitness+; there’s no reason for more efforts at promo.  Dive right into the meditation/lesson and go with it to get your listener into a flowing experience.  2) Too much repetition; I don’t really want to hear the instructor repeating the same scripted piece multiple times throughout the session. I want it to feel like a true genuine natural lesson directly from the instructor, providing different approaches/stories/perspectives to the lesson at hand.  3) Obnoxious background music transitions. Whoever edits these with the background music must not be in the mindfulness practice arena. There is not rhythmic or seemingly unnoticeable change in the background music. It just fades out randomly and a different track with a completely different tone/vibe/energy fades in, and often it’s right in a period of silence when the instructor isn’t speaking… that’s very distracting.  Yes this is mindfulness practice; but I feel as though my guided meditation is being vulnerably released into your hands - Take me through a consistent flowing experience with no unnecessary distractions.

Les coachs parlent trop vite, avec un vocabulaire trop spécifique pour mon petit niveau d'anglais ...  Les sous-titres ne servent strictement à rien : allez lire ce qui est écrit en tout petit sur votre iPhone en faisant des jumping jack, du yoga et bien de la méditation, où tu es censé avoir les yeux fermés ... bref quand on doit s'arrêter en permanence pour essayer de relire des sous-titres, ça ne sert à rien ! title: Good except for Workout Measurment
text: I bought my Apple Watch 6 for health reasons. I find the reminder rings very motivating. I feel like the movement ring (red) is accurate, and the stand ring (blue) is accurate. However, the workout ring and measurements are usually inaccurage because the app is too sensitive. When I take a shower, it thinks I’m doing yoga or swimming. When I’m just walking around at work, it thinks I’m doing a workout. The worst issue is that it starts recording the “workout” without my permission. I have already switched off the recommended toggle switches. Please add one more toggle switch that says NEVER START A WORKOUT AUOTMATICALLY, or ONLY START WORKOUTS MANUALLY,something chrystal clear as to the meaning and function. This would prevent the app from deciding to record workouts, which invalidate ALL of the data regarding workouts for the day, and long term.

gist: Could you please add a feature to adjust the playback speed of the dance videos?
title: Request enhancements
text: Could you please add a feature to adjust the playback speed of the dance videos? I like the routines, but they‘re just a little bit too fast for me. If I could reduce the speed by 10 to 20%, it would be a great improvement. I‘ve randomly found a few videos that allow you to reduce the playback speed by 50%, but that is way too much. Another enhancement would be to add some workouts (strength, yoga) that are tailored for people with knee problems. There are a LOT of us out here who either already have or are in the process of ruining our knees. So, workouts without squats or lunges would be great.  I know the workouts for older adults at least show modifications, but there are only a few videos, and they are, in some aspects, not demanding enough. So, maybe you could create a set of workouts for people who are otherwise strong and in shape, but have to be very careful with their knees.  This is also one of the reasons it would be good to be able to slow down the dance videos. There can be a lot of torque applied to the knees when trying to turn and step quickly, especially if one is not yet familiar with the basic movement or sequence of movements. I am an ex-dancer, and if I am having problems doing this stuff safely, I’m pretty sure it’s a general problem.

Folks don’t often think of doing core fitness, yoga, dancing, Tia Chi while sitting but we adjust as we must. Doing the twist while laying down is a lot harder than doing it standing up. text: When the new iOS update came out I was excited to try this as Apple is generally a reliable company , but to my surprise this app isn’t actually the greatest . My first issue is the fitness+ . People shouldn’t have to pay to have better fitness apps , it’s just wrong to have to pay for help with health . It should be mostly free to use . However , the biggest problem with the app is the fact that you NEED your phone with you or (I assume) an Apple Watch . I don’t know about you but when I go get exercise, my phone isn’t a priority . If I take my phone with me I’m bound to get distracted . So I left it at home and used a non-apple watch to count my steps , but when I came home I was disappointed to see that I couldn’t add my steps on to the move goal . Other than that , the app is ok but I recommended using something else like strava , where you can add the steps on . Luckily though , this has just come out so there’s lots of time to update it .

gist: I wanted to add/record a workout.
title: Fitness app without tracking fitness
text: I went to a gym. I wanted to add/record a workout. It’s a fitness app right? To track your activity and workouts, right? Exactly like it seemed on the screenshots in Appstore, right? Well. There is no option to add any workout. Sounds impossible for a fitness app to do not record the workouts because this is what the app seemed to be designed for, but it truly does not. At least in some countries in Europe, for no reason, Apple users cannot have this functionality and the app does not look like on the screenshots in Appstore. It turned out to be extremely primitive - it only calculates calories based on movement (steps I suppose) and you can follow other people. That’s all really. Completely useless and not even worth downloading, especially when you have so many great and free apps which actually do what their name suggest ;)

gist: I like the variety of workouts and the workouts themselves, but wish Apple could work
title: Too many issues
text: I like the variety of workouts and the workouts themselves, but wish Apple could work out the following issues: - It would be great if you could pause and then resume a workout after being interrupted. I’ve tried several times to resume a workout after pausing; each time that I’ve tried doing so, the audio works but there is no video.  -Along those same lines, there should be a way to rewind or fast forward a workout. From what I can tell, there is not. - Workouts are listed by most recent. There should also be a way to filter the workouts from oldest to newest, so that you don’t have to scroll for an eternity if, for example, you’d like to follow the workouts in sequence. - I have tried to login to my fitness+ account from my Apple TV, but am blocked from doing so because I don’t have an Apple Watch. So i can only access my fitness+ account from my iPhone. This is counterintuitive. - I have also tried starting the workout on my iPhone and then “sending” it to my Apple TV, which worked initially, but after several minutes of working out the connection was lost and I had to start the workout over from the beginning. Very frustrating.

gist: The iPad app used without an apple watch does not record your workouts or count
title: App is a letdown to good workouts
text: The iPad app used without an apple watch does not record your workouts or count the activity toward closing your rings like the iPhone app does (I am assuming this is because they have walled off the health app from the iPad). The library is buried at the bottom and is featureless, so storing and tracking favorite workouts is unnecessarily difficult. There are no fast forward or rewind controls, so if you miss an instruction, get interrupted by the kids, or the app glitches, there is no way to get back to where you were in your workout. It seems like apple wants the app to feel like an actual workout class, where you do whatever workout is scheduled for the day and once you start you go until the end, but their stubbornness with philosophy and feel kills usability. Especially fast forward and rewind is such a basic feature that the only explanation is they are intentionally leaving it out. I have really enjoyed the workouts, but will cancel my subscription after the trial because of the app.

text: I’ll start out by saying my expectations were pretty high coming from experience using other top fitness subscription apps, figured given Apple’s brand it’d be up to par. That being said, you don’t hear a single moment of any actual music in the workouts - the instructors are trying extremely hard to work in “funny” anecdotes and obvious cookie-cutter language that doesn’t inspire anyone to do much hard work. The workouts are rather basic and few and far between in regards to them building diverse library. If you’re in a pinch and don’t want to spend money on the more well known fitness apps, it’s worth the free 3 month trial. Otherwise, pay a few bucks more for the real deal.

title: Inadequate if pretty
text: I’m still on the free version. I will not pay for it - any number of other workout programs do better if you’re travelling, not a gym member, or can’t afford equipment.  Four things would greatly improve this app: 1. MORE BODYWEIGHT - you shouldn’t have to own gym equipment or pay for a gym membership to use this app. This is too expensive to be making you pay for extra things in order to use it fully. 2. An option to turn off the music. Many apps have this. You should too. 3. Better integration with other fitness app. If Apple sells the workouts, it should integrate with this in-system app. 4. The subtitles make it hard to see floor exercises. Generally, you need more attention to the technique details - foot placement, angle of bend, profile shots etc, but the fact that your own subtitles hide the positions the trainer is in is particularly poor design.

text: I really enjoy using the Fitness plus subscription. I like how my watch readings shows up on the screen during my workout. I like how I can monitor my heart rate and calories burned on my iPad while I’m working out. Only downfall is occasionally it’ll stop reading my heart rate at times while I’m in the middle of a workout it’ll only show calories burned and time. Which is a bummer. *There are a few things I wish they would update in the app though for example I wish they had a filter for the part of the body you will be working out Ex: abs, glutes and focal point such as that. This way I don’t have to click on each work out and read the description and see what part of the body will be targeted.  *Another idea is if the title of the work out mentioned the targeted area of the body example: HIIT - Trainers name - ABS   I also wish it offered Barre Fitness as well. I have to switch apps and use my beachbody subscription to get those workouts in. I would rather it be an all in one and only use fitness plus for my workouts but not the current case. I also wish there was a filter for beginner and intermediate. I know each workout shows moderation for different levels but some are still really challenging for someone just starting out.

I absolutely hate country music and it would give me the flexibility to still listen to those workouts without being subjected to musical torture for 20 mins.

gist: This does not hold a candle to Garmin connect.
title: No where near what it should be
text: This does not hold a candle to Garmin connect.  There is no way to edit data of a completed workout.  Example, you do an indoor track run so you select outdoor run because the indoor run assumes treadmill. (And it’s suggested in the apple forums to select outdoor run for indoor track runs) The gps data is all jacked up and gives inaccurate distance. Now your vo2max is all screwed up.  You’d think you’d be able to just go into the workout and change the distance.  Nope. Can’t do it. You can only delete it.   There is no suggested recovery.  There is no workload.  You can’t create your own workout like a run and lift. You have to add a new workout. What I mean is, there isn’t a way to set up a single workout that has two different types of workouts in it.  Like I run, pause, then lift weights.  You have to select run, then add a new workout and select lifting.    The starting and stopping or pausing of workouts isn’t the best.  If you select any run, you better be prepared to run in the next 3 seconds. You can’t just hit a side button and start the run run that way.   On my ultra, hitting the action button only starts the last type of workout. So if I hit that, I better be doing whatever the last workout is.  Which I won’t be because I run then lift, again, two different types of workout.  I wanted to like this watch and fitness app. But it just isn’t anywhere near what Garmin does.

title: Fitness App Disappeared from iPad Pro
text: Have Apple One Premier subscription.  Updated iPad Pro to iPadOS 16.3.  Apple Fitness+ App disappeared from Home Screen, and not present in App Library. However, searching the App Store I can still locate the Fitness app, but can’t download it only open it. Workaround one: view and use Fitness videos one my iPhone.  Workaround two: search App Store (doesn’t appear in App Library at all) for Apple Fitness, open the app.  Workaround three: completely turn off screen time (not ideal for families with children). Fitness app comes back. Note, screen time settings were not changed before the update, and the Fitness app is and has always been allowed in ‘Allowed Apps’. It seems that there is a bug in the latest update which is linked to Apple Fitness and Screen Time on iPad. iPhone is unaffected.   Workaround four: downgrade subscription, don’t use Apple Fitness. Two stars because there has been so many past problems accessing the app, and I have spend many hours trouble shooting this issue for myself, family and friends. I expect more reliable service when paying such an expensive subscription price coupled with an expensive device.  Note: content within the app is good. Delivery of consistent and reliable service for this app is very poor. Fitness is highlighted as a key component of Apple One Premier. Thus the lack of availability and reliability of the Fitness app tarnishes the appeal, value and experience of Apple One and and the service of Apple overall.    When it comes to fitness activities and meditation people want to ‘just do it’. We don’t want to suddenly and unexpectedly be trouble shooting a missing app and trying to understand why. The why is the responsibility of Apple and its engineers. Apple customers pay very good money for very good products, and the expectation of a very good experience.

title: Absolut begeistert
text: Vorweg: Viele der negativen Bewertungen beziehen sich auf die Anfangszeiten von Fitness+, doch es hat sich seitdem vieles verändert wie wir festgestellt haben.  Meine Frau und ich sind eigentlich keine begeisterten Sportler, weder in Vereinen aktiv noch stemmen wir gerne Eisen wie manche Brüllaffen im Studio. Aber wir gaben dem Kursansatz von Fitness + eine Chance, haben uns einige Kurse rausgesucht und einfach angefangen. Es hat uns von Anfang an riesigen Spaß bereitet und erstaunt wie anspruchsvoll diese Kurse sind. Doch dranbleiben lohnt sich, mittlerweile freuen wir uns gemeinsam auf jeden Kurstag den wir uns eingetragen haben. Wir haben viele Kurse für uns entdeckt und nutzen sehr viele Angebote. Das hat sich auch auf der Waage und vor dem Spiegel nach ein paar Monaten gezeigt. Die Pfunde fallen, das Wohlbefinden steigt und dazu haben wir auch wieder mehr Zeit als Paar, da wir nun Kurspartner sind und uns gemeinsam mit unseren Trainern auspowern, das schweißt zusammen! Es wird wenig Equipment benötigt, es ist mit 80€/Jahr zudem sehr fair und das beste daran sind die motivierenden Trainer, die jede Woche neue Kurse bereitstellen. Das Angebot wächst damit stetig. Langsam beginnt Fitness+ auch mit aufbauenden Programmen, bspw. 4 Wochen Programm für HIIT Kurse. Probiert es aus!

gist: Update on the app - one year later and I renewing my annual subscription as
title: Game changer - love this app
text: Update on the app - one year later and I renewing my annual subscription as I am still using and loving this app - I can level up or down and focus on different parts of my body depending on what I’m training for. Right now, it’s core and toning as I prepare my bikini beach body for Hawaii. Brilliant!  That said, I’ve downgraded to 4 stars as there are a few tips the team might consider: - being Australian, it would be useful to include metric weights and measurements (every time, not just sometimes)  - please add the focus of the set in the title (eg not just ‘mindful cool-down with Greg’ but ‘upper body cool-down’ or ‘whole body cool-down’ etc so you don’t have to waste time clicking and opening til you find something suitable - useful for all mat, hiit and strength workouts  - add a ‘routine’ page so you can save a weekly routine of your choice of classes so you don’t have to search each time you return to workout. Right now, I’m working on a bunch of classes on alternate days and it’s annoying to have to scroll to find them every time I come back to exercise.  Simple and effective changes will improve the user experience.  Thanks team - you have helped me get fit again, I am truly grateful!  ,, 2022 As someone who had been fit and active but had prolonged inactivity forced upon me after an injury, this app has been perfect for motivating me to get active again. Closing the move, exercise and activity rings every day has been a game changer. My fitness level has been all but restored within three months - I have lost the extra weight I gained, I can literally see my muscle rebuilding where it had wasted away, my heart health has improved, my step count tripled and I have so much more energy each day. I trialled the free version when I purchased my Apple Watch - I thought, why not, 3 months free, what was there to lose? I’d just started going to a personal trainer after recovering from an injury and a series of surgeries, but he was about to have a holiday so I was left to my own devices. The app gave me the convenience of guided exercise whenever I wanted, rather than having to get in the car to go to the gym and motivate myself. It has so many exercise options and new sets to choose from with different trainers each week. Yes, looking at other reviews, there are definitely things I’d improve (eg intuitive starts and pauses to walking/running, more sensitivity to stand function which sometimes fails to register). Please, app designers, please work these frustrations out - surely it can be done. Despite its shortfalls, I’m giving it a 5 star review because it has been the single most effective app I have ever used - it pulled me out of a two-year funk and has supported me to be restored to a fitness level I never thought I’d enjoy again. It’s not a silver bullet, but it is good for people who are determined to put disciplines into their life, and willing to make the changes in lifestyle. I put my tv away, put reminders in my calendar to kickstart my new routines and make this work. I’m SO glad I did, I feel ten years younger.

gist: Update: Apple has addressed many of the issues in my original review.
title: Mostly great, needs some updates and fixes
text: Update: Apple has addressed many of the issues in my original review. Thank you! My new suggestions are: let us schedule rest days or input sick days on our watch. Sometimes I get discouraged by breaking a streak even when doing so is needed or beyond my body’s control. Rest days let me manage my time without getting fixated; and they’re necessary when sick. Being able to schedule rest days so I took them before I got injured or burnt out would make it easier to stay on track and avoid feeling discouraged about progress. I’ve got a packed, demanding life. I’ve got school age kids who make our home a revolving door of viruses. I’m in my 40’s and more prone to injury than I was in my 20’s. I feel like the metrics could make room for all of that.  The trainer team is phenomenal. 5 stars to the trainers and whoever was in charge of casting them. The workouts and variety of workouts are also great. Items I would like to see addressed and updated: 1) [had been fixed] 2) [has been fixed. Thank you!]. 3) [addressed but not per my suggestions for audio. Still sounds better overall]. 4) where I am connected to friends on my fitness/watch; I find a lot of the automatic responses pretty rude and sarcastic. I’m all in favor of less smack talk and more positive affirmation/encouragement. I would be mortified if I accidentally sent one of my tender hearted friends one of those mean responses.

gist: app terrible versus Pacer and Wahoo for tracking
title: Watch is nice, app is terrible
text: I bought a watch Series 8 primarily for the health features, particularly the fitness monitoring. I have been using the Pacer app for five years, and a Keiser Indoor bike with the Wahoo Systm app with a Polar heart rate monitor for three years. I’m very fit and track my caloric intake and expenditure daily. While the heart rate monitoring of the watch is very accurate, the calories burned calculated by the app and watch are off by 75% - too high. I’ve tried recalibrating the watch according to Apple’s guidelines to no avail. I’m sure there are better ways to monitor your exercise but this app and the Apple Watch aren’t the way to go. Disappointing. On a ski day with 16 runs, 4:45 hours on the mountain the watch said I burned 933 calories, which is ridiculous. I’ve never burned 933 calories in one day doing anything. It counted my entire time on the mountain as if I was skiing whether I was on the lift, eating lunch, or using the bathroom. Completely ridiculous!

I could care less about counting them. Personally, I wish I could turn the option off. gist: Indoor walk and run activities - treadmill users should have the ability to add elevation
title: Enhancements needed
text: Overall the Fitness app functions well and effectively monitors activities. Some enhancements that would make this a 4-5 star app in my opinion:  1. Indoor walk and run activities - treadmill users should have the ability to add elevation and mileage to the work outs as this would more accurately reflect the distance and intensity of the workout. (Other apps allow you to do this but we should not need other apps).   2. Cycling (indoor or outdoor) - app should convert strides or measured rpms to steps for the purposes of accurately capturing steps for the day. On days I ride rather than walk / run the app tells me I am taking less steps because it doesn’t factor in cycling. gist: However, one major drawback is the lack of detailed exercise technique guidance.
title: Great Coaches, Music, and Vibe, But Technique is Missing
text: The Fitness+ app by Apple offers a fantastic workout experience with motivating coaches and energizing music. The app provides a wide range of workouts, catering to different fitness levels and preferences. However, one major drawback is the lack of detailed exercise technique guidance. This becomes particularly noticeable during fast-paced HIIT workouts, where new movements are introduced quickly. Currently, exercises are only shown from a frontal view, without close-ups or slow-motion demonstrations. This absence of technique guidance hinders users' ability to perform exercises correctly and increases the risk of injury. To address this issue, the app should include separate short videos that focus on the techniques of the exercises, allowing users to familiarize themselves with proper form before starting the workout

gist: The AirPlay on the TV works well apart from the occasional glitch.

text: I love some things about this service: The trainers are enthusiastic and encouraging and (in my view any way) quite diverse. The sessions are fun and engaging. The specific feature I have found most irritating to date is that I can’t use my wife’s iPad to play rowing sessions. More generally for a service that obtains a huge amount of data there is a weirdly ‘one size fits all’ approach to delivering the service. I would like to do a heavy weights session one day and recover the next. Do a hard run and be expected to take it easy for a few days. In my late 40s I would expect to be given more recovery time than I needed in my 20s. I would like a series of sessions - particularly on the rowing - which look at improving my VO2 max. The stuff above seems tantalisingly possible. One final thing - it may never rain in Southern California but for those of US who run in drizzle quite a lot a watch with a touch screen isn’t great. Some clarity on how to customise the buttons would be helpful.

text: I used Fiton in the past but my husband encouraged me to try Fitness+ since I now have a watch that supports it. I love the integration between my Apple TV and watch! I also love that you can see the music tracks from any workout in case you like a song and want to add it to your library. Great feature! What could use some work, in my opinion, is the filtering and menus. I absolutely hate scrolling down to the bottom to get to my saved workouts. I also hate not being able to have menus instead of through the whole page to find something. This is for both the mobile and Apple TV versions. And I was so used to being able to filter workouts based on fitness level that now it seems so clunky and cumbersome to have to watch a preview to see what I might encounter and try to gauge the level from there. When you have 30 minutes in the morning, the last thing you want to do is scroll though a bunch of workouts you’d never consider just to get to something that seems doable. I love yoga workouts so maybe there could be a way to quickly access yoga workout and then filter by level and time from there. Because let’s be real, even with modifications, not every yoga workout can be for beginners. And beginner ones aren’t ideal for expert level. This seems like such a no brainer, to have better filters, I’m honestly surprised Apple let it go out and stay like this.

title: I don’t get the hate, this app is great!
text: First of all, I’m not a bot and I wasn’t paid to write this. I used the app for the first time today and did a 30 minute run. Running has always been hard for me because I find it difficult to get out of my head and it seems like it just drags on and on. I’m lucky if I make it a mile and a half when I, first getting back into it, and at my best I only ever made it up to 4 miles.  Today, however, I did the 30 minute run with Scott and I was really surprised. They way they “gamify” the run if you have an Apple Watch where you can see you heart rate, distance, cadence, and activity ring was cool, but the “Burn Bar” was the coolest feature. This is Apples definition of what it is:  “ The Burn Bar is a way for you to compare your effort to others who've done the same workout. It adjusts to account for weight to allow for an equal comparison and is shown as your calories burned. If you leave it on, your workout data is anonymously added to the Burn Bar competition. The Burn Bar is available for High Intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill, Cycling, and Rowing workouts.” I’m a little competitive by nature, so having this really pushed me to work harder, and the combination of the interesting commentary from Scott and everything I mentioned above contributed to me running 2.4 miles on day one (and I am out of shape). I’d encourage you to give this a try, especially if you have an Apple Watch.

title: Some advanced notice????
text: I have used this app for a few years now and have recommended it to many people because of the varied workout types and a vast selection. I would give this a five star rating if not for one thing… vanishing workouts.  I had workouts that I added to my library (which, I would have thought would act like a storage space rather than a directory). Some of these I did regularly and others I liked and would return to on occasion. Recently, I discovered that some of my library workouts - including one that my chiropractor suggested I use as a good preventative maintenance for an earlier sustained injury - had vanished. Checking the workout sections showed that they were no longer listed anywhere. Cleaning up cloud storage space? I understand that server maintenance will occasionally require that files be deleted but it would be nice if users could be notified that certain workouts are scheduled for removal. Perhaps even given the option to purchase, for a one-time fee, and download those files for local use as long as they maintain their subscription (maybe just 25 or 50 cents per selected file since we’re already paying for the subscription).  The code for this isn’t that complex and it would give users the opportunity to decide how much they really want a particular workout that is likely to be removed because the overall community isn’t using it as frequently as your analytics would like. Just a thought.

gist: So choice is brilliant if you only have a certain amount if time for example.
title: Good but could be so much better.
text: Currently in the trial phase and really love the quality of the videos and interaction from the trainers.  There are many videos for each workout type which is great.  So choice is brilliant if you only have a certain amount if time for example.   I am used to Insanity HIIT workouts and these are really good.  The  treadmill running are good too - would like too many more that don’t have inclines as not many people will have these types of machines.  Perhaps someone could say if you don’t have an incline increase speed by X for example.  Where is think it needs improving is the warmup & down and stretching after a workout. Which is THE MOST IMPORTANT PART of a workout. These should be incorporated within the workout as part of the workout.  I am struggling to find a PROPER cool down and stretching session for my HIIT workouts. There is lots of leg action in the HIIT but barely any form of strecthing the hamstring, groin and thigh area.  So I have do to my own.  If you want inspiration watch a few of the Insanity workouts.  Would love to see  more attention to this part  - or do a dedicated  Cool-down and stretch session which people can go to do as part of any exercise.  We could all do with the bit of extra stretching from time to time.  I really like the way the instructors pass out the instructions.  What I would really like is to have the option to turn off the music though. I like to listen to certain music when exercising. Again something I think shouldn’t be that hard.   Appreciate that this is relatively new and a work in progress.  Look forward to seeing more developments and enhancements.

gist: This is a great app, especially the watch integration… but Fitness+ workouts are very limited
title: Love this App, but Not Enough for Seniors
text: This is a great app, especially the watch integration… but Fitness+ workouts are very limited for seniors & others with mobility limitations. Although they include modifications in most of the workouts, far too many involve getting on and off the floor. They have one set of very nice “Workouts for Older Adults” but after 2 years they’re getting old. And even one of those requires getting on the floor so I mostly skip it. While many of us can do it if necessary, it can take us long enough that we’ve missed a lot of the workout in the process. At a minimum, if they don’t want to make more senior-specific workouts, AT LEAST enable us to search for workouts that don’t involve being on the floor. Nothing more frustrating that starting a workout that looks promising only to find out they’ve buried some floor exercises in the middle. Half the old ladies in my water aerobics classes wear Apple Watches, but I won’t recommend Fitness+ until there is a better library of workouts for us as virtually all of us feel the same way about getting on the floor.  Hope someone actually pays attention to these reviews & works on this!

text: Seitdem ich eine Apple Watch zusammen mit dem iPhone benutze, werden die Daten automatisch erfasst und ich bin über meinen Bewegung von Trainingszustand gut informiert. Das ist nicht schaffbar und unmotivierend. Ein weiterer Verbesserungsvorschlag: wenn man es an einem Tag nicht geschafft hat, seine Ringe komplett zuschließen, wäre ein Folgetag, bei dem man deutlich mehr Stunden steht/Kalorien verbraucht oder trainiert hat als möglicher Ausgleichstag motivierend. gist: What I do struggle with is a lack of basic features between the app and
title: Really Lacking Features
text: It’s a good set it and forget it app. I’m not interested in Fitness+ because it seems to be focused on workout videos, and I have no issues planning my own workouts. What I do struggle with is a lack of basic features between the app and the watch. First, you only have the ability to customize the workouts on your watch. Look I’m getting older and my eyes don’t want to stare at the tiny screen and try to adjust the intervals, time for each rep, goals, etc., Also, the only notification that the work intervals has ended and recovery interval has started is the watch vibrates. It’s a very subtle vibrate so if you’re running and the watch isn’t super tight, it’s easy to miss. Especially if you’re wearing layers. There should be options for a sound to go with it (the alert option is only to notify you of target metrics.) if you want to charge for more customization go for it but I prefer the Under Armor Map My Run app for my running training because it’s a lot more flexible, and is a reasonable rate for what you get. Last thing, I’d love to know the algorithm for these monthly challenges. October told me how I was doing so well with open water swim and to get three this month.  1. I have never done an open water swim as I only do laps in a pool, and 2. I live in Michigan. Now maybe some brave souls may hit the lake in October but not me. Not sure what the app is looking to motivate me to do here but it might want to take into account location when making certain recommendations or challenge goals.

gist: I do lots of different kinds of exercise and am very self motivated, so I
title: “Stand” and “Flights Climbed” Inaccurate/Makes Me Neurotic
text: I’ve been using this app via my Apple Watch since probably 2015 (it’s now 2023).  I do lots of different kinds of exercise and am very self motivated, so I didn’t NEED to use this app, but I like comparing data, so I was interested in seeing what it said about my various fitness indicators.  Overall, there are a lot of helpful components to this app.  Unfortunately, there are enough inaccuracies and non-customizable features that it is sometimes infuriating.  The “stand” ring is one of those.  I can’t tell you how many times I have stood for 50 minutes straight only to have it tell me that”it’s time to stand!”  If the watch is unable to accurately perceive standing, or if Apple is actually trying to encourage lower body movement (not just standing), then, please, rename the rings Movement (instead of Standing), Exercise, and Calories (instead of Movement).  The Flights Climbed feature also doesn’t work.  I could walk up and down the steps in my house for thirty minutes straight and have not a single flight of steps be logged.  I also take issue with the watch setting goals for me (I’m thinking of the monthly goals here).  Yes, I aim to be fit, but sometimes I have other priorities than burning a certain number of movement calories in a month.  And what if I’m on a plan all day?  Perhaps standing every hour is not one of my goals that day.  Let me be in charge of my goals.  On the other hand, sometimes I spend all day hiking… and my watch runs out of battery life during the hike.  So my calories and exercise can’t even be recorded.  I don’t like having these inaccuracies recorded as fact.    And I don’t like how this watch is encouraging me to be neurotic about something that “matters,” but that I shouldn’t be obsessive about.  I shouldn’t feel like I need to shake my arm up and down at the end of the day to push the Movement ring across the finish line and appease an APP.  In the end, this “health” app is negatively affecting my mental health.

Please address this algorithm issue. Otherwise it defeats the purpose of having you “automatically” set up work plans for the users. gist: I’m a slow jogger and after the update to watchOS 10.1, I noticed that Stride
title: Stride length not recording
text: I’m a slow jogger and after the update to watchOS 10.1, I noticed that Stride Length no longer shows up on my metrics.  Even after receiving help from the Apple Engineers, the problem wasn’t solved.  Thereafter, I did several experiments on my Apple Watch Ultra and my wife’s Apple Watch Series 7. I think I found the issue. There seemed to be a lower limit now for stride length before it shows up, and I believe the limit is 0.6m. When we do slow jogging at conversational pace, stride length went to 0.4-0.5m and will not show up on the Apple Watches. Once we pick up the pace, above 0.6m and the stride length metric works normally.  Prior to watchOS 10.1, the Apple Watches will measure stride length down to 0.4m, maybe even lower. I don’t understand the reason to implement the lower limit and exclude the slow joggers from a useful metric like stride length.  Can the engineers remove the lower limit of stride length so all runners of varying age, fitness and training objective can benefit from it? Thank you.

When you get there, the trainers are not in alphabetical order. So for example I love Greg for Strength and Spin and yet hes on the bottom half of the list. Why? When you select a trainer its easy to sort by workout type, length and even music which is great.  Whats NOT great is if you save or download your workouts they appear at the VERY BOTTOM of the main page in My Library. Why make people scroll to workouts they already chose and want?  When you get to the saved and downloaded workouts you cant filter either. So if I wanted 20mn workouts or Greg only or Rock only NOPE! You have to scroll through the list to find what you want. Again...why make people scroll so much when the app obviously has the ability to sort? Can you guys PLEASE make a menu on the first page so I have the option to get to the Trainers or Library (Saved and Downloaded workout)s? Also cut back the amount of rows of stuff you are pushing. A row or two, cool but 8 or so rows seems a insanely excessive especially when this app doesn't seem to be learning that I obviously would not choose, lets say Rowing, because I don't have a rower not row boat etc!  Also maybe allow people to set a row of stuff to keep an eye on. Like alert me for new Greg workouts.

gist: Because the app does not offer exercises for differing levels of ability, THE CUSTOMIZED EXERCISE
title: DIFFERENT FITNESS LEVELS NEEDED
text: Because the app does not offer exercises for differing levels of ability, THE CUSTOMIZED EXERCISE PLANS ARE GARBAGE. They promote quitting and deleting the app.  The app is truly only useful for people in peak physical shape. Those of us with different fitness abilities are merely an afterthought. This is entirely obvious from the way the so-called modifications receive the briefest of mentions. All of this makes their claims of wanting to promote physical fitness and healthy habits incredibly insulting.  Instead of treating people with differing levels of fitness as pitiable pariahs, each of the routines should be offered at different experience/ability levels. That would allow for more customization and more engagement. It would also allow for more meaningful tracking of progress.  For example, I can make it through most of the Core and Yoga routines with no problem. At times I struggle with the Kickboxing routines. And the HIIT, Pilates, and Dance routines are so frustratingly advanced that I rarely make it through an entire exercise. If I could access routines based on my ability and experience for each category, I would actually find the app useful and engaging instead of it making me feel like trash as I struggle through exercises the trainers are doing so breezily.  With all of the resources at your disposal, Apple, I know you can do better than this.
