gist: It’s cringy LA fakeness at it’s worst.
title: Fitness + is Blues Clues for 20-something’s
text: I actively despise Apple Fitness+. It’s cringy LA fakeness at it’s worst. While people blame Peloton for seeming cult-y, nothing can prepare you for this fake energy of the patronizing drivel that’s spoken during each class. It’s as if every instructor (primary + joining friends) has an off-screen boss, forcing artificial smiles and awkward laughs, giggles and reactions at weird moments when nothing funny was said. My class tried really hard to correlate every single moment in the workout to watching a season of your favorite show… it was miserable and repetitive filler-commentary, and all of the music sounded the exact same. The set looks like a fake-brick scene, straight from the musical ‘Rent.’  It’s hard to believe that any one of the instructors has any real experience instructing. How have they not improved things in over a year of producing this content? - so, in short, if you want to watch something with the writing of Blue’s Clues, aimed squarely at super young, insecure 20-something’s that never developed their brains past the 3rd grade, good luck and have at it. As for me, I’m running for the hills!

text: I’ve been using this app with the intention of sharing and comparing my data with friends and family, which seemed like a promising feature initially. However, the experience has been less than satisfactory due to a persistent issue where the data does not always display correctly for shared profiles. Despite both parties being able to see my data without any problems, there are times when their data appears as zero to me, which is clearly inaccurate. I’ve taken the time to meticulously check all the relevant settings on both my end and the end of my friends and family to ensure that everything is configured correctly for sharing. Despite these efforts, the issue persists, leading me to believe that this is an inherent problem with the app itself rather than a misconfiguration on our part. gist: Most fitness app I’ve looked in to are too in-your-face and aimed at people who
title: Great for getting a sweat worked up daily in a fun way
text: I had very low expectations for this app. Most fitness app I’ve looked in to are too in-your-face and aimed at people who want to get buff or whatever. I just wanted something with a more relaxed feel, toned down decor, and fun routines that got me in shape. I have been loving this app for that purpose.  I’m really impressed with the instructors, and I especially love their diversity in gender, age, body type, etc. One is even currently pregnant, and it’s great to see how she works the modified routines. That, the fact that they use some sign language, and the way one instructor is usually demonstrating a low-impact modified version of the workout makes the classes feel welcoming and accessible no matter how I’m feeling. I think the instructors do a great job at explaining things and being encouraging, sometimes making it clear there’s no “right” way to do it, like the idea is to be moving and enjoying yourself. No one needs to see the mess I make of the dance moves, but I’ve really enjoyed trying them! The routines have you moving in about the space of a yoga mat, so it works well if you only have a small space in your house to use for workouts.  I don’t use any of the app’s gamified stuff or awards, so if that’s motivating to you, I’m not sure how this app measures up. For fun at-home routines that work lots of muscles and work up a sweat in 10-20 minutes, I’ve found it to be perfect. Shout out especially to the diverse and kind instructors,if they rotate in more older instructors and more variety in body types, I’d love it even more.

gist: I do get frustrated when I do a workout, I can see it on my

text: I have completed 100+ trainer led workouts in the last 7 weeks. I have enjoyed the variety of trainers, workouts, and music. I do get frustrated when I do a workout, I can see it on my summary for the day, but it does not “check” off of my plan. I have had this happen 4 times in the last 6 weeks and it is discouraging when I’m on track, but have to redo a workout just to get the completion credit. Competing with other friends has been great. I switched from 8 years with Fitbit Premium to Apple Fitness+ with an Apple Watch primarily because FP got rid of challenges. I would love if I could have 2-3 friends competing with you at a time, but the 1:1 is better than nothing. Sometimes the awards are not totally accurate with the activity that it should be awarding for. There have been times that I have exceeded a previous goal, but the award gets “stuck” at a previous metric. I have used my Apple TV, iPad, and iPhone to exercise and all have maintained a considerably seamless. Overall my Apple Fitness+ experience has exceeded my expectations and previous experience with Fitbit.

Ich brauch nicht unbedingt eine automatische Erkennung, was denke ich bestimmt machbar wäre, aber einfach eine Möglichkeit Liegestützen hinzuzufügen. Oder auch Sit-Ups oder Squads. So eine Übersicht wäre hilfreich - es gibt zwar viele Apps dafür - aber wenn alles in Fitness gehen würde wäre das doch schon sehr angenehm. Wäre toll wenn sowas noch integriert werden würde. title: Shockingly bad at calibrating distance.
text: So I’ve been using this app to track my distance and calories burned for over a year now, but it wasn’t until I started training for a half marathon that I noticed that the distance the app says I’ve run was all over the place. There would be times I went ran the exact same distance two days apart but the app would say that one day I had ran an extra half a mile.   I knew it was inaccurate but I didn’t realise by how much until I ran the half marathon today. According to this fitness app, rather than running the standard 13.1 miles, the organisers must have been way off because according to my phone I’ve run over 18 miles today on the half marathon course. Shockingly bad!  Overall I would rate this fitness app as terribly poor and inaccurate, but I suppose you can at least use it to compare the distances and calories that it says you’re burning from one day to the next. I’ll still use it for this purpose, just to keep track of which days I’ve worked harder than others, but as far as keeping an accurate record of these details I wouldn’t trust the app on this phone as far as I could throw it (and the phone would still claim I’d not thrown it as far as I actually had, just to provide another blow to my ego).

title: Tolle App und ein paar zusätzliche Ideen
text: Grundsätzlich tut die App, was sie soll, aber wenn möglich würde ich mir noch ein paar Features wünschen, wie zum Beispiel die Nutzung der App auch am MacBook, weil man da ja doch einen etwas größeren Bildschirm hat, als am Handy und nicht jeder hat die Möglichkeit ein AppleTV Gerät mit in den Urlaub zu nehmen und irgendwo anzuschließen, das MacBook hingegen ist leicht eingepackt. Zusätzlich wäre es schön, wenn man sich die Videos auch ansehen könnte, ohne trainieren zu müssen, weil es bei manchen Übungen eben praktisch ist, wenn man sie sich vorab ansehen und die korrekten Bewegungsabläufe einprägen kann. Auch eine bessere Sortiermöglichkeit der Trainings wäre toll, wie zum Beispiel bei Yoga nicht nur nach Dauer und Trainer, sondern auch danach, ob ein Training nur im Stehen, Sitzen, auf Knien, … durchgeführt wird. Ich versuche nämlich aktuell auf Yogapositionen zu verzichten, die auf Knien sind, weil ich aktuell leichte Probleme mit den Knien habe und wenn ich das erst mitten im Training feststelle, dann kann ich das Training leider nicht vollständig absolvieren. Zusätzlich wäre es schön, wenn man sich auch die passenden Workouts leichter zusammensuchen und markieren kann, beziehungsweise selbst Trainingspläne mit vorhandenen Workouts zusammenstellen kann. Zur Sprache, da habe ich mit meinem Englisch kein Problem, aber dass die App für alle anderen Sprachen als englisch nur auf der Text-Spur und nicht auch auf der Audiospur verfügbar sind finde ich schade. Der Aufwand die Videos in der Sprache des Users auch noch nach zu vertonen sollte sich in Grenzen halten, weil eine Übersetzung des Textes ja bereits vorhanden ist. Wenn der User dann die Auswahl zwischen Originalton (mit Untertitel) oder Muttersprache hätte wäre das deutlich besser! Immerhin zahlt man ja auch Geld für das Abo.

gist: Did you miss part of the instructions from the trainer?
title: Total fail
text: Did you miss part of the instructions from the trainer? Too bad rewind is not an option. Are they doing an exercise you can’t do? Can’t skip ahead, no fast-forward allowed. Looking for a specific workout in your saved workouts? With no folders or filters to help store and search your saved workouts you just gotta dig through until you find it. The entire Apple Fitness platform is a failure for forcing its rigid interface onto users rather than allowing us to have control over our fitness experience. If it’s not a live class I should be able to rewind and fast forward and change the audio to whatever I want. Would you rather listen to a podcast or audiobook rather than the cringe inducing drivel being spouted by the spin instructors? Well, you can’t. It’s the cheesiest, dumbest monologue you’ll ever have the displeasure of sweating to. The best you can do is mute it and pair your AirPods to a different device which is the only thing that keeps me from flinging my iPad across the room every time the spin instructor compares the class to a music festival or some such nonsense. It would also be extremely helpful, especially for the hearing impaired, to have clear instructions displayed on the screen - not subtitles of what the instructor is saying (90% of which is garbage) but simple prompts to increase intensity or stand up, etc. Yes you can watch what the instructor is doing but sometimes it’s hard to tell especially when you have the audio turned off. This probably wouldn’t be an option for other apple fitness workouts but when doing something repetitive like spin it makes total sense. Do better Apple.

title: Great app, but needs improvement
text: What I love: -1. The way it automatically syncs to your watch. No more forgetting to start or end a workout on your watch - the app does it for you. 2. What needs to improved: 1. I would love to see Kettlebell workouts. Kettlebells have become increasingly popular, and I am shocked that Fitness+ hasn’t included them yet. 2. For the plans, I wish I could delete & add some of my favorite workouts. For instance, I made a plan, but I really want to include the strength workout featuring Daft Punk. I can’t find a way to delete one 20 minute workout and add in another one of my choice. 3. I think the whole Health & Fitness apps really need some updating. You should be able to edit your workout, like the start and end times for when you forget, or the distance of a run when you are on a treadmill or do a measured track but the watch records it incorrectly. 4. I wish you could fast forward and rewind in the workout. I know that might make things difficult since it syncs to your Apple Watch, but it’s annoying when you have two workouts in a day, but both workouts spend 3 minutes doing a warmup. I don’t always need to warmup for my second workout but there’s no way to skip it.5. Sometimes the app refuses to connect to my Apple Watch - I think that’s probably the glitch I’ve encountered the most often.

text: I love that there is not where that shows in app purchases but if I look up other apps it will say there are in app purchases. Für sehr aktive Menschen, zum Teil frustrierend und ich finde es gefährlich, da Menschen die sich nicht viel mit Gesundheit, gesunden Verhalten und Co auseinandersetzen, definitiv in ungesunde Verhaltensmuster erzogen wird.  Gerade bei Frauen ist Übertraining sehr schädlich!  An sich ne gute Sache und ich mag die App auch, aber ich würd mir wünschen, dass realistische gesundheitsfördernde Maßnahmen implementiert wird und man nicht wieder dazu erzogen wird „Man muss viel machen, dann bist du viel wert und schaffst alles“

gist: I’ve been using Apple Fitness workouts consistently since the beginning of the pandemic and find
title: Love Apple Fitness,please add a trans trainer!
text: I’ve been using Apple Fitness workouts consistently since the beginning of the pandemic and find it to be better than anything  else available on the market and for a fraction of the price. When I travel for work and have other equipment available, there’s a workout to correspond (rowing, stationary bike, etc). But I can always sneak in a 30 min strength workout no matter I am or what equipment is available. Would love to see a 45 min strength option in the upper/lower/total body sections. Beyond the practical review is the quality and diversity of trainers,I love that Jenn has been added to the strength crew, increasing the number of women of color trainers. I really appreciate the celebration and inclusion of a variety of cultures and identities throughout the months and years,it’s part of why I have stuck with the app this long. My hope is that Apple is ready to add a trainer who is openly transgender. As an LGBT athlete, I’ve appreciated how many openly gay trainers there are on the Fitness Plus Team but it’s been almost four years now without a trans trainer and I’m scratching my head about this, given how many trans trainers there are in the U.S. and abroad.  Keep up the great work and thanks for putting out such a great product for those of us committed to an inclusive and diverse idea of fitness.

title: Not knowing the moves in a workout is literally causing me pain
text: I have a chronic connective tissue disorder (Ehlers Danlos Syndrome) and shoulder/elbow/knee injuries. I pick a workout because it says it’s low impact or something similar because that’s pretty much all I can do right now. But because so many of the workouts don’t give you a list of moves you will be doing I end up picking ones that have stuff I can’t do (pushups, planks, squats, lunges, excessive jumping, etc) then I’ll get into a 30 minute workout and can’t do half of it because I didn’t know that I couldn’t do it. If you would LIST the moves we’ll be doing in the description (which is literally what it’s for!) then that would weed out so many of my issues! The trainers already make a list of moves for the workout, why can’t you guys just put them in the description? It would make it SO much easier on people with injuries or other chronic illnesses like mine.

title: Zu teuer für das was es ist
text: Vorweg: ich habe keine Apple Watch und habe die App nur mit dem Handy benutzt. Ich weiß nicht ob manche der Dinge nicht zutreffen mit einer Watch. In dem Fall sollte das aber auch vorher klar gesagt werden. Das Konzept ist cool, aber ich finde nicht weit genug gedacht. Ich finds schade dass die Auswahl der Aktivitäten sehr begrenzt ist. Wenn ich nebenbei eine andere Sportart ausübe, gibt es keine Möglichkeit das einzutragen oder in den Plan zu integrieren. Selbst einfaches joggen ist nicht verfügbar, nur Laufband. Es gibt zwar das Zeit zu laufen Training, das auch echt sehr cool sind, aber das kann ich nicht im trainingsplan integrieren. Die Videos ist an sich nicht schlecht, wobei teilweise zu schnell, wenn man es zum ersten Mal macht. Auch die Aufnahme selbst, teilweise von zu weit weg, da ist es manchmal schwierig zu erkennen wie die Übung funktioniert. Da muss man sagen, findet man sehr viel bessere workouts auf YouTube. Die Trainingspläne sind auch nicht sonderlich gut durchdacht, man sagt wie oft man trainieren will und welches Training und genau das wird zusammen geshuffelt. Sich selbst für den jeweiligen Tag ein random Video rauszusuchen, schafft man dann doch auch alleine. Dafür brauch ich dieses Feature nicht, da hätte ich mir was personalisierteres gewünscht. Insgesamt: viel zu teuer für das was es ist.

gist: The product would be better if the music was chosen to enhance the exercise instead
title: Good app, but I have a few suggestions.
text: I’ve been using Fitness+ for several years.  I enjoy most of the workouts.  I especially like the fact that I can see my stats (heart rate, calories, etc.) while I’m working out.  I do have a few suggestions to improve the app.  (1) I’m a musician and I find it frustrating that the strength workouts never follow the beat of the music. My assumption is that Apple is trying to advertise Apple Music.  The product would be better if the music was chosen to enhance the exercise instead of the other way around.  (2) The introductions to the workouts are downright silly, something like: “First we’re going to do something and then something else and then we’ll repeat that three times”.  Tell me what muscles are being targeted or at least the name of the exercises we’ll be doing.  (3) I was looking forward to the dance routines, but they are too hard (and the Senior dance routines are too easy).  (4) The cooldowns in the strength videos are way too short, which would be ok, if the Mindful Cooldown videos were more comprehensive.  I end up making up my own cooldown routines, but I would rather follow an instructor.

gist: Could be a really cool app, but even with the new trainer/music audio focus, there’s
title: The music ruins it,just add more options!
text: Could be a really cool app, but even with the new trainer/music audio focus, there’s no way to escape the default playlists. Downloaded the app because my favorite yoga teacher moved here, but without being able to turn off the curated playlists, there’s no way to drop into a meditative space and fully connect with my own inner experience. How can I listen to my body and assess my mental and emotional state when the practice has a built-in “vibe” that’s intended to manufacture feelings externally, instead of honoring what’s present internally? People practice yoga in many ways and for many reasons,please consider those of us who prefer to practice without music. Many platforms include music as an optional feature for yoga and workouts, which is great, because everyone has different preferences! Having the ability to choose to practice in silence, select my own music, or, at the very least, opt for a more neutral playlist, something ambient or without lyrics, is an essential feature.

text: I absolutely love this app! There are always new workouts so you never grow tired of starting the same routine over and over. The coach’s are filled positivity helping to make each workout feel empowering. And the ability to have a small bit of control over what music you listen to is nice, although I wish there was more. It would be nice to create your own playlist to workout to or more music style options. There is also a good variety of workout styles to select from. I have been enjoying the strength training and cycling options on the days I workout at home. The yoga videos are amazing replacements for the days the yoga studio I attend is closed.  I want to give it a 5 but am giving it a very strong 4 as I don’t think many of the workouts are beginner friendly. I wouldn’t say anything is extremely advanced but as an example, I’m new to cycling and would love a way to build my endurance without randomly selecting a cycling workout and hoping for the best. It would be nice to have a way to filter easy vs hard workouts or have some indication of beginner, moderate, advanced levels. I have definitely learned that a workout is not any easier because it is 10 minutes vs a longer 20+ minute option.

title: Problèmes Techniques
text: Bonjour Apple, L’application Forme par Apple est une excellente idée, elle permet de créer, de suivre et d’atteindre un objectif sportif. Cependant, je trouve que l’application nécessite énormément de modifications et de résolutions, car elle rencontre un grand nombre de problèmes techniques. 1) L’actualisation de l’activité prend trop de temps, elle n’est ni rapide ni instantané. Il faut plus de 10 min pour savoir à quel niveau nous sommes (calories dépensées, nombre de pas, distance parcourue). 2) Lorsque l’activité a été mise à jour, certains facteurs restent bloqués au résultat précédent (par exemple les calories dépensées ont été actualisées mais pas le nombre de pas et la distance parcourue). Ces problèmes techniques sont au quotidien v tous les jours et également sur tous les appareils Apple de mes proches. Par ailleurs, l’ergonomie de l’application est à revoir, il manque le choix de la mesure des pas pour un objectif journalier et d’autres mesures, une option pour signaler un problème etc. De ce fait je n’ai ni pu signaler mes problèmes techniques sur l’application ni sur App Store qui ne propose pas une assistance ou un signalement de problème pour les personnes n’ayant pas fait d’achats sur Forme. Ainsi je vous ai fait cet avis afin de prendre en compte des problèmes techniques récurrents de l’application. Je vous remercie par avance de prendre en considération mon avis, de répondre à ma quête et de résoudre les problèmes dans les plus brefs délais. Cordialement

title: I Want to Love It
text: Sustain:   I love the social aspect I have with my family and friends who have Apple Watches.  It is the only reason I feel the need to use my Apple Watch over my Suunto or Garmin watches.  That said, I have some ideas for improvement in the event Apple actually takes feedback from consumers. Improve:   I love the ability to compete with my friends who have Apple Watches but it needs more customization capability.  My “opponents” often give up after failing to meet one day and although the workout should be their true prize, blah, blah, blah, I think it is a missed opportunity to help them succeed.  Daily competitions that allow more than 600 points would solve this problem instead of always having to settle for the we both win result.  Yes everyone wins if we are striving to be healthy,  but some actually want to compete against our friends and family because it is fun to push ourselves to achieve more.  Additionally, monthly competitions would also be a great motivator  to encourage sustained effort over longer periods instead of “losing” over one day because you were busy with life’s expected and unexpected events. I would also love to see a feature to add workouts that feature added weights such as weighted vests or ruck marches that increase calorie consumption based on the added weight.  In the era of functional fitness, CrossFit, and the multitude of ways people are staying fit, it seems like an important and easy solution to keep long time Apple product users such as myself interested.

title: A Frustrating Mix of Motivation and Glitches
text: Apple Fitness+ has the potential to be a fantastic motivator. The app gamifies exercise with colorful badges and rewards, making fitness fun and engaging. It's a great way to encourage people to stay active and reach their goals. However, persistent glitches in the app are undermining this positive experience. The most frustrating issue is a bug that randomly erases move awards. All that hard work and commitment can vanish in an instant, leaving users feeling discouraged and demotivated. It's incredibly disheartening to see your progress erased, and it makes it difficult to stay motivated to exercise. While Apple Fitness+ has some great features, these glitches are a major drawback. The app needs a serious update to fix these issues and ensure that users' hard work is recognized and rewarded. Until then, it's difficult to recommend the app wholeheartedly.

title: Dno dna
text: Tak dennej aplikacji sportowej na przestrzeni wielu lat jeszcze nie spotkałem, a wnikliwie przetestowałem ich z 10.  Od wielu lat używam cały czas aplikację GARMIN. Wspomagałem się jeszcze aplikacją endomondo, a po jej zamknięciu używam STRAVę?  W/w aplikacje prawidłowo naliczają kilometry, kalorie, kroki itd. Zgodnie ze zdobywanymi wartościami poszczególnych treningów prawidłowo są zaliczane odznaki.  W aplikacji Fitness tak niestety nie jest. Mógłbym na ten temat napisać długie wypracowanie, ale podam kilka przykładów.  Np. przy odznace „Wyzwanie miesiąca - wrzesień” trzeba było przejść lub przebiec 9km dziennie prze 14 dni. Ja miałem 10km dystansów 16 i odznaki nie otrzymałem.  Odznaka „7 treningów w tydzień” - w tym przypadku należy zaliczyć 7 co najmniej 5’ treningów. Te odznakę mam od roku i jeszcze jej nie zdobyłem, mimo że praktycznie każdego dnia mam jakiś trening, a czasem nawet kilka (ćwiczenia siłowe, joga, spacery, rower) i to znacznie dłuższych niż 5’. Jest tak dlatego, gdyż w wyzwaniu tym nie napisano jakie mają to być treningi. Odznaki „Cel W ruchu 200, 300, 400%” zdobywam praktycznie każdego dnia, ale odznaki nie otrzymuję. Wielokrotnie otrzymuję informacje, że muszę jeszcze spalić np. 100kcal, aby zdobyć odznakę. Mimo spełnienia wszystkich warunków odznaki nie otrzymuję. Takich problemów jest jeszcze dużo - dlatego też odinstalowałem tę beznadziejną aplikację.

gist: Now it will only register activity it deems intense enough to be considered “active exercise”.
title: Exercise ring issues
text: I used to like this app until they updated it. Before when you logged an exercise activity it counted all the minutes of that towards your exercise ring. This was a huge motivator for movement in general because even low intensity activity like golf or yoga helped meet the exercise ring goal. Now it will only register activity it deems intense enough to be considered “active exercise”. That 3.5 hour round of golf you just played? We’re only counting 14 min of that as exercise. Disheartening to say the least. Why have the capability of logging certain activities if you’re not going to count them anyways? Might as well call it a cardio ring if you’re requiring a certain heart rate cut off to meet your arbitrary requirements to be considered exercise.

As examples I’ve just completed two months of daily goals, two months of targets, 8 perfect move weeks, hit the 500 daily move targets etc. yet the awards still show data pre-these goals. One award is even missing completely.  What’s the point of designing a system to encourage better health, when the system itself doesn’t deliver realtime data and award the requisite goals.  Apple needs to fess up and let people know if they still support this product or remove it from the App Store.

title: Great Potential, But Needs Better Data Visualization
text: The Apple Fitness app is undoubtedly great, and I appreciate how seamlessly it tracks all my activities. The integration with the Apple Watch is excellent, and it keeps all my fitness data in one place. However, compared to what other apps offer, it’s just slightly below par. One key feature missing is a monthly or yearly recap of activities. Having a clear summary of my progress over time would be incredibly motivating. Additionally, the app could really benefit from visualizing recovery processes, which are essential for balanced fitness. Another suggestion would be to introduce widgets, like a monthly walking or running distance tracker, that could display data directly on the phone. These widgets and visualizations would make it easier to grasp long-term progress at a glance. Apple clearly has all the data; it’s just not being utilized to its fullest potential. As a loyal user who loves the Apple Watch, I’d urge the developers to put in the effort to make tracking and visualizing fitness data more insightful and engaging.

title: Rezension zur Apple Fitness-App: Verbesserungsbedarf bei der Synchronisation
text: Die Apple Fitness-App zeigt deutliche Schwächen im Bereich der Synchronisation, was die Nutzungserfahrung erheblich einschränkt. Besonders auffällig ist, dass rückwirkend manuell eingegebene Daten, die über andere Apps importiert werden sollten, nicht wie erwartet synchronisiert werden. Dies betrifft vor allem Anwendungen, die normalerweise nahtlos mit der Fitness-App zusammenarbeiten. Die mangelnde Integration sorgt für Frustration und erschwert eine verlässliche Nutzung der App, insbesondere für Nutzer, die Daten aus verschiedenen Quellen konsolidieren möchten. Eine zuverlässige Synchronisation ist essenziell für eine Fitness-App, um eine vollständige und akkurate Übersicht der persönlichen Aktivitäten zu gewährleisten. Apple sollte hier dringend nachbessern, um die App in diesem Punkt von „mangelhaft“ auf ein nutzerfreundlicheres Niveau zu heben.

gist: I’ve been using Apple Fitness for a while, and compared to Google Fit, it has
title: Bicycles
text: I’ve been using Apple Fitness for a while, and compared to Google Fit, it has a major drawback: without an Apple Watch, it cannot distinguish between walking and cycling, making it practically useless for tracking different activities accurately. It’s hard not to see this as a deliberate limitation to push users toward buying an Apple Watch. Meanwhile, Google Fit can differentiate activities using only a smartphone, proving that such functionality is possible without requiring extra hardware. This is just one example of how Apple’s ecosystem intentionally limits features to drive sales of additional devices, rather than providing the best possible experience. Over time, these restrictions are making Apple’s ecosystem less competitive compared to others. I hope Apple improves this by enabling better activity tracking on the iPhone alone, without forcing users into extra purchases.

text: There have been quite a few times that I have pulled up the app and been unable to play a video, or while I’m working out the video pauses and buffers before knocking off all together. This, especially, is frustrating because oftentimes I am halfway or further through the work out and have to start over. There isn’t a fast forward option or an option to pick up where you left off. I’m not able to just start over, I have time constraints which is why I built my custom plans in the app.  Also, even though I have selected the trainers I prefer, I still keep getting videos by the ones I don’t particularly like which makes it hard to enjoy the video or get the most out of it.  Aside from those things, the premise of the app is amazing and I love it when it works. text: I want to love this app. I really do. Its best feature is the ring. The satisfaction that comes with spinning it is unparalleled. It’s second best feature is the fact that it plugs directly into Apple’s health app. However, therein lies a fault because it takes forever to show your progress. In a world of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Bionic chipsets, there’s absolutely no reason why there can’t be real time updates. And with what we pay for these devices, we shouldn’t have to wait on our phones to do anything. One last fail, is the inability to challenge friends to custom challenges. Something as simple as spinning a ring once for the day; spinning a ring twice for the day; spinning a ring twice for the day for three days, five days, seven days straight. Custom, in every meaning of the word, or at least most. I know it’s impossible to make everyone happy, but this app could be so much more than it is, and the Apple DEV team owes it to its consumers to put in the work and brain power to make it happen.

gist: As much as I do love the app and everything that does to help me
title: Three star well deserved
text: As much as I do love the app and everything that does to help me track my fitness, I feel like it’s missing quite a few major components that could make reviewing the workout more beneficial for the user.  For any distance based activity, the only way to find out the top speed is to go into the workout details, click “show more” and then clicking “15 min” selection. Only then can you see your top speed for biking, running etc. This information should be included on the “Workout Details“ section-especially without having to adjust the time segment to see the ACTUAL top speed. As a training cyclist, this is very important to me.  The second feature I think would be excellent is to introduce a more triathlon style of switching workouts at my own pace without setting any Schedule before hand and losing current progress of an activity. My city has exercise gym equipment at various parks and I sporadically like to stop and do some repetitions for a few minutes during running or cycling. What this does to my full work out review at the end of the day is divided up my biking segments and my workout segments instead of showing it all lumped together with one number for each workout.   Lastly, one feature that I think would be nice is an easy edit for workout segments. There are times after a long bike ride that I forget to turn off the exercise and it continues to record me while I’m driving home. It would be nice if I could just trim that time as easily as I can edit a video in the photo app. If these features get implemented, I’ll change my review to five stars. I honestly do love the app and what it does for tracking, but some of the inconveniences are annoying.

title: No es para mí
text: Los entrenadores parecen gente estupenda. Hay mucha variedad. Y el uso del reloj de Apple es un plus. Pero con el tiempo, tras muchos meses de uso y de dejarlo y retomarlo varias veces a lo largo de los años, he descubierto que no es para mí. Al final usar Apple fitness ha terminado resultándome una cosa distópica, deshonesta y hasta dañina, a riesgo de sonar exagerado. Me terminé sintiendo como si en el exterior una guerra nuclear volvió inhabitable el planeta, o algo parecido, y alguien diseñó un programa de entrenamiento con muchos estudios de psicología y deporte en mente para intentar emular “cosas positivas” en los receptores que viven en bunkers mientras el mundo fuera se va al garete... Tras un tiempo me he dado cuenta que prefiero algo más honesto aunque no sea tan “falsamente” cálido, como FitnessBlender o software que tenga ese aire un poco menos de “diseño tras el telón” (dicho de otra manera, con unos protagonistas que se estén más bien calladitos y actúen en consecuencia, es decir, como si estuvieran grabándolos en un vídeo y fueran unos modelos estupendos y maravillosos de movimientos y ejercicios, y no mis fingidos amigos) o directamente algo verdaderamente real y “analógico”. Ver a unos tipos sonriéndole a la nada en la que uno se convierte tras una pantalla no me mola y encima pagando (y obviamente no lo digo por la cantidad, que es comedia comparada con un gimnasio, en términos brutos). Apple fitness es lo que es al fin y al cabo: un producto, un objeto muy bien diseñado y  envasado para presentarlo a sus consumidores con un mensaje de fondo sobre todo el “amor” con el que lo ofrecen al mundo, pero que no deja de ser un producto, un objeto, un fetiche para muchos, un simulacro.

gist: I really want to write a glowing review but I can’t.
title: Just not good enough
text: I really want to write a glowing review but I can’t. Don’t get me wrong, some of the workouts are good and the trainers (of the one I’ve tried - mainly female strength training) seem quality, but there is no way to filter by fitness level aka where you are on your fitness journey, ability; such as knee-friendly, seated or no jumping workouts. There isn’t even an option for choosing core training. You can perform a search, but the workouts are titled using there already exists activity type categories, so you don’t know what you’re looking at in the search results and of it doesn’t seem to relate, or I can’t tell if it does. And, I’m not about to go through every item to see. Plus the preview (which is all you can access without doing the workout itself,) or the blurb, doesn’t clearly give me that information I’m looking for. Thankfully this is a free trial, needless to say, I won’t be continuing with the subscription. These are easy wins which I think will make it safer and support the accessibility needs community too.

title: Vielen Dank
text: Für mittlerweile viele Jahre Fitness+. Und Vieles hat sich an mir und in mir durch und mit euch bewegt. Haltung, Körper, Seele und Geist, alles mit eurer Hilfe zu Besserem gesteigert. Bei aller Liebe jedoch nerven ein paar Sachen akut und nach wie vor: Ich möchte gern die Audio-Spur der Coaches deaktivieren, sodass ich nur die Übungen sehe (sind über die Jahre vertraut geworden), und damit nur die Musik genießen kann, was, wenn sie ausschließlich mal zu hören wäre bei all dem aggressiven Geschreie der Trainer, ein echter Gewinn sein könnte. Außerdem könnte man so vor allem die Antipathien bei ganz bestimmten Trainern minimieren, die einen einfach nur zu laut, zu schrill und vor allem unverständlich zu schnell anbrüllen. Vielleicht brauchen und wollen das manche, aber ich hätte gerne die Freiheit, das auszuschalten und mehr Musik zu bekommen. Ich denke, viele Leute wissen hier, welche bestimmten Personen wirklich unsympathisch coachen. Also Apple, dieses Feedback gab ich und viele andere Leute an vielen Stellen schon und wünsche mir, dass ihr das beherzigt. Machbar wäre es und das auch ziemlich leicht.

When I start hiking and have been out for three hours, then I expect my watch to say I have three hours/180 minutes of activity and not 54 minutes. title: Love the workouts, hate the syncing errors
text: I do yoga, strength, cycling, core, Pilates, kickboxing, and meditation regularly on my AppleTV. They’re all great. What’s not great is that while the activity log clearly shows I’ve finished workouts in all of these categories, the awards counters do not update even after several days. Some awards categories just completely disappear for no reason , strength and yoga no longer have counters or icons at all despite me having completed more than 50 of each. As someone who is motivated by the gamification aspects of Fitness+, it’s very frustrating that Apple hasn’t figured out how to do basic syncing between two of their devices: the AppleTV and the iPhone. Multiple other users have posted about this problem over the last 5 years. I hope Apple fixes this before another 5 pass.

title: Logistics issue
text: I really enjoy this app as the ‘rings’ concept is very motivating to close them every day and encourage an increase in overall fitness.  My issue is that now that I have an Apple Watch, if I miss a day of wearing my watch, my steps no longer show up and my “move” ring is no longer closed as it used to prior to me having an Apple Watch. I am dedicated to closing my rings every day so even if I forget to charge my watch, I would still like the data to reflect that I at least closed my move ring. Unfortunately when you forget to wear your watch, your steps are solely tracked by the health app and the health app and the fitness app do not share information. Ideally, as a user, I would like to see these two apps share information and I would like to see the fitness app pull the step data from the health app on the days I do not wear my watch. I contacted Apple support regarding this issue and the agent simply kept repeating the phrase “that is normal behavior” once you have an Apple Watch. This was really disheartening as my concerns were not addressed. I consider this a bug that should be addressed and fixed in the next IOS update.

text: Screenshots all show a ‘Plans’ tab between ‘Explore’ and ‘Library’. This has disappeared from my Fitness+ top bar. I now have no way to access my previous plans, nor create a new plan. When I go to delete app it warns I will lose my history (which seems strange considering all of Apple’s other cloud-based integrations through iCloud), although I’m almost at the point of doing so because Fitness+ has little utility for me without custom plans (I’m not going to search for every single workout I do, will just work out on my own at that point or use some other app). Before this issue, would have 3 stars - UI still not all that great, and workout video libraries hit and miss. I do like the integration with Apple Watch, I’m assuming it offers better privacy than competing fitness apps, and subscription is included with Apple One (which I already use anyway). title: Fairly Accurate On Steps, Horrifically Inaccurate In Calorie Count
text: So, as someone that has been on both sides of the isle, not being able to lose weight and losing too much weight, this app is odd. It counts calories at what seems like a discounted rate, I haven’t been updating my measurements but they aren’t too out of date. 6’2 and 179lbs, with a 30,603 steps down, that is or at least should be 1,200 calories burned, to this app it’s barely under 800. While it doesn’t seem like a huge amount, I can imagine less knowledgeable on their height and weight base burn and the amount of additional energy cost needed while being taller to do those kind of numbers getting discouraged by the numbers not reflecting the amount of work put in, quitting all together. That isn’t and has never been the goal for fitness, in fact it should only be to cultivate a split that works best for the individual. I know having an 800 calorie burn goal is obsessive, but I couldn’t imagine someone having a normal 500 calorie step goal, you’d probably need 20k steps minimum to make such a goal, and for context that’s about 8.5 to 10 MILES. That’s about one and a half times a walk through the FULL Central Park loop. I don’t know how they’ve messed up the math here, but they definitely have.

The depression it caused for no reason essentially was definitely avoidable had Apple had measures in place to prevent this. That was 200+ days ago now (I know because I’m working on a new streak), now today I was faced with not ending a workout and my watch recording a 12 hour workout on my app. Rewarding me for a new record long workout. WHAT?! so now essentially no matter how long I work out I will never beat a goal of 12 hours. Again, this should be “goals” that are allowed to individually be reset. I want to start all over but then I know it will affect my mental health with re-starting a streak again and I won’t risk that feeling again. Please work on these things, Apple. gist: Apple Fitness, paired with an Apple watch, has so much potential, but right now it
title: So much potential missed!
text: Apple Fitness, paired with an  Apple watch, has so much potential, but right now it feels like a missed opportunity. Where this app really falls short is in camaraderie, competition, and motivation. Other fitness platforms have figured out how powerful community can be. Weekly, monthly, and annual challenges. Team competitions. Badges, milestones, and real incentives to stay consistent. These are the features that actually keep people moving, and Apple is barely scratching the surface. There is little sense of friendly competition or accountability. You cannot easily participate in meaningful group challenges, long-term streak competitions, or seasonal goals with friends the way you can on apps like Myzone® or Peloton. Those platforms make fitness feel social, fun, and addictive in the best way. Apple Fitness, by comparison, feels isolated and flat. I was also disappointed that there was no real “Year in Review.” Many fitness and lifestyle apps now provide an annual recap that celebrates your progress, milestones, and consistency. It is motivating, shareable, and helps users reflect on how far they have come. Apple completely missed that opportunity. Apple has the data, the ecosystem, and the user base to be the undisputed leader in fitness tracking. But right now, it falls far short of what is possible. If Apple took cues from platforms like Myzone® and Peloton and leaned into challenges, community, and yearly progress storytelling, this could easily become the best fitness app on the market. Instead, it feels like a basic tracker with very little soul.

title: Dexcom G7 in Fitness App
text: Dear Apple Support Team, I would like to request the ability to display blood glucose data directly within the Apple Fitness / Workout app on Apple Watch. Blood glucose is an important metric for many athletes, and it is especially critical for people with diabetes during exercise. Glucose levels directly affect performance, safety, and real-time training decisions. I am using a Dexcom G7 continuous glucose monitor, which transfers glucose data directly to the Apple Watch (Direct to Watch). While this works reliably, the data is only visible in the Dexcom app or as a watch face complication. During activities such as cycling, I have to switch away from the Workout screen to check my glucose level, which is inconvenient and unsafe while moving. As Apple Health is positioned as the central platform for health data, I would expect blood glucose to be treated as a first-class metric, similar to heart rate, and be optionally visible within the Workout display itself. Integrating real-time glucose values into Apple Fitness would significantly improve usability, safety, and inclusiveness for athletes with diabetes. Thank you for considering this feedback. Kind regards

I’m a wheelchair user, and while I’m an ambulatory wheelchair user and can take a few steps at a time, I can’t stand for more than a minute - sometimes not even that - and the number of seated exercise programs I can find on the app is one. In the nicest possible way, most of us will end up disabled at some point in our lives, the more so as we get older, and it shouldn’t be beyond the imagination of the product manager to think that a broader range of workouts might serve a bigger audience. So, hit me up for a paid subscription when you actually decide that us disabled folk are worth catering to as well.

text: I like the feature allowing you to challenge your past self when biking, but the UI is missing some key features. Also, why doesn’t it default to in order of nearest start location instead of just by Date? I’m probably not going to challenge a route with a start that is kilometres away from me. Many of my routes are commuting to things so I route there and a route back.  I would love to see a feature where my results can be combined, and my list of challenge options will automatically orientate themselves based on current location yet would be aware of loop routes. (this will need to be an op-in setting or easily accessible toggle switch)  Also, like the complications on an Apple Watch. Why can’t I modify my display for when working out? gist: However, the user experience , especially around customization , needs significant improvement.
title: Lack of User Experience Customization
text: I genuinely enjoy the workouts and the coaching quality on Apple Fitness+. The trainers are engaging, the content is motivating, and the overall concept is excellent. However, the user experience , especially around customization , needs significant improvement. The biggest issue is the lack of true editing within Custom Plans. If I want to make even small adjustments, I often have to rebuild the entire plan from scratch instead of simply modifying existing settings. This makes it unnecessarily time-consuming and discourages flexibility as my schedule or fitness needs change. The “swap” feature is also very limited. Instead of allowing users to freely swap in any workout that fits their needs, the app only allows selections from a restricted list. This reduces personalization and makes it harder to adapt workouts to real-life preferences or goals. Another usability challenge is equipment selection when creating schedules. Currently, it feels too restrictive , for example, I may want workouts that combine both mat work and dumbbells so I can alternate between standing exercises and floor work for recovery or muscle balance. The current options don’t reflect how many people actually train, and it limits creativity and practicality. Overall, the workouts themselves are great, but the customization tools and interface feel rigid and not very user-friendly. Improving flexibility, editing capabilities, and equipment filtering would significantly enhance the experience.

title: Problema conteggio vasche app nuoto con tavoletta
text: Sono un cliente Apple assolutamente fidelizzato e da molti anni ormai utilizzo regolarmente l’app nativa Allenamento Nuoto di Apple su Apple Watch e, in generale, la trovo ben strutturata e semplice da usare. Tuttavia, ho riscontrato un problema significativo nel conteggio delle vasche durante gli allenamenti in piscina. In particolare, il numero totale di vasche risulta spesso errato quando si eseguono “esercizi” solo gambe con la tavoletta o senza e o con un solo braccio per volta. In queste situazioni il sistema non riconosce correttamente il movimento, probabilmente perché si basa principalmente sulla bracciata per rilevare le vasche completate. Di conseguenza, diverse vasche non vengono conteggiate oppure vengono conteggiate solo parzialmente, falsando i dati finali dell’allenamento (distanza totale, passo medio e calorie). Questo limite incide in modo rilevante sulla precisione complessiva del monitoraggio, soprattutto per chi segue programmi strutturati che includono serie tecniche di esercizi a gambe o braccia, per migliorare la tecnica, molto comuni nel nuoto. Sarebbe auspicabile un aggiornamento software che migliori l’algoritmo di rilevamento, integrando in modo più efficace i movimenti delle gambe e i cambi di direzione a fine vasca, anche in assenza di bracciate complete. Spero tantissimo che venga introdotto un miglioramento in futuro, perché l’app ha grandi potenzialità ma, allo stato attuale, il conteggio delle vasche non è sempre affidabile per allenamenti completi e strutturati e non vorrei trovarmi costretto ad usare dispositivi di altre marche per ovviare al problema.

title: Review: Great concept, but key improvements needed
text: Apple Fitness+ offers strong variety and high production quality, but for a premium-priced service, some important improvements are necessary. Many exercises lack a proper lateral camera angle during explanations. A simple side view at the start of each movement (squats, push-ups, shoulder work, yoga alignment, etc.) would greatly improve posture understanding and execution safety without affecting the clean aesthetic. The absence of voice dubbing is also a major limitation. Subtitles are not practical during intense workouts or yoga poses. Users cannot maintain correct alignment while reading. This becomes even more problematic because the app does not allow rewinding during a session. If you miss or misunderstand a cue, you cannot quickly go back to review it. Poorly executed movements repeated over time can increase the risk of discomfort or injury. A voice-over option would significantly improve accessibility and safety. Dance sessions would benefit from clearer breakdowns and more neutral choreography options. In styles like salsa, masculine and feminine patterns traditionally differ. Offering more neutral variations would make sessions feel more technically balanced. Finally, offline playback should be more reliable. Even after downloading workouts, launching them often requires an internet connection. The offline experience needs to be smoother. Fitness+ is good, but still highly perfectible. With better technical clarity, language accessibility, and improved usability, it could truly match Apple’s standard of excellence.

title: Great but with great flaws
text: I feel really conflicted because on one side I find it really great to exercise from home, with a wide variety of options, and also with meditation included.  On the other side its flaws really feel unjustifiable for such a huge company, especially considering these are things customers have complained about for years.  The two main issues for me are the lack of “levels” (beginner, medium, experienced etc), as I often end up with workouts way beyond my current fitness or experience level, when being able to increase difficulty up step by step would be the most beneficial option.  The other main flaw is the fact that there isn’t a “resume workout” function or a way to go back/forward in the exercise (if the app/internet crashes, if you missed something etc). title: exactly what I needed
text: This app has helped me get back into a regular fitness routine after a difficult moment in my life. I’ve used fitness+ for over 4 years. It may sound cheesy but, on hard days, it feels really good to have a trainer motivate you through a workout. I appreciate how trainers on Apple Fitness+ treat workouts as physical and mental endeavors that one should be proud of for doing.  The variety of workouts you can do is AMAZING! Great if you want to mix things up or if, you know, are quick to judge your improvements for one type of exercise and need to try something else for a while.  The music used to bother me but then I learned that you can filter by type - and that they’re always adding more! I love the new J Pop and K Pop!! More more more!!!! It’s always such a sweet surprise when I pick a new workout and it’s themed after a month or a celebration. As someone in both LGBTQ and AAPI communities, I really love how inclusive the trainers and the workouts can be. Gyms can be much less forgiving…and wildly expensive!!

text: Korzystanie z tej aplikacji jest frustrujące głównie przez bardzo ograniczone możliwości przesyłania obrazu na telewizor. W dzisiejszych czasach brak wsparcia dla popularnych metod jak Chromecast czy bezpośrednie odtwarzanie w przeglądarce to spory minus. Użytkownik zostaje praktycznie zmuszony do korzystania z AirPlay lub Apple Tv 4K, co znacząco podnosi koszt i komplikuje cały setup. Aplikacja fitness powinna być wygodna i dostępna na różnych urządzeniach, szczególnie że treningi często lepiej ogląda się na większym ekranie. Szkoda, bo sama zawartość treningowa jest na dobrym poziomie, ale brak elastyczności technologicznej skutecznie psuje całe doświadczenie. Z tego powodu nie zdecyduję się na rozpoczęcie płatnej subskrypcji, trudno uzasadnić dodatkowy koszt, skoro podstawowa funkcjonalność nie spełnia oczekiwań. W efekcie aplikacja sprawia wrażenie bardziej ograniczającej niż pomocnej.

gist: Apple TV and Watch Ultra 2 connection unreliable
title: Enttäuschende Verbindung zwischen AppleTv 4K und Apple Watch Ultra 2
text: Die Apple Fitness App bietet grundsätzlich gute Trainingsinhalte und eine ansprechende Oberfläche. Allerdings ist die Verbindung zwischen dem Apple TV 4K und meiner Apple Watch Ultra 2 alles andere als zuverlässig. Immer wieder wird die Uhr nicht erkannt oder die Verbindung bricht ab, sodass Trainingsdaten wie Herzfrequenz und Kalorienverbrauch nicht korrekt übertragen werden. Gerade bei einem Premium-Produkt und einem entsprechend hohen Preisniveau sollte man erwarten können, dass die Geräte aus demselben Ökosystem reibungslos miteinander funktionieren. Apple bewirbt die nahtlose Integration zwischen Apple TV und Apple Watch sehr stark. Wenn diese Funktion jedoch regelmäßig Probleme verursacht, sollte entweder die technische Umsetzung verbessert oder die Werbung entsprechend realistischer gestaltet werden. Für den Preis und den Anspruch, den Apple an sich selbst stellt, ist das leider enttäuschend. Ich hoffe auf eine zeitnahe Lösung durch ein Software-Update.

Sometimes I want to change the order of that week’s workouts, but I can’t. Or change the type of workout (not just the length) for a specific day but, again, I can’t.  • Why do German subtitles keep popping up? I don’t want to keep stopping to change the CC settings for that video.

title: Leicht enttäuscht!😞
text: Apple Fitness+ macht mir grundsätzlich wirklich viel Spaß. Die Kurse sind abwechslungsreich, die Trainerinnen und Trainer sind motivierend, sympathisch und fachlich einfach top. Man hat wirklich das Gefühl, gemeinsam mit ihnen zu trainieren, und genau das motiviert mich regelmäßig, dranzubleiben. Auch die monatlichen Challenges und Aufgaben finde ich sehr gelungen. Sie geben einem ein klares Ziel und sorgen dafür, dass man sich immer wieder neu aufrafft , selbst an Tagen, an denen die Motivation eigentlich im Keller sitzt. Umso frustrierender ist es leider, dass hart erarbeitete Auszeichnungen nicht zuverlässig angezeigt oder vergeben werden. Es ist jetzt schon mehrfach vorgekommen, dass in Apple Fitness+ einfach Tage fehlen oder gelöscht wirken. Diese lassen sich scheinbar nur eventuell über ein Backup wiederherstellen , und selbst das ist nicht sicher. Zusätzlich würde dabei die Arbeit des jeweiligen Tages möglicherweise nicht berücksichtigt werden. Das ist wirklich enttäuschend, denn für mich sind diese Auszeichnungen mehr als nur kleine digitale Abzeichen. Sie zeigen meinen Fortschritt, meine Disziplin und meine Erfolge. Wenn am Ende eines Monats die Auszeichnung fehlt, obwohl ich hart dafür gearbeitet habe, fühlt es sich an, als würde meine Leistung nicht gewürdigt werden. Es sieht dann so aus, als wäre ich einfach nicht fleißig genug gewesen , obwohl das nicht stimmt. Der Support war bisher zwar freundlich und bemüht, aber leider konnte sich das Problem niemand wirklich erklären oder dauerhaft lösen. Vielleicht nehme ich diese Auszeichnungen auch sehr ernst, aber genau sie motivieren mich, jeden Monat weiterzumachen. Ich würde mir daher sehr wünschen, dass dieses Problem ernsthaft geprüft wird und es konkrete Lösungsvorschläge gibt. gist: calorie numbers inaccurate or differ from Apple Health
title: Gut
text: Gute App, aber wichtige Funktionen fehlen! Die Apple Fitness-App ist grundsätzlich gut und übersichtlich, allerdings fehlen wichtige Funktionen, die bei anderen Fitness-Apps wie Nike oder Adidas bereits verfügbar sind. Besonders enttäuschend ist die Funktion, abgeschlossene Trainings als Bild herunterzuladen oder zu teilen. Dabei werden nur sehr wenige Informationen, beispielsweise die Gesamtzeit, angezeigt. Es wäre wünschenswert, wenn man den Hintergrund individuell anpassen und weitere Trainingsdaten wie das Datum, die Herzfrequenz, die Distanz und andere wichtige Statistiken einblenden könnte. Andere Fitness-Apps bieten diese Möglichkeiten bereits – bei Apple fehlt diese Funktion leider noch. Ein weiteres Problem ist die Bewegungserkennung während des Trainings. Wenn man beim Joggen stehen bleibt, um sich zu dehnen, und sich dabei nur mit den Armen oder Händen bewegt, scheint die App diese Bewegungen teilweise weiterhin als Aktivität zu zählen. Dadurch können die aufgezeichneten Trainingsdaten ungenau werden. Hier sollte die Bewegungserkennung dringend verbessert werden. Mein Wunsch an Apple: Bitte diese Funktionen mit einem Update nachrüsten! Die Grundlage der App ist gut, aber gerade bei der Trainingsauswertung, beim Teilen von Ergebnissen und bei der Genauigkeit der Bewegungserkennung gibt es noch deutliches Verbesserungspotenzial. Andere Anbieter zeigen, dass es besser geht. Ich würde mir wünschen, dass Apple hier nachbessert, damit die Fitness-App ihrem Potenzial wirklich gerecht wird.

gist: It is completely absurd that a paid subscription service like Apple Fitness+ lacks basic video
title: Rigid service bad interface
text: It is completely absurd that a paid subscription service like Apple Fitness+ lacks basic video playback controls like standard rewinding or fine scrubbing. Trying to follow complex movement practices like Yoga or Pilates is infuriating. When learning a new pose or trying to check form, alignment, and foot placement, missing a single visual cue means you either have to restart the entire video segment or guess the movement blindly. Removing the ability to simply jump back 10 seconds to rewatch an instructional setup is a massive oversight for an instructional platform. It prioritizes a rigid playback experience over actual user learning and safety. Until Apple adds basic media playback controls,like every other fitness app and video streaming platform on the planet,this service is not worth a monthly fee for anyone trying to actually master form.

title: Good but Long Overdue for some new features
text: I’ve been using Apple Fitness for several years now. Started with my watch about 10 years ago and signed up for Fitness+ workouts about 6 years ago. The Pros:  I love the variety of workouts and that each category gets several new workouts each week. I enjoy the trainers and that they rotate who leads and include a trainer focused on modifications. For the most part I can keep up with them thanks to the format and explanation prior to each set. I also like that there is a way to sort and select different workout durations and targeted body areas (although yoga needs this option!). The Cons:  • Not being able to rewind or fast-forward is infuriating. If you get interrupted or miss what they showed, you can’t run it back to catch what you missed. If the app quits and you have to restart a workout, you can’t skip ahead.  • Sometimes the workouts stall during the countdown and if you clear the app and start over it still shows that you’re in a workout and asks you to cancel, though there’s nothing to actually quit. Also, if a workout ends and I don’t go back to the start screen before turning off the Apple TV, the next time I open the app it won’t let me connect and I have to restart the whole system. No other apps do this so I don’t think I it’s the device itself. • Explicit music is popping up more and more and I really wish they used clean edits or gave an option to lower the music volume. I don’t like having to worry about what music content is in the background if my kids walk in and frankly some of the song selections are not tasteful and I don’t like that I’m stuck listening to explicit language or trashy content.  • I have been pregnant and regaining strength postpartum twice since I started using Fitness+ and though many of the female trainers have been pregnant over the years, the prenatal and postpartum programs have only one set of videos that have never been added to are severely lacking. At this point I don’t know how there isn’t a comprehensive nine-month prenatal program and at least a 12-week recovery program. What’s there now is abysmally limited and it feels like a huge missed opportunity on their part. It would maybe be enough to attract a mother that’s getting started with exercise but to someone who is very active there just isn’t enough and there could easily be more videos in longer formats.

text: 1. 字幕設計違背運動安全與本意 在進行瑜伽、核心或正念緩和等運動時，使用者需要專注於肢體動作與呼吸，多數時間視線並不會停留在 iPad 或手機螢幕上。要求非英語系用戶在運動過程中頻繁抬頭或扭轉脖子去「閱讀繁體中文字幕」，不僅容易造成運動傷害，更完全失去放鬆身心的本意。 2. 語音活動對非英語系用戶形同虛設 主打戴著 AirPods 就能出門的「戶外健走」等語音活動，在沒有提供中文語音的情況下，對台灣用戶毫無實用價值，完全浪費了硬體設備的優秀體驗。 3. 忽視現有 AI 技術，服務明顯落後 在 AI 語音合成（TTS）與即時翻譯技術已極度成熟的今日，貴公司連搭載 M4 晶片的設備與高階手機都能推出，卻在每月收費的 Fitness+ 軟體服務上，吝於投入資源生成多國語言配音。這種只提供單一語言語音的做法，令人難以相信這是全球頂尖科技公司的產品水準。 【具體建議】 請儘速利用成熟的 AI 生成技術，為 Fitness+ 的所有影片與語音活動加入「中文配音」選項。哪怕初期是 AI 生成的語音，只要指令清晰，都能大幅降低使用門檻。在未提供完善的多國語音支援前，目前的 Fitness+ 對台灣用戶而言，完全不具備訂閱價值。

title: Potentially great but...
text: Once again the developers have created a beautiful app. They are one of the most consistent developers in terms of features and UI. Their apps are consistently the best designed and best supported apps in their categories. I was really looking forward to the release of this app. Many calorie tracking apps suffer from feature bloat and template-like app design. This feels carefully crafted and comes supporting Siri Shortcuts and an Apple Watch app from the off (although mine hasn’t appeared yet). Unfortunately this app lacks the standard and most needed feature of a calorie tracking app: barcode scanning. Without scanning it becomes far too much effort to track calories, and way less accurate. Another issue is that the listed foods are all American, meaning users in Europe will struggle to find suitable foods to log. I’m hoping these issues will be addressed in the future as this is almost certainly the calorie tracking app I would like to use, but functionally it’s just not up to standard yet.

gist: I’m pretty sure this is one of the few (if only) calorie tracking apps that
title: Beautiful, easy, no-subscription calorie counter
text: I’m pretty sure this is one of the few (if only) calorie tracking apps that doesn’t make you sign up for an account, pay for a subscription, and all of that other extra stuff that most of them require. It does ask you a bunch of questions when you start (weight, height, birthdate, etc) to calibrate it and a goal weight. The purpose of the goal weight is to give you an idea of how many calories per day someone with your body type should have. If you’re fine with your weight, just put that in and it will just help you to maintain that. Once you’re past that, the main interface is beautiful and intuitive. Your calories are visualized as little balls in a larger ball and they increasingly add more balls whenever you log calories. It shows you how many you’ve consumed so far and how many calories you have left so that you can meet your daily intake amount. It’s pretty easy to log your foods as you go along. Just press the + sign, toggle the meal (breakfast/lunch/dinner/snacks/other), add the amount of calories, and submit it.  You can create custom entries you can name and enter the calories as well as the macros (protein/fats/carbs). You can also use their search which I haven’t used so much but seems to cover many of the more commons foods/drinks etc. This is a great calorie app and like I said, the lack of all the other nonsense that seems to be required for most other tracking apps is its best feature. You don’t have to try to lose weight or do anything, you are allowed to simply track your calories if you want. No subscriptions, no life-gurus/coaches, no custom diet plans. Its everything I wanted, with none of that other crap

gist: But even in the US of A the exact values of a cup (and oz.
title: Great - as long as you are in the USA
text: An excellent App from the US flawed by a blatant disregard for the rest of the world  It appears that it never occurred to the developers that Cups is not a known unit of measurement in most countries. We use liters and grams instead. But even in the US of A the exact values of a cup (and oz. and inch) are defined in metric values, so in many cases the conversion is simple. Why the app does not do this for all types of food is beyond me.  What good are the preferences for kg and liters if I still see cups and oz.? And of course outside of the us the barcode scanner is completely useless.  The developers point out that they use an US database. Well, that was obvious. But if they want to market their app in the rest of the world, that might have to change. Most Germans don‘t know the English word for Blumenkohl, Pfälzer Saumagen or Maultaschen anyway, and don’t care for US brands that are not available here. So either add a warning that this is not properly localized, or add more databases. That being said, when I travel to the US - which will never happen, but still - I’ll like to switch to the US database.

gist: Not bloated with ads or its own social network, & it doesn't bombard you with
title: Minimalistic UI; needs better food database
text: The good: ~ Simple calorie counter with a minimalistic UI. Not bloated with ads or its own social network, & it doesn't bombard you with hastags & acronyms like an ADHD teenager (cough, Noom). ~ Easy to create custom 'plates', which let you log foods you frequently eat with one tap. ~ Seamless integration w/ Apple Health app. ~ Good macronutrient tracker. Must have premium to use it though. ~ Can purchase a lifetime premium account, instead of having to subscribe indefinitely. The bad: ~ AWFUL food database. Difficult to search & many incorrect entries, with no option to flag them for review. The premium search seems much better, but I'm not sure it's worth $15/yr or $30/lifetime. (I very much like this app, but this is the reason I uninstalled). ~ I strongly prefer a target calorie range instead of a single value. I've only seen this on SparkPeople though. Some days I eat too much & others I eat way too little. Also, I find a range much more realistic than a single number. Is anything less than that target good? Is it Price is Right style - get as close to the number without going over? 🤷‍♀️ ~ No diet safeguards on this app. Which might be good people, but could be dangerous for others. Calory recommended I eat ~900 calories/day to lose weight fast. Most medical professionals warn against eating less than 1200 cal/day for women.

gist: I was looking for an app which would add up my calories and macros for
title: Works well
text: I was looking for an app which would add up my calories and macros for me, and Calory works well for my purposes. One problem which I had with other calorie counting apps is them insisting that you have a weight goal in mind when using the app. I do not own a scale, as I prefer to use metrics other than weight to measure my health, and my wife has an eating disorder. Without a scale, most calorie counters are all but useless, but not so with this one. While I did need to give a weight upon opening the app, I could then adjust the number of my target calories and macros manually and since then it has worked very well for me. My favourite part of using an app rather than doing the math on paper as I did before is the UI, which shows me at a glance how many calories, protein, fat and carbs I have left in a day. The app’s UI is very clean, and it did not take me long to master it. My biggest issue with the app at the moment is that I have found that customizing the quantity of food is at times very difficult. When I search for food, sometimes I am able to just write how many grams or cups I ate. Other times, however, I have to change the units of the serving size to something which I can measure, and then do the math and tell the app what percentage of a portion I ate. For example, tonight I made a dish with 60 grams of red onions. When I searched “red onions” in the app, I was given the choice of immeasurable units (I don’t know how much a slice is because it really depends on the onion) or even measurable units (the closest I could find was 100g, so I told the app that I ate 0.6 of a portion.) If there is a way to do this without having to do any extra math I would be delighted to know, because as I said, I was in the market for a calorie tracker with the express purpose of finding one that could save me time by doing the math for me. That said, I feel that myself and anyone in a similar situation would have a better user experience if the ability to customize the quantity of my food was easier to find. Perhaps just having a suggested quantity along with the ability to edit this quantity would be helpful in this case. I acknowledge that I am fortunate to own a kitchen scale, and many people may feel that an approximation of their food quantities is sufficient. Aside from that, I would recommend this app to anyone who is looking for a clean, simple, flexible calorie counter.

text: I love this app. It’s the only food tracking app that allows me to prioritize sodium in addition to my macros and calories. It’s widgets are top notch as well, and I love the way the little red balls fill up the screen when you go over. A perfect visual metaphor.  Minor frustration: when adding food to a given meal, if I select an item from my recent list, the item goes into the meal I last ate it with. For example, I click the plus sign on lunch to add a scoop of protein powder, and my recent food features the protein powder I had with dinner the night before. That scoop gets added to dinner despite me having clicked the add to lunch button.  Feature Request: the thing that would make this app absolutely indispensable to me would be the ability to pre load and then check off items. For example, in the morning I tend to pre plan my day, constructing a meal plan that fits perfectly to my macros.  I’d love a little check box or something that let me keep track of which pieces of my meal Plan I had consumed. It wouldn’t need to interact with the totals to be useful, those could be updated right away, it would just allow me to remember which snacks and such I had eaten. This is particularly useful with supplements where it can be hard to remember how many scoops of protein I’ve had in the day for example.

title: Very Happy
text: Update: 12 June 2021 The app keeps getting better ie. If the food you are searching for manually or via barcode isn’t found you can scan the nutrition label and give it a name. Not a new addition but it is an awesome added feature that is well worth mentioning. Pros: -great support from the developer. I got answers to questions before I had even committed to a subscription. -the help website is quite comprehensive and will likely have an answer to your questions. -very cost effective in comparison to the industry leader? MyFitnessPal. (thousands of searchable recipes). -syncs using iCloud to iPhone, iPad or Mac with one subscription. -detailed macro nutrients so you can see your ongoing daily intake of proteins/sugars/ fat etc. -you set your activity level and the app calculates your daily calories. Ie. If you set your activity level from sedentary to very active; it will suggest a daily calorie intake based on that. There is also a "calories burned" setting. You can turn this on and allow access to the Health app. (not sure how this works) -if you often eat the same meal (breakfast cereal & milk, coffee, cream, sugar etc) you can save this as one of your "plates". Next time you have this same meal; one click adds ALL of the ingredients. Cons: -takes a bit of time to become familiar with it, but in the end, it is worth it. -Canadian food database and barcode scanners are good, but needs improvement and I'm pretty confident that this will improve. In conclusion; you'll need a subscription to access all of the features but I think you'll like it. Recommended.

gist: I’ve used a lot of different calorie counting apps and this one is shaping up
title: Great app, but needs a few fixes
text: First of all I really like the simplicity of this app and as a very visual person I LOVE that I can just take a quick peek at the home screen to gauge how I’m doing on my calorie goal without having to do the math. I’ve used a lot of different calorie counting apps and this one is shaping up to be my favorite but there are a few things I’ve been frustrated with.  1. My calorie goal, weight goal, starting weight, and stats of that nature keep resetting to their default numbers. I keep periodically needing to re-enter my manual calorie goal and my current weight/weight goal. The app is showing that I gained 99 pounds in 1 day lol and I don’t know how to fix it, because there doesn’t seem to be a way to manually edit your weight from previous days, only the day you’re currently on. I’d like the resetting issue to be resolved and I’d also like to be able to edit the info from previous days.  2. I also don’t like that if I want to see info about my daily macros I can’t access that info after the day-of. The day begins at midnight, but for someone like me who works nights sometimes I don’t get a chance to enter all my food before the day ends and then I can’t see how much protein I had or how many carbs or whatever. You can only see your calorie totals on days that have passed, not an overview of all your info, which I find frustrating. If I want to know if I hit yesterday’s protein goal I need to manually calculate that info, which is tedious. I’d also like to be able to look at my weekly or monthly overview and be able to see how many days I hit my protein goals (or whatever goals, for me my diet just happens to be very focused on protein right now). Other than those 2 issues, I think it’s a great app and I will continue using it. I’ve recommended it to a couple friends who also really like it, but they’ve also expressed the same frustrations.

gist: The only complaint I have is about the net carb count.
title: Great app, but a somewhat inaccurate net carb count.
text: This app is fantastic, and it syncs up perfectly with the WaterMinder app as well as the Health app. The only complaint I have is about the net carb count. Fiber isn’t the only thing that can be subtracted from total carbs in order to calculate net carbs. For example, sugar alcohol and erythritol are two ingredients that also count towards calculating net carbs. However, the app’s current design doesn’t count anything other than the fiber content when it calculates net carbs, mostly because there’s no place in the app for these nutrients/ingredients to be noted in the food items. When adding in our own foods, it’d be great if there were spots for items such as sugar alcohol (g) and erythritol, and other items as well, to make calculating net carbs more accurate for people on special diets who can only consume X# of net carbs daily. One other issue of note is that the “meal” function doesn’t work properly. Every time I try creating a “meal” in the settings, it will end up glitching when I go and add said meal to my calorie count later. It doubles some food items, removes other food items, and then when I try going back into the settings and, for example, removing the extra food items it added for no reason, it ends up removing ALL of the food items even though I save it as being one of each food item. Very annoying.

gist: Used this app for 2 + years; during that time my first year was positive
title: ❌ Lifetime purchase switched to FoodNoms
text: Used this app for 2 + years; during that time my first year was positive but things progressively worsened… I started encountering bugs around the one year mark and couldn’t use shortcuts to input food anymore. This was frustrating and support wasn’t able to help diagnose the issue. Widgets also don’t update their display properly. And while I’d purchased a lifetime membership, I didn’t see many changes coming to Calory (besides the feature updates to match new iOS additions like widgets and shortcuts). I didn’t feel like the core experience was very improved, and, while I get that many users are hoping for specific features for their use cases, I generally saw my experience using Calory decline as changes were made that didn’t improve what I believe to be the core user experience. I get that a calorie tracking app shouldn’t be constantly changing the core feature of calorie tracking, but there’s a lot that could be done with Calory to  match what FoodNoms is doing. I will happily pay a subscription to have a calorie tracking app that is efficient, effective, and ultimately provides me the ability to create a feedback loop to make decisions that affect my overall health through dietary choices. Calory is no longer that app.

text: So far I like the design of the app a lot. I like that it’s easy to add calories from a meal, which makes this app preferable than many other calorie counting apps for me. However, I am absolutely baffled that there is no way to log exercise. This should be a very simple feature to implement. If I can add positive calories from food, it should be relatively simple to add negative calories from exercise. All the developers would need to do is just add one more category. Had I realized you couldn’t do that at all, I probably would have purchased a different app instead. It’s rather disappointing because I see reviews from a year ago complaining about the same thing, but clearly nothing has been done to change it. If you do work out though, you’ll need to find another way to keep track of your exercise and mentally adjust the day’s allotted calories accordingly.
