gist: I just want to be able to add x grams of y food into the
title: Bloated and Cluttered UI Makes Me Angry
text: I just want to be able to add x grams of y food into the app and have it log that amount of carbs, fats, protein, saturated fats, and calories. Instead it makes you put it into a meal, then a plate that goes into the meal, then a food into a plate, and then select a QUANTITY (not grams) to input into your log. I boil my chicken breast and they don’t have an option for that. So I enter the nutrition info for 98 grams of chicken breast. I go to add the food to the meal (scrolling passed all their preset foods and plates) and all I can enter for the amount of chicken breast is a quantity. So if I weigh an extra 36 grams of chicken breast, I need to divide 134/98 to get the quantity or I need to edit my custom food for this specific meal. Say I make a typo and erroneously add a plate/food that I did not eat. There’s no easy way to delete an entry, you can only edit them. So if you make too many entries you have to go through all this trouble to get rid of them. Say you don’t want to group your food into meals and have your home screen cluttered with “Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Other”. YOU CANT. Say you don’t want to use the plates feature. It can’t be gotten rid of. Say you don’t want to use their nutrition information. Then you have to scroll all the way to the last tab to select My Foods every time you want to make an entry. gist: Calory has a nice, clean and clutter free interface but that’s where it stops.
title: Clean but basic and full of bugs
text: Calory has a nice, clean and clutter free interface but that’s where it stops.  Scraping of recipes from the internet is a complete disaster and the user has no ability to edit these once imported. Manually creating recipes is also a chore with the ability to only add one… ingredient… at… a… time… and having required fields for no reason. Some entered recipes do not correctly calculate calories and nutrients per serving which results in incorrect information being logged. AI recipes (whatever this is) just doesn’t work at all, no recipe is returned.  User profile weight does not update from the Health app even though permission has been granted. Seems the read permission is only for updating weight in the tracking section. This could potentially affect the users calorie intake if its not updated - one to watch out for if you are using this to try to control your weight.  The camera orientation is locked making scanning of UPC codes pretty tricky on iPad unless your device is in portrait orientation. Scanning of nutritional labels is also a disaster and simply does not work and you can only scan UPC codes from US so the app is pretty useless for users from other markets.  Having Calory on two devices doubles up everything, such as macros, plates, etc. And there’s the case of the disappearing logs! If you try to re-log your food, the nutrients and macros are doubled up in Health app. Trying to correct this is like navigating a minefield. There’s no integration with Water Minder which seems like a missed opportunity.  Plates is a nice idea but when logging a plate as a meal it lists every ingredient in the plate rather than the plate name. Having “Meals” instead of “Plates” would be more beneficial.  The app gets 4 stars for the design but the functionality reduces it to 2 stars. I’m glad of the trial period, I want to like this app but I don’t think its worth the subscription cost unfortunately as it is a very poor implementation of what a food logging app should be. The results from this app could lead people down the wrong path as they are consistently confronted with incorrect logs and information.

title: Mind-altering Awareness
text: This app has been a real boost for me. As a woman of 51 years, I have been dieting off and on since I was 12. You will notice from the tone of this review that I was reticent to lose weight, skeptical of counting calories after all my “successes” with fad diets, and largely selfish of my own indulgences. Let’s begin.   Here are the exceptionalities of this app: 1. It’s fun. You can tilt your phone and the balls move around. It’s actually even a little fun when you go over your calories. The balls spill out around the outside of the circle to signify superfluous calories. Fun!  2. It’s easy to record. I got the annual subscription, so I can use the bar codes. For food without bar codes, you can scan the Nutrition Facts, though this functionality is only reliable for the calories and serving size.  3. You are in control. I took it slow and started out by telling the app I wanted to maintain my overweight body,just to get used to using the app and to feel some success. I did that for over a week. It sure felt great to be complimented on meeting my goal of maintenance!  4. Failure is not an option. (Or rather, it IS option. Is just not called “failure.”) You don’t have to give up when you go over your calories. You don’t have to stop using the app if you choose to have a cheat day. Overages are built-in to the process.  5. Fasting. For those of us who are competitive, compulsive and impulsive, the fasting feature is amazing. Every day you have the feeling of setting a streak or record of how long you’ve fasted. Allow the app to alert you on the Home Screen. Then, every time you pick up your phone, it will tell you: “you’ve been fasting for __:__:__.” Every second counts! So many times, I have been less than excited about maintaining my fast until I see that screen. It is motivating without demoralizing you for stopping. In fact, whenever you do stop, a “ta-da!” sound plays, like you’ve accomplished a great fast rather than failed to fast longer. Secondly, the app tells you which stage of fasting you are currently in and what the next stage will be if you make it. Detailed explanations of the benefits of each stage are listed. You can encourage yourself by reading all about the autophagy happening and such. Alternatively, you can choose not to fast at all.  Here’s where the app falls short:  1. It’s not always easy to find foods you eat all the time. The app should first prompt you for recent foods when they match your input. Saving to favorites isn’t easy and not necessary.  2. It’s impossible to say you’ve eaten more than 2 servings of something. This makes it difficult to log 3 slices of bread or a huge bowl of cherries. The default is to either log the serving size or 100 grams. That’s nonsensical. The serving size should be the default, but you should be able to log the number of grams if you like.  3. The scanner for nutrition facts is awesome but needs to be improved.  Overall, I strongly recommend this app, especially to those of us who are control freaks and want to lose weight but are skeptical of commitment. This app eschews pressure and guilt in favor of celebrating success.

gist: However, the onboarding experience was frustrating.
title: App is fine.
text: The app has a very visually appealing design, and I like the way it presents tracking and progress, it feels modern and motivating at first glance. However, the onboarding experience was frustrating. When signing up, the app repeatedly pushed a paid subscription and free trial. Even after pressing the “X,” I was met with prompts like “Not ready to commit?” followed by another discount offer, instead of being taken directly to the free version. It took several attempts just to access the free features, which was unnecessarily time-consuming and off-putting. Unfortunately, the food logging experience was also difficult. Searching for something simple like “sausage sandwich” returned hundreds of unrelated or overly specific entries, none of which matched a basic meal. Manual entry wasn’t much better, as it required knowing and inputting every ingredient and calorie individually. As someone who works part-time while studying at university, this isn’t practical or efficient to do at the end of a long day. Overall, while the app looks great and has potential, the aggressive paywall and cumbersome food tracking make it hard to recommend in its current state. I hope future updates focus on improving accessibility, search accuracy, and ease of use.

title: Excellente qualité et fiabilité
text: J’avais un peu hésité au départ à m’abonner, mais je dois dire que je ne le regrette absolument pas.  Par rapport à la version de base, l’abonnement apporte un grand confort supplémentaire :  - la possibilité de classer ses aliments selon les repas de la journée en créant ses propres catégories donne une grande clarté, et permet de s’y retrouver beaucoup plus facilement. - les très nombreux graphiques disponibles avec l’abonnement permettent immédiatement de repérer les tendances pour les corriger : trop de sodium, de graisse saturées, pas assez  d’omégas trois… il devient alors possible de repérer visuellement les effets d’un aliment sur un nutriment (comment une sauce soja peut faire exploser le sodium par exemple). - le support e-mail est très appréciable : le service clientèle est très réactif, très performant dans ses explications, et permet d’exploiter pleinement toutes les possibilités de l’application. - la base Oracle, surtout dans sa version Web, apporte aussi une aide précieuse pour trouver les aliments les plus riches en un nutriment donné. Beaucoup d’applications se centrent sur les calories et les réseaux sociaux avec des données parfois sommaire et pas toujours très fiables, le grand avantage de chronomètre est de se centrer sur la qualité des informations et de la présentation sans fioritures inutiles. Que du bonheur…

Overall, I’m very disappointed. gist: I always ended up back with MyFitnessPal, but kind of hated it.
title: Can’t believe how good this is
text: Just wow.  I’m a long time food and activity tracker, and have used most of them.  I always ended up back with MyFitnessPal, but kind of hated it. It was definitely quick since I’d had it for years, and over that time inserted lots of recipes, etc.  But still, I was always disappointed when it came to the accuracy of the data and the nutrition information. MyFitnessPal is one of the best, to be sure, but focuses heavily on calories. Cronometer does all that, easily as well as MFP, but the level of detail, analysis and support when it comes to actual nutrition is just the best, no question. I can’t even believe it.  I wasn’t going to write a review on this, I rarely review things, but when I came across the “Ask the Oracle” feature, I felt like these people have been so thoughtful with their app, that I immediately stopped using it, and came here to write the review.  While the app has many superb and distinctive other features, the Ask the Oracle feature lets me immediately ask what kind of foods might help me increase a mineral or vitamin, etc,  so let’s say I see that my vitamin K levels are low (easily spotted by the app), I go to the Oracle and select vitamin K, and it pops up (a) the daily target, (b) a list of ranked foods with their Vitamin K values per 100g, (c) the caloric value of that amount. It’s pretty incredible, really. And while all of this is available via some googling action, I don’t know where you could get both an analysis of your diet’s deficiencies along with a very slick way to address that.  There’s tons more I’d like to write about, but as noted, I rarely write review and this is enough. Suffice it to say, you’d be doing very well if you want a real diet tracker for real health, that’s very easy to use, and you choose this one.

text: Was looking for an app that enabled me to lose weight and also track nutrients. This app has done both and I am very satisfied with it. After a week to adjust to eating more protein and fats and less carbs I have been steadily losing weight since and the nutrient tracking has proved a useful tool as a vegan.  I’m “thrifty” (ok tight) and wasn’t willing to pay for an app, so after several false starts I came across chronometer. It is easy to use and has many UK barcodes in for quick scanning. May consider a yearly subscription for a few of the extra features, but it’s working so well at the moment I don’t actually need to.  Downside is the lack of micro/macro nutrient information when scanning barcodes, such as my daily protein powder, despite being in the database does not appear to be providing me with any amino acids and is only counted towards my overall daily  protein measure.  Generic foods from the database do give these details, but adding my more bespoke foods and the ease of scanning the barcode is the trade off, and I can live with that. Great you tube tutorials and the forum boards are a good source of know how. The ability to copy from other days is useful as I have the same breakfast everyday and batch cook.  Overall I am very satisfied with this app and would recommend to anyone who wants a comprehensive free app to help lose weight (maybe gain...personally never had that problem!) without too much faff in recording. It has helped me adjust my eating and honestly I am enjoying using this app and the journey to a healthier weight. 😁

gist: It makes you want to use it hourly.
title: Professional Quality
text: Tried all similar “top rated” apps (11 of them) in the “Health and Wellness” category. This is the one that beats all others in ease, simplicity, professional grade, and best live and written support. It makes you want to use it hourly. This app is accessible to anyone, but it can be really leveraged by those serious about their health,those who are curious, committed, and creative.  Curious - the developer’s team of dietitians did the work, now you get to enjoy their professional knowledge. The other apps boast a “community” and they post their knowledge to each other. That’s an easy way of saying they’re avoiding the work to produce reliable content. How many strangers would you trust with your nutrition anyway? This app has professional dietitians who have input troves of data on every biomarker and relevant nutrition target.  Committed - when you commit to consistent input, the value increases. When you have the data, you can make the changes. This app makes it easy to monitor, compare, and correlate the changes you make and how this affect the body. Creative - you can input your own foods,even though whatever you can think of is one of the many databases this app taps,and you can make your own recipes. So instead of adding individual ingredients for a dish you eat all the time, you just call up your recipe and add it to your day. So fast and simple. The cool part is, as you get creative with your ingredients, you can see in real-time how those additions affect the balance of nutrients in the dish.

gist: But I wanted to better track my food intake, so I purchased a digital kitchen
title: Lets me enter a food’s weight!
text: I had been using a competing app since April 2016, and had managed to lose weight using it. But I wanted to better track my food intake, so I purchased a digital kitchen scale. That’s when I discovered that my old app frequently did not let me enter foods by weight, only by volume and/or number of servings. For a while I used my iPhone’s calculator app to convert the weight of what I was eating into a number of servings but that got old quickly. Cronometer lets me enter the weight of everything that I eat. I don’t have to worry about how tightly I have packed a quarter cup of shredded cheese; my scale tells me exactly how many grams I have measured out and that is what I enter. Life is so much easier. There are few things that I miss in my old app. A daily irritant is the lack of integration with Siri shortcuts. Every morning I take a handful of vitamins and drink 28 ounces of black coffee. I put vitamins into a recipe, but it still takes five keystrokes to enter them. Shortcut integration would let me do this with one voice command.  Cronometer ‘s barcode recognition is steadily improving. And while I appreciate the availability of micronutrient data, it’s not a feature that I’m currently using. The biggest issue is that the Cronometer app requires Internet access to open. I own cabin in a dead zone and Cronometer won’t let me enter any foods when I’m there. Instead I have to open Notes and write down what I ate, then re-enter it all later, usually after having to re-enter my app password. My previous app would let me keep my favorite foods on my phone and resync with the web site when service was again available. Despite that, it’s a good app that I continue to use, and despite the above caveats, would recommend to anybody.
Excellent app. Very easy to use, helped me blast through a weight loss plateau. Couldn't recommend more highly.

title: Best of its kind
text: I was a long time user of the (now very old and largely defunct) DietPower software. As the years rolled by, I tried most of the other online health and fitness apps, and none of them were a suitable replacement. They often had terrible food entry, were very noisy, and were often more focused on support groups than they were on the primary task of just logging food and exercise! After a decade of trying most of the other apps and being dissatisfied, Cronometer was worth the wait! The food logging is nearly perfect - the searches are fast and intuitive, and the barcode scanner is fantastic too. The ability to easily copy old records (even whole meals) to today’s food diary makes data entry lightning fast.  Exercise entry is simple and there are categories for nearly everything- and all are easy to find. The calculations for calories burned is straightforward, and the entries allow you to enter custom values if you track them in another app such as Runkeeper. Integration with devices looks excellent (though I’ve not used that feature yet). Best of all, the interface on both the app and the website is clean, uncluttered, and very intuitive.  I have nothing but gratitude to the folks at Cronometer for getting it so *right*! Strongly recommend!!

gist: I subscribed to Cronometer because I wanted to have only ONE app to log my
title: Fasting Section isn't Useful
text: I subscribed to Cronometer because I wanted to have only ONE app to log my food and log my fasts. However, I've opted to stop using the app because it didn't fulfill a need (which I could only discover by paying).  I've also opted not to get a refund, because I believe in the company and want it to succeed.  As an experienced intermittent faster, I have a schedule that I *try* to keep but can't always. Moreover, on most days I exceed my planned fasting time. This is where this app failed me: the fasting timer starts and stops as scheduled - regardless of whether I have started or finished a fast. If 2 o'clock rolls around, a message pops up telling me I've reached my goal and the timer stops. This is also the case at 6PM when I'm supposed to start my fast - the timer begins without me. If you're a distance runner, and your pedometer starts before you hit the pavement, or stops timing when you reach the 5K mark even though you continue on another 2k-3k, it's a pointless app.  A vastly more useful design would be: - notification to start or stop my fast - MANUAL start and stop of fast - ability to edit start and stop times easily (after a fast) - fasting history (maybe even paired with weight).  I've returned to my previous apps (one of which has an equally poor fasting section but already had my food log).  My suspicion is that food-log specific apps are trying to appeal to fasters like me, and are rolling out updates to their product before they're really of any use.  I'm out a chunk of money, but hope my contribution leads to a better UXD.

text: 6/25- The issues have been fixed! I’m really happy to be able to use the app again. And more than that, it’s really great to see a responsive team that listens to new ideas and bugs and follows through. Thank you! I loved the app until the last couple of updates- it was the only app that really let me look at micronutrients, easily toggle off and on calorie counting while still tracking nutrient data, and gave me lots of trends and general data with a more accurate database. But the second to last update removed the ability to toggle calorie counting off and on by permanently adding calories to your macronutrients summary so you can’t track protein, carbs, and fat without seeing calories. That’s also the only place you can see a deficit if you have one set up now, as the general energy summary only shows overall calories now and is not intuitive at all. I did contact the team but received generic instructions for turning off calories that are no longer accurate since the update. I emailed back but haven’t had a response since. Unfortunately I think it’s time to find a new app to use and recommend to people given it looks like these changes are here to stay.

gist: I have a very healthy mostly plant based diet, watch what I eat, exercise regularly
title: Absolute Best App!
text: So easy to take control of your health with this. I was diagnosed with serious B12 deficiency that did not show itself until painful symptoms in my hand/arm. Later tested deficient in VitD and Calcium that had affected my bone density already. I have a very healthy mostly plant based diet, watch what I eat, exercise regularly etc but those two experiences made me wonder - what other deficiencies could I have? and what if I  am more proactive to address it instead of waiting until my body starts failing me? Cronometer has been incredible in helping me look at my diet and filling those vitamin/ mineral deficiencies. Fast and easy to plug ur foods in - using ANY unit of measurement you could possibly want. Make your own “recipe” for really fast entry of something you eat routinely. I make food by “ handful of this pinch of that” and the flexibility of putting say .6 oz of on food .9 grams of another without having to convert yourself - LOVE that. Easily see where you are deficient over day or week and will tell you what foods to eat to make up gap. If I’m doing awesome on some of nutrients I can easily look up what foods are giving me that so I can make it habitual. Little aHA moments - rarely got enuf vitE then realized I never put my Yerba mate tea in each morning - boom, suddenly vitE right on track. Now I know my tea is an important part of meeting my nutrition needs, and if I do t drink it, I need to find an alternative source of E. This app is the most user friendly way to really examine the fuel you use, fix the problems before they manifest physically & avoid the health implications of just “hoping for the best” It has also allowed me to avoid having to rely on supplements of questionable quality or concentrations. Although in one case with protein, it became apparent I could just not eat enough food to meet needs so am supplementing at low level. The data source they use is great - used by several universities and researchinstitutions.  Ok! Rant over. Just thinking about long term quality of life, avoided health care costs over my lifetime. So much good could come from such a great app - so it’s worthy of a rant :)

text: The user experience could use a lot of love. Most of the settings are confusing to set up even when sitting with a nutrionist. The data is also really lacking. While it is great you collect so much micronutrients, if i just want to see my day’s total or week’s total (of macro and micros), it’s hard to find if it even exists. The ability to create my own charts is nice but hardly needed. I would have to create too many charts to get all the comparisons instead of being able to just look up the raw values. Setting up up the energy tracker is also severely confusing. The system forces you into a ridiculous deficit unless you set it to neutral. For example, I have been losing weight by eating 2000 calories. My goal consumed calories is 2000. But when I put in to lose 1 lb a week which is what I have been doing, the system wants me to eat 1500 calories. No, I want to eat 2000 calories not 1500. It also adds in activities weird. By using the activity level, it tries to add on the additional calories (2500 calories to eat vs 2000) you would burn so that you end up neutral for the day and not in a deficit. This is where I want to have a deficit. It’s like this application does everything backwards. I don’t want to be under eating and mal nourished. I want my activity to put me into a deficit as it should. Overall this app is at best a 3/5. The only upside is it shows significantly more indepth micro nutrition than most of the competitors but falls short everywhere else.

title: Cumbersome interface and lacking features
text: First impression was good, app looks nice and seems to offer a great deal of information. So initial impressions were good.  However, in the first minutes of using it I already came across a number of drawbacks. First of all, when registering on iPhone the app does not trigger the iCloud password service to suggest a secure password, which is basic functionality on an iPhone that should just work.  Then there's the food definition. To create a new food, I have to go through the barcode scan process and scan or enter a barcode label, a process which involves taking photos of the packaging (why?) and nutrition table which is cumbersome and adds little to no value (the OCR of nutrients doesn't work most of the time with non-standardised European food labels anyways, so manually entering is quicker than waiting for OCR to finish). There's a way to skip the scan but that's hidden in the My Foods section (the default is through the scan process). You can also only give a food a single name (there's no entry for brands like in other apps which makes managing similar foods from different brands a mess). And while it's nice to be able to create custom units and set a weight per unit, why can I only enter nutrients in either per unit (e.g. slice, portion), per gram or per oz (28g) when the standard for displaying nutrients is per 100g???  Once the food is in, it will have the same symbol (apple) as any other food, as there are no food-specific icons available as in other calorie counter apps (so you get fish or steak with an apple symbol, which looks silly and makes it impossible to quickly discern different foods in a list visually). Lastly, I noticed that the app is sometimes slow to display not just data but also UI elements as if this was a PWA, not a real app.  I was looking for something to replace another app I am using (which is Losing It by being killed by extreme ads and lack of improvements, despite me paying for it), but unfortunately Cronometer already failed at the basics the other app does right so for me it's not a good alternative. What a shame, as all these things are really basic and could probably be rectified easily.

gist: Finding my regular foods is so easy, e.g., cod liver oil only requires ‘cod’ and
title: Excellent nutrition website and app
text: Very well designed system for keeping track of nutrition status. Finding my regular foods is so easy, e.g., cod liver oil only requires ‘cod’ and it suggests it right away. I like the recipe feature. For instance, I have written a recipe for my homemade bread and fruit cake, which are stored on the app; then weigh each slice before I eat it and enter the amount. I often tweak and edit the recipe from week to week, which is no problem. The app even allows me to enter the cooked weight of the bread or cake. This is so useful as a lot of water is lost during the baking. Personally I only deal in the weighed quantity of foods….not in ‘servings’. I like it to be precise as possible. I have a small digital kitchen scale which makes that easy. However, you could use servings if preferred. As the day progresses I can check how many calories, fats, protein, carbohydrates and nutrients I’ve consumed. By the end of the day, I check if I’m short of any vitamins or minerals etc., which helps me adjust consumption of the necessary foods. My preference is to do a week or two of detailed food recording, weighing everything I eat. Then take a break from it, as it is time consuming. I only occasionally eat out and never buy ready-made meals, so I have a lot of control over what I eat. I’m very happy with the app.

The main issue I have with this app is sometimes it exports to apple health correctly and sometimes is doesn’t. I had day where I consumed just over 90g of protein. Looked in apple health and it said 5g. I then refreshed the day on cornometer and apple health updated. Not to the 90g I expected but to a new figure of 13g. I refreshed again. It changed again to 82g. Refreshed again, went back down to 5g. I’ve given up trying to get this app to export the correct data to apple health. I’d say the apple health data is accurate 60% of the time. Yes, I’ve tried deleting all data in apple health. Uninstalling the app, everything. Nothing works.

gist: best for deficits; imports active calories, input BMR
title: The best calorie counting app but not perfect
text: The bar is honestly so low when it comes to these apps. I will say that when it comes to tracking caloric deficits this is the best app. If you have an Apple Watch you can automatically import your active calories. Input your BMR into the app and your burnt calories are effortlessly tracked. This almost the sole reason I use this app. Other apps like MFP and LoseIt! would try to “guess” my calories burnt and then do a bunch math gymnastics to calculate a “calorie adjustment” from my workouts. It constantly was off by up to 500 calories. But this app still is lacking. The UI seems like it was made by freshmen software engineers. If you are in the middle of making a recipe and lose internet connection or leave the app for too long you can kiss your progress into that recipe goodbye. Want to separate your food diary into separate meals like every sane human on earth would want? Better pay up. It’s not even broken into time chunks it is literally just a compact list and if you add a lot of piecemeal items it can get long. And the home page might as well not exist. They don’t make the views simple and digestible. Maybe one day we will get a calorie counting app whose quality makes it easy to fork over cash but it seems like the strategy for now is to club you into submission with ads. Still bottom of the barrel. Just at the top of the bottom.

text: I used  MyFitnessPal (MFP) for a few years and got tired of all of the syncing issues and also the dizzying array of incorrect subscriber food entries which lead to tons of inaccurate and frustrating tracking. Yes, it’s visually appealing. But there’s truth to the old saying about dressing up a pig. It’s still a pig.  I researched, found, trialed, then switched to Cronometer and never looked back. Syncing across multiple devices is rock solid. The database is vetted. Also, Cronometer allows much more flexibility defining daily calorie goals which is so helpful when workouts dictate different daily needs. And when and if needed, their tech support is responsive and very helpful. Lastly, subscription costs are lower than MFP.  I’m never going back. Keep up the great work.

I decided to get a jumpstart on logging so that it would be a habit by the time the new year started.   Even though I didn’t win the competition, I’m happy to report that thus far I’ve lost 9.6 pounds.  It’s not a huge amount over two months, and I have quite a way until I reach my goal, but I’m quite happy, especially because I am now able to fit into clothes I haven’t worn in years. It already has a huge database of foods that you can choose from.  Also you can scan a barcode for the calories on prepackaged food which makes the lookup even quicker. I have added many more recipes, but those are also really quick to add because you just choose the ingredients from the list and it adds up the total calories for you.  I thought that I would maybe not be able to keep up the calorie counting long term but with this app I’ve been doing this absolutely everyday for more than 2 weeks and it hasn’t been a struggle at all.  It just takes a few seconds to enter something in as I eat.  It helps make me aware of how many calories I am consuming and when I should stop!  I have lost 4 pounds already.

So if you tried Cronometer before, give it another go because they’ve improved what was already a great app so much over the last two years.    One of the best new-ish features added is the ability to auto program repeat foods, vitamins, supplements etc that you eat or take daily. Huge time saver! No more need to copy from the prior day or week. You just hit a banner reminder on each day’s tracking and everything auto populates to the category/time etc that you set it for. text: I like to keep tabs on my food intake and what it’s providing me. Cronometer provides that but I find it difficult to use.  Specifically, the amounts of each food item are different than the amounts I’m actually eating. For example, for papaya one raw whole papaya is my only choice when I’m actually eating 1/2. Other foods give you options in grams. I have no idea how many grams 7 raspberries are.  As a result, while I am recording I know it’s not as accurate as it could be.  Cronometer could be a much more useful tool if it were simpler to use. It’s as if it has complicated itself by trying to be able to do too much. It’s intricacy is overwhelming and could easily lead any but the most computer interested to quit it entirely and that’s a shame.  Perhaps there could be two versions: one which allows food recording with more flexibility and calculation in terms of fat, carbs and protein and one with all the other information provided now.  Or, at a minimum, have a very detailed training video explaining all its components and providing examples of it being used and a very robust customer service element enabling users to quickly have their questions answered in real time by a real person. title: Accuracy is on point!
text: I love this app! It is simple to use, loaded with data points and most importantly accurate! Prior to trying Chronometer I was a user of MyFitnessPal since 2013, and a premium subscriber since inception. I grew frustrated with the app in 2015 after Under Armour’s acquisition brought on the premium subscription, particularly because there were several known bugs that were never addressed that affected premium subscribers. As more and more features moved behind the pay wall and prices kept increasing my frustration grew, and the tipping point for me was having to change my location to Canada to get marginally more accurate nutrition data from their database. With that, I decided to give Chronometer a shot about a year ago, and am very happy I did. The interface took some getting used to compared to MFP, but it’s not a very steep learning curve at all. The best thing about this app is definitely the accuracy in the nutrition data, especially when selecting “CRDB” as a source. I’ve yet to have to send a correction or input the food as my own after scanning a barcode. While I had a premium subscription for both services I actually scanned my Icon Meal barcodes (if you use Icon and MFP you know how often this data is wrong!) and I always found accurate micro and macro nutrient info in Chronometer when many times not even the right food would show up in MFP. I love the simplicity of the app, I feel like the developer isn’t trying to be ok or decent at EVERYTHING, but rather REALLY good at a couple, and I appreciate that. I have other apps I use for tracking and sourcing workout plans, tracking measurement progress, etc and I don’t need my nutrition tracker to do all of that - especially at the expense of continuing to be the best at their actual category. I hope that Chronometer continues to stay in their lane and does what they are doing, because they are the best at this point! My only VERY minor and extremely selfish complaint is that I wish it utilized family sharing so that I didn’t have to pay for 2 memberships a year for my spouse and I, but I also understand why they don’t.

title: The best one out there
text: I have used many of these apps in the past five years as a premium user (Loseit, Macrofactor, My Macros+, LifeSum, and MyNetDiary). Although each of these apps have several standout attributes, I have found that Cronometer is the best of the bunch when it comes to design, features, accuracy and overall user experience. I especially find the calories burned combo of BMR + Tracker (Apple Health) + TEF super useful - it’s opened up insights that other apps have failed to do by the transparency of the calculations in energy expenditure. Creating the custom graphs is also incredibly helpful; I created several (daily step count, resting heart rate and exercise minutes in Zones 1-5) that help me correlate my energy consumption (calories in) with my energy expenditure (calories out). Most of all, this app more than any other has influenced my behavior and habits which I am most grateful for. No app is perfect - and Cronometer has its drawbacks - but I have yet to find such all around all-star that compares with Cronometer. Definitely wins the Gold medal as of this review.

text: I use the fully free version, I’m a week in and this is how I feel so far!  For the juggling of daily life, it provides a comprehensive detailed nutrition list of everything in any dish from nearly any chain, in addition to anything to can buy at the store.  I’ve used for about a week now, after discovering my cholesterol was 300 🙈 and immediately had to do something before my meds could even get approved from my dr, I was going through the pantry and Reddit looking for help.  Reddit led me to this app, and I used it to record a salad burrito I got from salad n go from last weekend, and it popped up right away!  I was so happy everything I ate from home and out at chain restaurants was there!  I don’t spend much time anymore worrying and googling I just add it in-  I noticed after looking closely that there was no way the Thai wrap from salad & go was only 100cal that sounded so sus, so I researched it, and the chart they used for the information was from 2022, so I easily found the report item button, and they emailed the back the next day saying they used the 2024 information I sent them to update everything!  I was so impressed with the support to improve this app.  Additionally it’s super user friendly, if you accidentally add to lunch instead of dinner, you can just drag and drop.  You can add exercises(it’ll calculate the burnt cal in a tracking wheel), notes 📝(I use for my weight rn but I will use as a med journal for side effects too), and You can ⭐️food items that you regularly use and find them quickly.  I’ve lost 5 lbs in the last week.  I do fluctuate pretty regularly, but cutting most dairy, most preservatives and deli and red meat being able to track my cal intake and not mindlessly munch out of the kids snack hoard, I think is doing its work.  I’ll update later to see if I’ll be asked to pay, I imagine they have a cholesterol/fat tracker in premium I haven’t messed with it too much yet, being a busy professional single parent I’m just stoked I’m actively doing more than throwing meds at it.

title: Possibly the most accurate micro nutrient tracker and most customizable tracking app
text: I spent a long time last year trying various nutrition apps and was unable to find one that tracked micronutrients. The best I found had a great UI, but only offered a few micro options. One I was really interested in was added sugar specifically, which I could not find on any other app. They also mistakenly called them macros.  The few that did have micros, did not work with canadian barcodes. One has a nutrition label scanner instead that works well with canadian labels now (it used to get confused by the bilingual words). However, there is no per gram calculation, which means you have to calculate the portion you use as a fraction of the serving size based on the weight you used on your own, which gets messy. The database is also US based, so all of the foods are inaccurate for Canada.  On the other hand, Cronometers features are much better than any other app I’ve tried so far. The other apps may have improved since I last tried them, but I doubt they work as well.  I specifically love Cronometers extensive nutrient tracking options, accurate (country based???) incredibly easy to use food database, the ability to select multiple items, copy the previous day, and more. I also appreciate how they don’t include useless inaccurate features such as using the camera to “scan food”. The ability to edit the menu options, what is displayed on the summary screen, and the diary groups is also great. And the ability to drag and drop items between groups!!! The things I would improve would be: 1)making the menus more consistent between each other and more intuitive. It’s hard to find stuff. (Whats the difference between nutrient targets and macro targets???) 2)allowing us to edit a database item if some of the information is inaccurate. (Sometimes added sugars are only listed as sugars) 3)more widgets, such as one that only shows micronutrients 4)ability to show nutrient targets in terms of grams/grams instead of percent? 5) hide unused blank micronutrients fields for an item TLDR I finally found a good micro nutrient tracker with an accurate canadian food database and even more features than I hoped for and am finally motivated to start consistently tracking (since I’m mostly concerned about my vitamin deficiencies). I will definitely be getting premium soon.

title: Best tracker out there
text: This is the best calorie and nutrient tracker I’ve used and I’ve used several, including MyFitnessPal and Practice Better. Neither of these apps hold a candle to Cronometer. Being able to look at your micro nutrient intake is critical for several areas, which this app makes obvious by breaking it down into categories, like metabolic health, bone health, immune health etc. Additionally, when you look at your micro nutrient intake under your daily report, you can scroll all the way down and look at important nutrient ratios, like that of copper and zinc, for example. Personally, I didn’t realize I had an imbalance between these two micro nutrients which can cause a lot of problems, because zinc competes with the absorption of copper. So if you happen to be supplementing with zinc, you could be accidentally making yourself copper deficient, which can cause a whole host of issues. Thanks to this app, I was able to balance out my macro and micro nutrient intake. I’ve already been recommending it to friends and family!

title: Cronometer: Precision Nutrition Tracking with a Learning Curve
text: Cronometer is a data-lover’s dream, offering meticulous calorie and nutrient tracking powered by one of the most accurate food databases available. Its standout feature is granular micronutrient breakdowns (vitamins, minerals, amino acids), making it ideal for keto, vegan, or medically restricted diets. The barcode scanner, custom recipe builder, and integration with fitness trackers add versatility, while the free version is impressively robust. However, the app’s clinical interface and sheer depth of data can overwhelm casual users,expect a steep learning curve to navigate its charts and settings. Premium features like advanced reports and ad-free use are pricey, and manual entry for obscure foods remains tedious. While less flashy than MyFitnessPal, Cronometer is **the gold standard for detail-oriented trackers**, best suited for nutrition nerds or health pros who crave precision over simplicity.

text: Overall, I find this app very useful. There are a couple of quirks, but nothing is perfect. However, there is one glaring negative feature that, despite my effort to share with the dev team, persists. When you delete multiple items from your diary, a green banner pops up that has an “undo” button it. This is fine, except it completely obfuscates the “add new food” button. So, if you delete multiple items from your diary, you have to wait for each banner to pop up, remain for ~2sec, then leave. This banner applies for each individual item you remove. So, say you remove 10 items - you’re waiting 10-20 seconds before you’re even capable of adding a new item. Seems like a small bug, but compounded over days when you’re always modifying your diet, it leads to a tremendous amount of wasted time.  You can swipe down to remove the banner, but you must do this for each banner. So, for the previous example where we removed 10 items in a row, you have to swipe away the “undo” banner 10 separate times to minimize the wait period before you can add a new item.  Dev team - please work on this functionality.

text: I have been using this app since November of 2024, it is currently June of 2025 and I finally have the confidence to properly write a review! Now the part you all want to know, how successful is your weight loss journey?  As stated I have been using the app since November, but due to life circumstances I only started taking it seriously in January/February. However, since I started taking it seriously and following my goal I have lost 10 pounds! (11 depending on the day)  Which follows a healthy weight loss goal of 2-3lb a month.  So my friends, if you are looking to lose weight in a healthy way, or just looking for more information on your nutritional breakdown, this app is a great tool that I highly recommend.

gist: Full-screen ads and constant upselling, grind away at already-fragile motivation.
title: Crippling Ads and Punishing Premium Price , A Demotivating Experience
text: I’ve used Cronometer on and off for years, and while its tracking capabilities are excellent, the recent ramp-up in advertising crosses a line. It’s not just intrusive , it borders on bullying. Full-screen ads and constant upselling, grind away at already-fragile motivation. For anyone struggling with consistency, self-discipline, or health challenges, this feels less like a helpful tool and more like a punishment for not paying up. Yes, developers need to be paid , no argument there. But an app that exists to support long-term behaviour change must be accessible and usable in its free version. Right now, Cronometer’s free tier feels deliberately sabotaged to push users into a premium plan that is, frankly, overpriced. The result? Instead of supporting change, the app actively undermines it. Either make the free version genuinely functional and humane to use, or drop the premium price to something realistic. Otherwise, Cronometer risks becoming yet another wellness tool that only helps those who are already thriving , and alienates the people who need support the most.

Most reputable calorie tracker apps have a safeguard that won’t let you set your daily calories below 1,200 (the minimum recommended for adult women without medical supervision). This app allowed me to set a dangerously low target, which goes against established nutrition and health guidelines. When I contacted support, they simply told me how to change my goal, but did not address the underlying issue of user safety. Many users, especially those new to nutrition or at risk for disordered eating, could be seriously harmed by following such advice. Allowing calorie intake recommendations at this level is not only irresponsible, but it could also lead to liability issues for the developers. If you care about your health, or are concerned about apps with safeguards and ethical responsibility, I would recommend looking elsewhere until this is fixed.

title: Best Nutrition Tracking App Ever
text: I’ve been happily using Chronometer every single day for 10 months now. It is the easiest, most efficient, and most intuitive app of its kind and has AMAZING reporting/data analysis tools, even in the free version. Entering food is really quick, which is the single biggest contributor to me sticking with the app,I get frustrated fast when it takes a bunch of taps to enter every item. It has huge food database and it’s easy to add anything not in their database. I’m a scientist, so good data presentation and analysis tools are important to me. I love the flexibility of reports and graphs, being able to customize what metrics to view on and what timeframe, and easily change to see short and long term patterns. These tools are best-in-class, when other apps think showing you macro counts for the day is advanced analytics. The data tools have helped me spot dietary trends and view the effects of adjusting my habits, helping me make a measurable difference in multiple facets of my health. The paid version has some nice-to-have features and the subscription is more reasonable than competitors so I upgraded, but absolutely feel like I could have achieved the same usage consistency and health results with the free version.

title: Get rid of MFP
text: YO, listen up fellas , real talk from a 6’3” 225 lb lifter who logs every single bite: MyFitnessPal in 2025 is straight-up unusable. Open the app and you’re instantly hit with full-screen ads, pop-ups, and 30-second videos you can’t skip. Want to use the barcode scanner on the free version? Nope, locked behind a $20/month paywall now. The food database is still a complete mess; half the entries are random guesses from 2012. You’ll find ten different “chicken breast” options ranging from 60 g protein to 6 g protein. Trying to dial in a serious cut or bulk while ads for pizza chains keep flashing? Absolute chaos. I deleted it and never looked back. Cronometer is the absolute king. Zero ads. Seriously, none. The screen stays clean, no interruptions, no nonsense. Barcode scanner is 100% free and actually accurate; scan a steak or a tub of Greek yogurt and it pulls real lab-tested USDA data, not some random person’s guess. It tracks every micronutrient that actually matters: choline (huge for big egg days), real DHA/EPA numbers, selenium, molybdenum, copper/zinc balance, all the stuff that keeps you strong, lean, and feeling like a beast. The design is a little nerdy (kinda looks like a spreadsheet got jacked), but it’s lightning fast and doesn’t treat you like a walking wallet. Bottom line, brothers: If you’re still using MyFitnessPal in 2025, you’re basically guessing your nutrition while getting marketed to death. Make the switch to Cronometer. Thank me later when you’re 225 lb, shredded, and actually hitting every micronutrient without a single ad in sight. Cronometer = Top tier MyFitnessPal = Fallen soldier, let it rest in peace

title: Powerful nutrition tracking but limited localization and UC
text: Cronometri is a scientifically solid and accurate app, particularly strong in micronutrient tracking. From a data perspective, it is one of the best available. However, for non–English-speaking users, especially in Italy, the experience is unnecessarily demanding. The app is only available in English and requires constant translation of technical terminology. In addition, the Italian food database is very limited, forcing users to manually create and enter most foods and beverages to maintain accurate tracking. While effectively contributing to building the database for a new market, users are still exposed to advertising, which feels unbalanced. Some form of recognition or incentive for early users in underrepresented regions would improve fairness and engagement. From a usability standpoint, the interface feels rigid and less intuitive than competing apps, and the overall experience could be more fluid and empathetic. A clear weekly calorie deficit/surplus report,standard in many other apps,is also missing. Cronometer has excellent foundations, but stronger localization and UX improvements are needed to fully justify its potential.

HOT TIP: I always include the calorie count in my descriptions in parentheses and it turns out that’s been super useful for me. I also create lager portion versions for my husband when he asks for help and it lets me create special versions for him. Oh, and my macros? To my absolute SHOCK…I discovered that over time, simply by making small changes in my own time…I accidentally balanced my macros without even trying! Just by focusing in improving health choices, I added more veggies and such. I also love that it tracks the micros. I was interested in all the misc nutrients but didn’t consider how helpful it would be to also hone in on sugars and sodium. For me, Noom was super helpful and Cronometer was a great next step. I also love that it links to my Fitbit as well. Health and lifestyle changes truly take a lot of time and learning and fine tuning, plus we still evolve along the journey and I am glad to have an app like this to help. Sidenote: I tried myFitnessPal for a short time and never paid, so I really can’t compare much other than to say the free version was not my thing.

title: The only way to track food intake
text: I’ve tracked my food intake several times over the years and mostly I hated it. But it as I’ve hit a plateau on my weight loss goal (down 33 pounds, but wanting to get 5 more), I knew that careful tracking could help me reach my final goals. Thus I decided to try this app I’d heard about: Cronometer. I’d used MyFitnessPal before, several times, but I hated it and never felt like it gave me deep insights. But from the moment I started using Cronometer I really appreciated the way the app was designed. It’s super easy to log foods, it integrates with my Apple Watch data, so all my exercise calories burned get accounted for, and it’s easy to create both recipes and meals. The reporting,both daily and 7-day averages,is terrific, providing deep insights into macros and vitamin intake and allowing me to take action on what I consider to be excessive levels of sodium. It just feels like this is an app designed by people who really want to draw maximum value out of understanding their food intake. I can’t believe I’m saying it, but I just honestly enjoy tracking my food intake in ways I never thought I would.

title: Free version review
text: I’m only using the free version at the moment, but so far I’m very happy with this calorie tracker and food diary. I use the dark theme and the app just looks great. The ads are a little annoying, for a while they were just still frames like pop ups and that was way less jarring to the intrusive videos they have now. The app is itself is pretty good. The nutritional breakdowns are visually interesting. The borderline excessive use of the charts and graphs is engaging. The colors are wonderful. Watching your % recommend daily intake on all the various nutrients vitamins and minerals for each day across your weekly report is genuinely fascinating and you can see very plainly where your diet is adequate or deficient. As I add foods a pie chart fills in showing my macros and how many calories I have left based on my goals and my target deficit. The weekly report is a really nice touch. Consistency is key. It’s just another tool to help keep me on track. Having to fill in every meal keeps me mindful of my food choices. I would pay for an add free version of the basic diary if that were an option. I’m not of fan of subscriptions. There are a few similar apps in this space, but I’m pretty happy with this one. I may check out their competition. I would definitely recommend Cronometer to anyone counting calories or anyone who just wants to take a closer look at their diet. Check it out.

title: Endlich eine Food-App, die im Alltag funktioniert!
text: Nach langer Suche durch gefühlt das halbe Food-Tracking-Universum bin ich schliesslich bei Cronometer gelandet und zum ersten Mal habe ich das Gefühl, dass Ernährungstracking im Alltag tatsächlich sinnvoll und angenehm funktionieren kann. Die App wirkt sehr durchdacht, übersichtlich und erstaunlich präzise. Lebensmittel werden zuverlässig erkannt, selbst einfache Kombinationen wie Müesli mit griechischem Joghurt wurden sofort korrekt gefunden. Genau das erwarte ich heute von einer modernen App. Besonders positiv: Cronometer versucht nicht krampfhaft, ein überladenes Lifestyle- oder Social-Media-Produkt zu sein. Die App konzentriert sich auf das Wesentliche: * Ernährung * Übersicht * verständliche Daten * saubere Integration Die Verbindung mit Garmin funktioniert für meinen Zweck ideal. Garmin liefert Aktivitäts-, Trainings- und Gesundheitsdaten, während Cronometer die Ernährung sinnvoll ergänzt. Genau diese Rollenverteilung ergibt für mich endlich Sinn. Im Gegensatz zu vielen anderen Apps wirkt Cronometer angenehm ruhig, logisch aufgebaut und wissenschaftlich seriös, ohne kompliziert zu werden. Man kann präzise arbeiten, muss aber nicht alles obsessiv tracken. Für mich aktuell klar die beste Food-Tracking-App.

title: Gute App, aber das reine Abo-Modell ist enttäuschend und sollte dringend überdacht werden
text: Ich bin ehrlich gesagt sehr enttäuscht. Die App selbst macht einen guten Eindruck und bietet viele interessante Funktionen. Genau deshalb wäre ich sogar bereit, Geld dafür zu bezahlen. Was mich jedoch davon abhält, ist das inzwischen leider überall verbreitete Prinzip, alles nur noch als Abonnement anzubieten. Warum gibt es keine Möglichkeit für einen dauerhaften Einmalkauf? Nicht jeder möchte für jede App ein weiteres laufendes Abo abschließen. Streamingdienst hier, Cloudspeicher dort, Softwareabo da – irgendwann summieren sich diese monatlichen Kosten. Viele Nutzer möchten eine App einfach kaufen, besitzen und nutzen. Ich gehöre definitiv dazu. Besonders schade finde ich, dass man als Kunde gar keine Wahl hat. Wer die Premiumfunktionen nutzen möchte, muss zwangsläufig ein Abonnement abschließen. Ein fairer Einmalkauf, beispielsweise für 50 €, 80 € oder sogar 100 €, wäre für mich wesentlich attraktiver. Ich würde sofort kaufen. Stattdessen bleibt nur die Option, die App dauerhaft zu mieten. Mir ist bewusst, dass die Entwicklung und Pflege einer App Geld kostet. Deshalb habe ich überhaupt kein Problem damit, für gute Software zu bezahlen. Aber ich möchte selbst entscheiden können, ob ich ein Abo oder einen Einmalkauf bevorzuge. Viele Nutzer würden vermutlich ähnlich denken. Deshalb meine ausdrückliche Bitte an die Entwickler: Führt zusätzlich zum Abo-Modell eine lebenslange Lizenz oder eine Einmalkauf-Option ein. Niemand verlangt die Abschaffung des Abonnements. Lasst den Kunden einfach die Wahl. Wer ein Abo möchte, kann eines abschließen. Wer lieber einmal bezahlt, sollte diese Möglichkeit ebenfalls erhalten. Solange es ausschließlich Abonnements gibt, werde ich die Premiumversion leider nicht kaufen, obwohl mir die App grundsätzlich gefällt. Sollte zukünftig eine faire Einmalkauf-Option eingeführt werden, würde ich meine Bewertung sofort überdenken und vermutlich auch die Premiumversion erwerben. Antwort: Vielen Dank für die Antwort. Ehrlich gesagt überzeugt mich die Begründung nicht. Fast jede App verursacht laufende Kosten. Trotzdem bieten viele Entwickler neben einem Abo auch eine Lifetime Lizenz oder einen Einmalkauf an. Genau das wurde bei Ihnen früher sogar angeboten. Die Entscheidung, diese Option zu entfernen, wirkt aus Kundensicht daher weniger wie eine technische Notwendigkeit und mehr wie eine Strategie, Nutzer dauerhaft an ein Abo zu binden. Ich habe grundsätzlich kein Problem, für gute Software zu bezahlen. Im Gegenteil. Ich hätte ohne Zögern 50 €, 80 € oder sogar 100 € für eine dauerhafte Lizenz bezahlt. text: **Français** Quelques points qui m'empêchent de migrer définitivement depuis MyFitnessPal : Trop de publicités vidéo en plein écran, ça casse complètement l'expérience. Une bannière fixe serait largement préférable, au moins elle n'interrompt rien. Incohérence sérieuse avec la synchro Apple Health : quand on crée un repas puis qu'on l'ajoute au journal, les aliments sont ajoutés individuellement ET la somme du repas est ajoutée en plus. Résultat : un double comptage des macros et micronutriments. Une fonctionnalité simple à coder mais absente : les aliments fréquents devraient être contextuels par groupe/repas, pas mélangés entre eux. Sur MyFitnessPal, les aliments qu'on utilise souvent pour le petit-déj remontent en premier dans le petit-déj, pas dans le dîner. Entre les pubs et ces soucis d'UX, MyFitnessPal reste pour l'instant la référence. Dommage, le potentiel est là. --- **English** A few things keeping me from fully switching over from MyFitnessPal: Too many full-screen video ads , it really kills the experience. A persistent banner would be far better since it doesn't interrupt anything. Serious inconsistency with Apple Health sync: when you create a meal and then add it to your diary, the individual foods get added AND the meal total gets added on top. That's a double count of macros and micronutrients. A simple feature that's missing: frequent foods should be contextual per meal/group, not shared across all of them. On MyFitnessPal, foods you often log for breakfast surface first under breakfast, not under dinner. Between the ads and these UX issues, MyFitnessPal is still the benchmark for now. Shame, since the potential is clearly there.

title: Can’t create a new food anymore on web version
text: I’ve been logging foods in Cronometer for almost 16 months, and a recent update introduced a frustrating issue on the web version. Previously, if I searched for a food that didn’t exist, I could immediately choose “Create New Food.” Now, the search always returns partial matches, even when the exact food doesn’t exist, so the option to create a new food never appears unless I type random gibberish. The developer suggested creating foods through Foods → Custom Foods → Create Food, but that doesn’t solve the problem. gist: To me, this should be an absolute necessity.
title: Great for macro tracking
text: First and foremost, this is an amazing nutrition app. The library of foods, structure, UI, and settings are generally user friendly. I’d use Cronometer over an app like MyFitnessPal any day. The reason its 4 stars instead of 5: There is no offline mode! To me, this should be an absolute necessity. I understand that it needs to sync your data to the cloud and what not, but there should more than definitely be a way to opt in to a local storage mode for temporary use. I have run into a few situations where this is very annoying. I recently got back from a 4 day camping trip (ZERO internet connection). As someone who tracks my macros for lifting, cutting weight/bulking, and spending a whole weekend hiking, I was very annoyed to find out that I could not track any of my meals. Even in areas of low signal, the app still does not let me access my day to track macros. I think most people that are in the same boat as me would agree. (Note to dev: if there is a reason for this, i’d love to learn why :) ) I hope they implement a feature for offline tracking, in my opinion, that would make this app the gold standard of calorie tracking/nutritional apps on the market.

title: I like this app - it’s been helpful for my health goals.
text: Real person review here. I’ve been using this app on and off for the past couple years, and it’s been my favorite nutrition/calorie counter so far. I like the different options of logging in food, especially the barcode scanner. I don’t use the premium version, so I can’t comment on the features it provides. However, using the free version I’ve been more than satisfied. I don’t mind the occasional ads, because they’re super quick and they keep things like that barcode scanner free. (Which I’ve seen other apps put behind their paid version, and why I don’t use them.)  In addition, this app has a huge database of food for information (uses multiple sources, which you can toggle if needed), so it’s a rare event when I have to personally login a new food.  And a different feature I like is that I can set my goal weight, and see and choose from options that tell me how long until I can meet that goal.  It also shows me daily macronutrient goals (protein, net carbs, fat) for target weight as well as balance options. I can also see a further breakdown of my nutrient summary whenever I want to check in the daily report section, which is interesting.  The UI is pretty easy to navigate, though you need to take a little time to learn where you have to tap/swipe to find the more detailed info. But after using it for while, I can comfortably see/find the info and option these days with no issue.  Speaking of issues, I did have one earlier today where I was not being shown search results for manually looking up food to add (barcode option was working fine), but after a message to tech-support through their “contact us” in the app, I got a reply very quickly and the problem was resolved within a couple hours. And now everything is working again. The fast response and turn around is what’s prompted me to make this review after all this time.  All in all, I’ve been very satisfied with the app and how it’s been working so far, and I would recommend it to anybody who needs to keep track of their macros/nutrient intake.

title: David’s review
text: Cronometer has a lot to offer in theory, but logging food takes far longer than it should. The database is cluttered with overly specific entries, and the search isn't smart enough to cut through them. Basic foods are the biggest problem. Searching "strawberries," "apple," or "banana" doesn't bring up a simple result. Instead, I have to dig through entries like "fresh cut strawberries" or "raw banana, peeled." Preparation methods are just as frustrating: finding whether a potato is listed as fried, baked, or oven-roasted is surprisingly difficult. The search also has no tolerance for typos. In MyFitnessPal, if I accidentally type "chucken," chicken still comes up. In Cronometer, one wrong letter returns no results at all, so I have to retype the whole search, which is especially annoying with longer ones like "McDonald's chicken nuggets." My only other complaint is that setting the app to the Action Button requires Premium, which feels like a basic feature that shouldn't be behind a paywall. Outside of these issues the app is solid. A more flexible, forgiving search bar would make a huge difference.

Mais les remarques sont nombreuses :  - application Apple Watch qui ne fonctionne pas correctement : les données ne se rafraîchissent pas suffisamment souvent voir pas du tout pour les étages par exemple - Il n’y a pas assez de complications sur l’Apple Watch par exemple sur la grosse horloge digitale  - si vous mettez à jour certaines données de votre application santé, HealthView n’en tient pas compte : par exemple le sommeil si vous changez la source des données par exemple, HealthView n’en tient pas compte et garde celui chargé le matin de manière permanente. Vous n’avez donc les données à jour sur HealthView ! Il faudrait que l’application vérifie que des données antérieures à la dernière mise à jour n’ont pas été modifiées pour également les mettre à jour. - on aimerait sur l’iPhone au niveau des exercices plus de détails car l’application Activité  d’Apple est pauvre avec pourquoi pas : les zones de fréquences cardiaques, la fréquence Max ... et reprendre les données de l’application Activité mais de manière plus visuelle    - sur l’iPhone je ne vois pas la pertinence des indications « Moyenne horaire » « Min Max » qui sont pour la majorité des données inappropriées et sans aucun sens.  Sinon l’application est très visuelle et très claire on voit facilement ses objectifs et les données pouvant être affichées sont multiples.  Dommage qu’ils subsistent quelques buggs ! Et les améliorations sont nombreuses.

gist: better than Health and Activity apps
title: Great App!
text: I have read many positive reviews but also a few negative ones. But I decided to try the app for myself. And I have to say that I really love it! I have been very frustrated this past year with the standard Health and Activity apps built into iOS.  The data displayed (especially the Health App) is very difficult to read and manage. Although this app basically just copies over the same data, it displays it in a MUCH better way, with quite a bit of customization.  And now I can easily see everything I want with just a quick glance. (I love the ‘Goals’ layout with dark mode). The only thing that I can’t figure out is where it is getting the data for Resting Calories.  This is the one field that doesn’t ever match the data from the Health app.  (And I assumed this app was just copying over the same info).  It’s usually about 50 cal (or so) off each day.  It’s not that big of a deal and I’m guessing it’s somehow calculating differently, but I’m curious to know how. My only wish is that they can eventually make this as an iPad app as well, with all the same data. I hate that there are no apps to show health data on iPad, so this would be a dream come true!

gist: clear health app Apple could learn from
title: Hier kann Apple was lernen...
text: ... nämlich wie man eine smarte und übersichtliche Gesundheitsapp macht! Die HealthApp von Apple ist ein einziges ärgerliches Trauerspiel und unübersichtliches Desaster. HealthView dagegen bietet vielfache Möglichkeiten sich die gewünschten Daten auf dem iPhone und auf der Watch sehr übersichtlich mit diversen Auswertungsmöglichkeiten anzeigen zu lassen. Die Einstellung ist mit einem An-/Ausschalter ganz leicht und erfolgt für die Watch separat. So kann ich bestimmen, was ich wo sehen möchte. Auch kann man die Reihenfolge bestimmen und Zielwerte eingeben. Für die Watch gibt es verschiedene auswählbare Komplikationen für verschiedene Zifferblätter.  Die Synchronisation zwischen iPhone und Watch läuft bei mir einwandfrei und schnell.  Am schlimmsten an der HealthApp fand ich, dass man sich auf dem iPhone nur kompliziert über die Aktivitäts-App den Gesamtkalorienverbrauch pro Tag anzeigen lassen konnte und auf der Watch überhaupt nicht. Außerdem sind irgendwelche Verknüpfungen von Kalorienverbrauch und Nahrungsenergie auch nicht möglich. In der Health App werden nur die Ruhekalorien und die verbrannten Kalorien separat aufgeführt. Addieren darf man selber und wenn man Kalorien zählt, die Nahrungsernergie dann auch noch subtrahieren. Ein Unding für eine so teure Uhr!!!  Von HealthView ist das perfekt gelöst, endlich kann ich neben meinen anderen gewünschten Fitnessdaten alle Daten zu meinem Kalorienverbrauch und Defizit sowohl auf dem Telefon als auch auf der Watch auf einen Blick sehen. Allein schon dafür habe ich gerne 10,99 € einmalig ausgegeben!  Ich hatte zunächst die App nur geladen und ohne InAppKauf getestet. Man kann sich auf dem iPhone dann 3 Datensätze anzeigen lassen und die Einstellungen ausprobieren. Dadurch konnte ich feststellen, dass ich hier genau das gefunden habe, was ich brauche.  Vielen Dank für diese App, weiter so!

Me gustó la estética y la facilidad de visualizar los datos, aunque no en todos los casos los datos son reales, son medias. Dejando a parte el hecho del funcionamiento o la estética de la aplicación, mi enfado con el soporte es: desde que entro el concepto de la membresía o pagar cada mes, todos los desarrolladores se han vuelto codiciosos. Insisten, una y otra vez, en intentar que volvamos a pagar por aquello que ya compramos. Y, como no compramos, nos van recortando el acceso hasta asfixiarnos, es decir, hasta que por aburrimiento o vuelves a comprar la aplicación o, definitivamente la borras de tus dispositivos. Quiero pensar que hay otras formas de que la empresa que desarrolla software gane dinero y que a la vez mantenga éticamente sus compromisos. Es decir, podía haber creado nuevas condiciones para nuevos usuarios y haber mantenido las condiciones iniciales para los que compramos el producto. Quizá haber incrementado una pequeña suma por actualización para seguir dando soporte. Alternativas había y hay muchas. Pero en ningún caso el desarrollador las ha ofrecido. En definitiva, espero y deseo que me restablezcan el acceso total a la aplicación sin restinciones, pues así fue como compré la aplicación. Un saludo.

text: This free app is so good, I left a $1.99 tip. It links to your Apple Health data and keeps a record of steps over time and applies that to step goals you set for your fitness level. Positive feedback in “achievements” is given when step goals are hit  and the streak feature makes it fun to push for consistency.  Most people can achieve their desired fitness levels by a proper low sugar diet, spread out in much smaller portions, eating every two hours or so, along with 10,000 steps per day. Get in the habit of 4,000 steps before breakfast and change your life. This app is perfect to track it!

At first I would do a mile and celebrate now I’m averaging 2-4 miles 4+ times a week. This is major progress for me and I feel so good now. I highly recommend this app and please if you can donate to the developers because this app is worth way more that FREE.

text: I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes over 2 yeRs ago and was obese. I lost over 100 pounds and this is attributed to watching what I eat and walking a lot of steps. This app allowed me to track my progress very well to keep me motivated. My suggestions where it can improve though: 1. A calorie counter would be useful. Though calorie counters aren’t totally accurate, the ones on some gym equipment has it and it becomes a useful tool to track progress. 2. Daily goal reminders would be nice. 3. Pace tracker that tells you in real-time if you need to speed up a little. 4. An individual walk counter that can track all of the data for a particular walk. 5. Midnight override. I walk late at night and I want all of the steps from my walk to count in the day I started the walk in. Right now it switches to the next day and starts counting which ai don’t like.

title: Back-Pocket Motivator
text: It’s been two months since day one. I’ve lost five pounds WITH NO OTHER LIFE CHANGES except that I check the little green app on my phone several times a day. At a glance, the helpful visual somehow steers my brain to choose movement over stillness.  I started out with a low goal , 2,000 steps a day. And I didn’t reach it the first three days. Ouch.  But after the next six days of going over 2,000 steps, I increased my goal by 300 (the median of my overage).  Now I adjust my goal after every six-day consecutive success.  I’m up to 6,000 steps WITHOUT SIGNIFICANT EFFORT... that’s the important part. My brain is engaged with the app in an extremely motivating way.  I love the visuals. It’s really accurate (I’ve tested it a lot). And it’s not bloated with bells and whistles that get in my way.  Thank you to developers, not only for the app, but also for your tip jar, so that I could say “thanks” in a concrete way.

title: Watch gets frozen on 0 after midnight about 50% of the time.
text: Seriously loved this app for my watch at first. After transitioning from a Garmin with the step counter, it was just what I needed to complement the ActivityTracker. However, I keep weird hours, and I am also a run streaker, who often has to do my daily run right at midnight. It’s incredibly frustrating when my watch is frozen at zero day in and day out, and I have to reset it to her three times, and put it on the charger 2 or 3 times before it will finally start counting steps. The steps DO count on the app phone, even if my phone is still, so obviously the app on the watch is tracking the steps, but it will not show up on the watch, where I need it to show up. Currently, my watch shows me to be at less than 500 steps, but my phone shows that I’m closer to 3000. I was wearing the watch while I ran on my treadmill at midnight, but the phone was sitting still on the treadmill. That means that I’m still dependent on my phone to know how many steps I’ve taken, which is pointless. That’s a discrepancy that will not work for somebody who manages statistics the way I do. The entire reason that I have the watch is so that I don’t need to carry my phone. If this can be fixed, I will change my rating to 5- stars.

title: For everyone, especially seniors
text: I gave this app five stars because it and similar apps perform the critical function of keeping people aware of exercise to augment proper diet...both of which can and do contribute to good health and longer life!    In other words, you either move or die. I am forever grateful for learning this as a young physician. My preferred form of exercise was once long distance running. But because I developed the bad habit of doing only right PLFs (parachute landing falls), I ended up needing a right hip replacement. And on one of my early jumps, I cracked the end of my left femur; so, I am now on the mend from a knee replacement.    Now, a little over 2 months out, I am back up to walking 2-5 miles three or four times a week. There is still some minor pain, but every good PT or orthopedist will remind you “motion is lotion”! Even if walking isn’t your thing, get out there and just do something strenuous 3-4 x per week. Good Health to you all, Dr. Marshall Dressel, COL, USA (Retired)

title: Awesome., seamless integration...
text: ...of the steps taken all day long... App includes everything from the most “ho-hum” (boring) but necessary activities we all have to do... to intentional power walks taken twice a day. It truly is a free app and the advertisements are not obtrusive...  However, the app developer offers you the option of donating a tip of $1.99 to help with the support  and continuing improvement of the app.  ( I just happened to find this tip option when I was looking deeper into the settings of the app. This was a full week after I’d been using the app and greatly enjoying it’s  proficiency and seamless integration with Apple Watch (and of course iPhone) I felt the least I could do was give the developer a small tip for this excellent app. And I found the tip also removed the ads (which weren’t obnoxious nor obtrusive in any way) If developer should read this: Allow me to thank you for this app.  I was severely injured about a decade ago; I am left with many medical complications and must work very hard every day to do the things that I once took for granted.  Even with my diligence I slowly get worse as more organs of my body are involved.  The best I can hope for is by continuing to eat clean, taking all my meds on time every day five times a day and by staying in shape; My doctors hope this will slow down the inevitable progression of my overall medical condition. Despite everything my medical team has advised -> and which I comply with 100%  (to keep my illness at bay) I continue to get worse.. But this app is helping! after the first few days I could see & feel tangible improvements! I wish I found it sooner it really makes it so easy to record how much I move every day and that motivation is a wonderful boost for someone who very often feels helpless & hopeless. Sincere Thanks !!!
