title: Would be great if it worked properly.
text: This app gives you achievements for things like meeting your step goal a certain number of times, or taking a certain number of steps in a day. That’s great, and it really encourages me to walk, moreso than just checking the number of steps on the Apple Health app.  The problem is that it simply doesn’t work properly. Today I climbed a steep hill, and it granted me 0 flights of stairs. I climbed the same hill five minutes later, and this time it gave me four flights. I would have hit an achievement if it had registered the first trek up the hill, but it didn’t.  And then sometimes it just randomly deducts steps I’ve taken. It credits them to me initally (and matches up with the Health app, so it seems to be an accurate number), then suddenly jumps to a much lower number. When I just checked my step count on the lock screen widget, it showed me 7900 steps, which is over my personal goal, thus giving me a 9-day streak. When I entered the app proper, it cut me down to 6449 steps, significantly below my goal and decimating my streak (and the April achievement). This is the third time I’ve seen this happen, and quite frankly, it’s the last. This app does me no good if it doesn’t accurately (or at the very least, consistently) track my activity. I’ll be deleting it and looking into alternatives.

title: Disappearing Steps
text: Where do they go? Heavens knows! It’s clear that the developer has a keen artistic eye as Pedometer++ has the most aesthetically pleasing and easy to use UI than any other Pedometer App out there and I love and constantly use the widget functionality for quick measuring glances. I’ve had this app for nearly 3 years now and as a person who routinely reaches 10k+ steps from morning gym sessions alone, there is one glitch/flaw that has never ceased to plaque the apps flawless functionality from the get go: steps go missing out of no where or are flat out, not counted. Just in the passed 2 weeks, there are 4 days where the app has seemingly caused a significant number of my steps to vanish into thin air EVEN AFTER THEY WERE COUNTED IN THE APP; even verified by cross referencing to Apple’s Health app that will often show a higher number. Nearly 10k steps have seemingly bestowed upon me the absolute pleasure of ghosting my counter and this has been a consistent problem for the app since day 1. The only reason I don’t flat out delete the app out of frustration some days is simply because the UI is absolutely gorgeous and I don’t think any other apps on the market measure up to the beautifully simplistic design. Please do something about the consistent step counter glitch; it proves to be a demoralizing frustration more days than you would think

When you are trying to get in shape to go back country skiing , it’s no fun to get cheated out of the altitude you have tried to climb every day What made me aware of this was that Pedometer showed that I had climbed 12 floors x 10’ , which is 120 feet when I knew I had climbed 400’. That was the most extreme ever but made me pay attention When I climbed a 1400’ hill it only showed 100 floors and the next time I did the exact same hill, it only showed 84! I don’t know if anything can be done about this??? Also, if you don’t hang out on top for a few minutes , the app never catches up to where you really are You might adjust the floor height to be 12 or 15 ‘? I can keep track of reality vs pedometer heights and  You could extrapolate what the floor height should be... Today 18 floors for 638’ really?

gist: ex-Fitbit user finds it nearly perfect
title: Almost Perfect
text: I may be slightly tilted because I recently traded in my Fitbit for an Apple Watch, and though I loved my Fitbit (it helped me shed over 30lbs) I am learning to love my Apple Watch just the same. The adjustment was difficult because I was spoiled by the simple all in one (heart rate, diet, steps, sleep etc...) app, and I’ve been chasing something of the same caliber since.  I spent the first few weeks with my Apple Watch downloading and many times buying apps but 90% of them were too focused on tracking one thing or overly complicated and disappointed where it came to working with other apps.  Now I have it narrowed down to a handful that I use daily and Pedometer is one of two that I use for activity tracking. It works great with IOS Apple Health apps as well as nutrition and diet trackers. It also tracks my steps either through my phone or watch and then that data is compiled to give me the most accurate reading, and my favorite feature is that I Don’t have to start a “workout” to get it to collect data. It is always counting even if I’ve closed out of the app. It also has a great Goal/reward feature which I love.  The only area that I wish it would get better at is tracking elevations. I have found it difficult to get to the gym on a daily basis so many times I turn to the staircases at my work to get in some cardio. Usually I end my day by doing staircase laps for half an hour yet it doesn’t usually collect this information. There is even a double staircase that I climb in this routine so it’s not an elevation problem. For example I just finished my workout where I counted 45 staircase reps (15+ steps each rep) yet my app only collected 7.  However this is a little nit picky because the important data, like heart rate, time, distance and calories burned is all accurate so the workout value is the same but since I set my workout by laps instead of minutes I like to keep track.

title: Loving it and hating it
text: Love this app when it works, which seems utterly random. Sometimes it counts my steps, other times I can take hundreds of steps and the count stays the same. I have been up and down my 13-stair flight of steps at least 9 times today; it counts 1. Yesterday it was counting my flights just fine. I’ve been using this for less than a week. I love the overall interface and on the days it decides to work I love the motivation to be more active. When I look at the progress I made at the end of the day, I just feel so proud of myself! It gives me strength to look foreword to the next day to see if I can get more steps than I did the day before.  It’s a wonderful app especially for those that don’t have any one around to give them a pat on the back or encouraging words for a job well done! Thanks

title: Simple and easy to use
text: This is a basic Pedometer with a few incentive goals built in. As you walk, the number of steps are calculated in real time, as well as the estimated distance covered and number of ‘floors’. There is freedom to set your own target step count and a few other preference settings like Km/Miles and preferred colour-way. I would have liked to interact with the stats on the touchscreen to have a slightly more detailed breakdown of the data, and perhaps more explanation of some of the terms, for eg. what constitutes a ‘floor’ and how to achieve them. Overall, if you want a basic pedometer app this will certainly do the job, but if you want any detailed information or analysis of your data then there are better apps for that.

title: Ruhetage ausgleichen
text: Ich schlage eine Erweiterung bzgl. des „Ruhetages“ vor. Es sollte bzgl. „Ruhetage erlauben“ eine rechnerische Basiskalkulation eingeführt werden. Sollte ein „Ruhetag“ erfolgen, könnte man die Schritte des Ruhetages und die Schritte des Tages davor (Zielvorgabe erreicht) und des Tages danach (Zielvorgabe erreicht) addiert werden. Liegt der Mittelwert über der täglichen Zielvorgabe, wird der „Ruhetag“ nicht als solcher gesehen. Ansonsten wird der Tag als Unterbrechung gewertet. Dieses Vorgehen sollte nicht nur für einen „Ruhetag“ gelten sondern auch für mehr als einen. Wenn also z. B. 2 oder auch 3 „Ruhetage“ stattfinden, sollte alle „Ruhetage“ sowie das Ergebnis des Tages davor und des Tages danach addiert werden. Ist der Mittelwert höher als die Zielvorgabe, gilt das Ziel als durchgängig erreicht.

gist: Maybe it’s just me, maybe I’m just slow, maybe I need two years to figure
title: I Don’t Know Why
text: What are floors? So far after using them for well over a year I have no idea what they mean or how they are at all useful. I can go on a hike with a 4000 foot elevation gain and collect no more than 30 floors. Then I can go on a local hike near the house with relatively no elevation gain and get 60 floors. Maybe it’s just me, maybe I’m just slow, maybe I need two years to figure it out. I also have some special awards that I have absolutely no idea where they came from or how to achieve them. One appears to be for something that occurred two years ago on a weekend humm... no idea. That leaves daily steps, accumulated steps, weekend awards, and monthly challenges bundled around a daily confetti graphics for a job well done. I get a ton more useful information from the Health app that came with my iPhone but it doesn’t seem quite as personalized as Pedometer++ so I’m still using both for two alternative purposes.  BTW, we are soon going to be in to the second week of 2021 and there is no new monthly challenge for January. Maybe it’ll pop up with the next update.

title: I don’t know why...
text: ...but I love this app! It’s not really that integral with the advancements in iPhone, iOS, Apple Fitness and such but for some reason I just can’t bare to take it off my phone! As a matter of fact, after a few years of using this app, I realized I never put my tip in the tip jar! So I made sure to do that today! What does this app offer that others don’t? Well, you get a nicely programmed app that looks great and functions very well. You don’t have to pay to use it despite the fact that there aren’t ANY intrusive ads. The ads have never even bothered me but paying was for the principle of it. I appreciated more than anything, non-intrusive ads. Usually “free” apps make you pay by bombarding you with countless ads and pommeling you into either paying to remove them or deleting the app just to make it stop. Not this one. So thanks for that! Now onto the app itself: The interface is simple but informative using graphs and colors to show you where you’re at in reaching your daily goals. There are basic color presets to give you a little control over appearance. You can also select a style for the app logo! A nice touch. With its streak and badge-based award system, this app makes reaching your weekly, monthly and annual step goals fun! Over the past couple years I’ve taken my daily step count from 8-9k to 14-16k per day simply because this app made me more aware of it than Apple’s native step counting system. It just puts it out there for you. Apple Watch integration makes counting more accurate.  The new widgets put your steps front and center, helping you to track at a glance.  There’s not much I’d change with this app really. It does it’s job as a designated step counter very nicely. If I were to make a recommendation it would be maybe a side-by-side daily, weekly (last 7 day total), monthly (last 30 day total) and annual (last 365 day total) step counter (not just Weekly at the bottom or Lifetime in the Awards section.) Or maybe be selectable time frames to be able to see how many steps I took in April 2020 and compare it to April 2021 and see if I improved in a year (if the data is stored).  It’s been cool to watch this app grow over the years and I look forward to keeping it attached to my fitness goals for a long time. Cant wait to see where we go from here!

gist: Yesterday, after three miles on the treadmill, I expected to see approx 6300 steps, but
title: Not accurate-esp w/ longer distance
text: I’ve been using this app for about 85 days now. When I first started, I was walking short distances ( 1 to 1.5 miles at a time) and it seemed pretty accurate and matched up with my treadmill pretty well +/- .1 miles. Now that I’m up to longer distances, it’s wildly inaccurate. Yesterday, I did 6.5 miles on my treadmill alone, yet it gives my daily total as 6.2 miles. Already today, I did a 3 mile treadmill session yet it says I’ve done 2.8 miles total. And it’s not just the distance,it’s the steps. My standard, tested and counted mile is 2100 steps. Yesterday, after three miles on the treadmill, I expected to see approx 6300 steps, but it was at 4500. I get a more accurate reading if I pause the treadmill every mile and open the app, but that’s annoying. It also fails to clock some of my flights of stairs. I wear my phone in the same spot as I always have while walking around so I don’t understand why the sudden discrepancy. I suppose if you’re just using it to clock your daily steps at home / work / shopping, it’s pretty good, but it if you’re also running or walking for exercise, your step count will show up greatly under your actual total.

gist: My only complaint is that though the steps seem to reflect what I do each
title: Useful app
text: I’ve started walking every morning and this app on my phone has helped me get a general sense of my distance each day. My only complaint is that though the steps seem to reflect what I do each morning, the mileage is not accurate. I am less concerned with whether the miles are literal miles, but would at least like the miles to reflect the comparative distances from day to day. For instance I did the same route on Friday as I did on Monday - except Monday I added a few more blocks. Yet Friday shows 4.5 miles, and Monday shows 3.8 miles (even though I went farther on Monday), and yet the step count does show the greater distance on Monday. All I can figure is a snafu in the GPS. So I’ve learned to rely on the step count more than on the mileage.  In the big picture though it is a useful app and it was free. So it’s really hard to complain too much. It is simple to use and tells me how far I go each day (in steps). It has lots of other bells and whistles that I have not taken the time to figure out. But perhaps one of these days.

His Apple Watch recorded just over 5mi (he started with 0mi) but on my iPhone with this app, I had just over 4mi (I started with .2 mi that day). We’re on the exact same walk. I didn’t understand how I could have 20% less mileage. I later mapped our route and it was 5 miles. Today is the same thing, except we’re on a 4 mile route. This app on my iPhone said I’ve done 3.3 (I started with .3) but my husband’s Apple Watch had 4mi. So this time, I’ve got 25% less mileage, even more inaccurate. gist: A couple of years ago I was diagnosed with cardiac issues including the need for
title: An App that cheers me on!
text: I love the Pedometer App.  Let me explain why!  I enjoy walking. As a 76 year old male I aim to walk 4 miles each day - usually early morning before breakfast.   My daily target is at least  10,000 steps.  A couple of years ago I was diagnosed with cardiac issues including the need for a new aortic valve and a double heart bypass.  During the “waiting for cardiac surgery” I felt it was essential to keep fit and keep walking. I knew this would aid my recovery.  The daily monitoring of my walking with the Pedometer App was automatic.  I was able to easily adjust my target as my health deteriorated - I managed to keep on walking.  In March 2022 I had open heart surgery and have had a good recovery.  I’m back to walking four miles each morning and managing around 13 000 steps a day.   The Pedometer App has a brilliant display, it’s easy to read and there are lots of variations on the settings. I love the confetti shower that I get when I’ve achieved my target.   I highly recommend this user friendly app.  👏 Peter S Quigley

title: The best motivation for retaining a walking streak!
text: This app motivated me to start a walking streak! I’m a software developer and since COVID-19 I worked from home. I realized that I was doing around 1500 steps each day.  It was a thought process to make more steps. Buying an Apple Watch did help, but it did not force me to keep doing it for more than one week.  Having a one-week streak on this app gives that bit of motivation to keep walking. The badges will give you that little nudge to take that streak to the next level. I love that I can increase my goal and challenge myself.  My suggestions: I would love to scroll through my streak and remind myself why I had a bad day or why I walked 26380 steps. Maybe an easy note system? A second suggestion would be to have a clear way that shows if a rest day is allowed. I understand that the rules are easy. But occasionally, I have to count, and I start to question myself if it was a 5, 6 or 7 streak.  The third suggestion would be related to the second one. I would love to set the rest day rules. Every so often, a longer or smaller period would be easier. Possibly, a specific day would be great.  I understand that the rules should be clear and easy. But this freedom can help people who need that harder or easier treatment.

title: I Owe a lot to this App!!
text: I did not think this was possible. I had a stroke a few years back at a very young age and was too embarrassed for people to know I was physically challenged. It took me three years to learn to walk again in a way that didn’t look like I had a disability, but I was very slow. (I realize that the way I looked was the least of my problems but as a single mom with two teenaged children, they were more sensitive than I was). But, this App motivated me to walk whether I felt like it or not. Even though I hated walking for the first four months I did it. It was painful. At the fifth month mark, it started to feel good and even now some days I only take 200 steps and other days I take 3,000 steps. Point is, I am walking and I know I wouldn’t be without this App. Thank you.  Sincerely , Lyn Legge.

gist: It seems wrong, in principle and logic, to allow rest days and then not take
title: Algorithm not in good faith
text: It seems wrong, in principle and logic, to allow rest days and then not take the rest-day-unbroken streak into consideration in allocating badges. For example, I walked a thirty day streak for June, two legitimate rest days are in the mix. However for the monthly streak the app notates 30 days and yet I did not get the “Perfect Month” badge, which is what I was really aiming for. Why allow your users the option for rest days, indicate that it “will not break your streak” and then penalize your user for incorporating a rest day when allocating badges; that just seems contradictory and misleading. It’s the second time something like this has happened and the logic here is flawed - either you disallow rest days or you honor the fact that you said a break every six days will not affect your streak and stick to that across the app.

title: LOSING STEPS, INACCURATE STEP COUNT
text: I recently retired from a very sedentary job and wanted to increase my daily steps. I even bought an Apple watch so I would have the pedometer with me at all times, since I do not carry my phone every place I go, i.e., up and downs and to the bathroom. I set an initial low goal of 3000 steps, which I make sure to get every day (except Sundays), even going well over my set minimum on most days. August 1st I wanted to increase my goal to 3500 and when I went into the app via my phone to set my new goal, I noticed that the step chart showed quite a few days as showing orange, and sometimes even red, even though I had reached  my daily goal, showing green at the end of the day. I continued to use the app for the month of August with my new goal of 3500 daily steps, again reaching, and exceeding that goal every day. Today is September 1st, and I wanted to increase my goal to 4000 steps, so I opened the app on my iPhone and again it is showing incorrect data via the chart, especially yesterday, August 31st, I cleaned and walked twice and according to the app on my watch hit close to 6000 steps. So, why is it that the chart via my iPhone says I had 88 steps yesterday? Really?! How on EARTH  did I manage to lose almost 5000 steps? It also showed the two previous days as 1117 and 1420. I get that just in one walk with our dog in the morning, and, again, I was well over my goal, into the green, on those days and now the chart is showing red, less than half my actual steps! So will someone please explain how I am losing steps? It's definitely time to get a new app for steps.

title: Not for international travelers
text: I have used this app for at least four years. It pains me not to give a five star rating because normally it is excellent. It keeps track of how many days in a row you reach your goal, but for anyone that travels internationally that is where the problem is. When you change countries and change time zones, your entire history gets shifted to the new time zone! I have over 1,000 days in a row of exceeding my goals. Recently I went to Japan from my home in Europe. And when I changed to the Japanese time zone, it dropped to less than 100! it changed my entire history to the Japanese time zone, which made absolutely no sense at all. Apple fitness freezes the past instead of dynamically updating it, which makes perfect sense. Why this app does not do the same mystifies me. If you don’t travel internationally, it’s a great app. If you do travel internationally, don’t waste your time on it.

gist: Since this app fails at its primary purpose, I cannot personally recommend Pedometer++.
title: Extremely inaccurate data
text: I’ve had Pedometer++ on my iPhone for over 30 months now(on 3 different iPhones and 2 Apple Watches), and it’s typically off by thousands of steps each day vs. Apple’s Activity app. I wear my Apple Watch for the entirety of each day, so the Activity app represents the most accurate assessment of my activity for the day.  Pedometer++ typically shows 2x the steps that I’ve actually taken. Since this app fails at its primary purpose, I cannot personally recommend Pedometer++. I’m currently using said app on an iPhone XS Max and Series 4 Apple Watch. If a future update begins counting my steps accurately, I’ll promptly update me review. Update: I decided to give this app another look to see if the accuracy has improved. In 2026, it’s still wildly inaccurate by thousands of steps each day. For example, per my Apple Watch - which is the gold standard for accuracy - I’ve been averaging just over 14,000 steps a day in May. Pedometer++ has me at 17,000-19,000 on days I actually walk 14,000. How can you develop an app for so many years and never improve the accuracy? You’re much better off using data from your Apple Watch.

title: Feature request: iPad companion app / large-screen dashboard
text: Hello Pedometer++ team, I really enjoy using Pedometer++. It is simple, clear, and very motivating for following my daily steps and progress. I use it with my iPhone and Apple Watch, and it has become part of my daily routine. I would love to see an iPad-compatible version, or even a companion dashboard for iPad. gist: Good app, surprisingly accurate with beauty in simplicity that does not sap battery power like
title: Good, practical.
text: Good app, surprisingly accurate with beauty in simplicity that does not sap battery power like similar GPS based apps.  In its simplicity it does not have the "neat" mapping and graphs capability but in practice, having no Start/End button makes this practical. Apps that utilize the GPS will always have start/stop button to where you will eventually forget to start for no credit, or worst, forget to stop it to sap up your battery reserves. Honestly, walking is an anytime, anywhere activity, it should be recorded all day and why map it? This app simply capitalizes on the built-in iPhone accelerometer and the health app included in the IOS. It simply counts motions that mimics a step. At midnight it stores your days result then restarts at zero for the next day. If it's worth supporting the developer and getting calories then $1.99 seems worth it.  It might count a non-step if your carrying the phone in your hand and perhaps by "flicking your hair" as others have commented. For best results keep the phone in your pocket as much as practically possible. This may not work so well if you keep your iPhone in a purse, just as the Fitbit was designed to be on your wrist. I find it plenty accurate. A GPS based app will likely give you more erroneous results. Turn on your favorite mapping app (or GPS based walk app) and lay it on your desk for a few hours. Through atmospheric conditions your phone will wander around a radius giving credit for walking just laying there.

gist: A couple of times I found that the app just stopped counting my steps at
title: Spotty
text: A couple of times I found that the app just stopped counting my steps at less than 20% of my total steps during a ‘Workout’. The other thing is, if you forget to hit ‘Finish’, merely pausing it won’t stop the time from accumulating so, even though you finished all of your walk for example in a planned “workout“, it won’t credit you the steps for the day you walked if you forgot to end that particular workout. Then, those step show up on the chart for the next day, but are not counted towards the next day’s steps either. So you don’t get credit for those steps, because they were really part of a work out that you did the day before, but it bled over into the next day because you forgot to turn hit ‘Finish’ that particular work out. Now, there are 2500 steps or so in this particular work out I’m talking about that are showing up for the following day because it was after midnight before I terminated the work out or ‘finished’ the work out, but they’re not showing up on the steps total for the next day, either. title: Wonderful Easy-to-Use App!
text: Yesterday evening I downloaded three different pedometers from the App Store for comparison with the built-in “Health” app: Steps, Pacer and Stepz. I have never used a pedometer before now. Then I went outside and did my stairs exercise in order to acquire my first set of data so as to compare the different apps. I must say that I like this app , Steps , the most! It is simple and straight forward, and it has just the data that I need , steps, miles, time and flights , without all of the extra data clutter that some of the other apps have. I also like the ease with which I can scroll left or right to see my walking history, or else tap on one of the seven day buttons, or else tap on a calendar button. The graphic interface is very clean and uncluttered, and the themes are pretty and easy on the eyes. While I paid the very reasonable and low price for the “Pro” version in order to get more themes to choose from, I must say that I like the default “Sunrise” theme the most. 😀 Let me also add that the steps count with this particular app is very close to the actual steps I physically counted as I did my stairs exercise. I carried my iPhone in my front shorts pocket as I exercised, and I walked on flat pavement in the parking lot, as well as up and down two flights of stairs. The fact that this app integrates with the “Health” app , and imports health data from the same , is an added plus. For the aforementioned reasons, I give the “Steps” app five stars! I encourage everyone to give it a try! 😀

text: This is a good little app, but for a couple of small niggles. Firstly, I love the fact that I can add friends and we can share our progress for. There are currently six of us doing a UK challenge because we all have quite sedentary jobs. We want to move more. It's also good that I can see my walk history. However, there are a couple of little issues that I really wish could be sorted out. The first one is that my watch does not seem to update until I have opened the StepsApp on my phone. I feel like if my health app can do this, why not my steps up. Secondly, if I go into the app itself on my watch, the number of steps there are five pages in it seems, and they do not agree with the complication on the front of my watch which is, for the most part, up-to-date. If these issues could be fixed, that would be great. VoiceOver seems to indicate that the number of steps is on the first page of the actual watch app itself, but it doesn't read this figure out to me, so either it's not there, or VoiceOver is unable to read it. If you could put this figure on the front page as well, or make it Read, that would resolve all my issues. If I had to have a wish list, I would also love the ability to be able to take part in walking challenges like you can on other fitness apps where you can use Maps. You can walk from the Shire to Modo for example on one of these apps. Being blind, we don't get to take advantage of this in normal apps, but I wonder how difficult it would be to add a soundtrack? Anyway, just my amusing. The app is good at what it does, it would just be nice to have that extra dimension.

The red flag is, I know I walk a lot more, move a lot more and do a lot more than the people under me, I am their “boss” and I set an example. So I purchased a belt clip step counter, and also purchased a wrist strap health tracker ( I won’t mention the name, I’m not a paid advertiser) and the iPhone steps app was insanely low. The belt clip steps app was way over double what the app counted and the wrist strap health tracker was around, or a little under half of what the app said. This can’t be a coincidence. I started to make sure I had my phone in my pocket for the last month to make sure it was “counting” my steps. gist: The Google Fit app went from being one of my favourites, for ages, to now
text: Form over function ruined a great app.  The Google Fit app went from being one of my favourites, for ages, to now being almost useless.  If you simply want to track basic metrics such as steps taken and distance walked/cycled per day/activity, along with a GPS based map of the route traveled, do not use Google Fit.  Some details are in the Journal, but they are buried instead of right there in your main view.  The interface looks pretty; but the gamification is complete and utter nonsense, merely dumbing down the app to the lowest common denominator.  Want to count daily steps?  Nope!  Congratulations on some completely meaningless "Heart Points", though!  Want to see a map of your route? Sure, but points along the route can be off by a kilometer, or more, a level of accuracy that's good enough for some I guess.  How about that 10km bike ride home, where you stopped at the grocery store en route?  Well, you were /clearly/ walking, despite large sections of the route being at 25-30km/h, a new World Record!  //facepalm//  Please, add back the basic features of the old Google Fit app, or simply release a Google Fit Classic, for those of us who have no need for these recent changes.

gist: And considering it is free, you really can't beat it.

After reconsidering overnight and thinking about what I want from this app I think it was unreasonable to change my review to a lower score. gist: You can't now click on heart rate or pace and get a full view of
text: Whilst the new Fit looks pretty and has a nice new layout it's taken several steps backwards in usability. You can't look up an exercise that you just did to see how far you ran or how many calories your burned etc. If you miss the info when you finish your exercise, say the distance you just ran, that's it until you open your phone.  Add to the above that for the third time since using Fit that it's not accurately sending the data back from my watch to my account. The phone shows 0km run. Open the activity on the watch. 6.79. Die Kilometer zwischen Uhr und Handy sind immer unterschiedlich, die Streckenerfassung ist offenbar rein Zufallsbestimmt und hat wenig mit der tatsächlich gelaufenen Strecke zu tun. EIGENTLICH finde ich diese "Fitness-Motivations-Geschichte" witzig und prima, ich FÜHLE mich motiviert. Aber dieser komplette Datenquark, der hier verzapft wird, wo NICHTS übereinstimmt und Werte zufällig hoch- und runtergehen, man überhaupt keinen Überblick darüber hat, was eigentlich gemessen wird - das ist leider "Big Data in Reinkultur": Keiner weiß, wozu die Daten zu gebrauchen sind, alle stöbern nur wahllos darin rum. Daher: Meine Hunde motivieren mich besser. Da sehe ich wenigstens den Erfolg. --------- NACHTRAG: Feedback über die App zu senden ist sinnlos, es gibt keine Antwort (hab's x-mal versucht). Anscheinend sind die Probleme seit über einem Jahr bekannt (viele Google-Treffer dazu), das ganze WearOS und die GoogleFit-App sind wohl eher Aprilscherze und gar nicht darauf ausgelegt "zu funktionieren". Google-Mitarbeiter schreiben immer nur "sende uns Feedback", das ändert aber nichts an der Nicht-Funktion.

gist: invents steps and calories; cannot control sync
text: Holt nicht die Daten aus dem verbundenen App. Schreibt mir Schritte und verbrannte Kalorien aus dem "Kopf" zu, jede Minute was anderes, auch wenn ich in dem Moment im Bett liege und mich nicht bewege. Verwaltung der App ist Schrott! Man kann die Sinchronisation mit anderen Apps nicht beeinflussen und nicht mal sehen wann es stattfindet. Sehr ärgerlich, dass das Bonus-Programm genau diese dumme App in Kauf nimmt und nicht die vernunftige von meinem Fitnesstracker...

Ansich finde ich die App sehr gut. Aber nachdem meine Schritte nicht mehr aufgezeichnet worden sind habe ich die App deinstalliert. Jetzt habe ich die App neu installiert, kann mich aber nicht mehr anmelden. Dauernd kommt ich soll meine Internet verbindung checken. Diese ist aber gut...

Ich bin nicht die einzige, die das Problem mit Aktivitätsminuten und Kartiopunkten hat? Ich dachte schon, es liegt an meiner neuen Uhr, weil es etwa zur gleichen Zeit angefangen hat. Da es nicht an meiner Uhr zu liegen scheint. Liebes GoogleFit-Team, findet den Fehler und behebt ihn. Die App hat immer so gut funktioniert. Hat fein Schritte gezählt und kardiopunkte. Wusste genau, wie lange ich draußen war und wo ich lang bin... Warum werden funktionierende Apps immer kaputtgeupdatet?

Seit letzten Update funktionierts nicht mehr. Schritte werden gezählt, habe aber keine km. Die bleiben bei 0. Oder Springen dann mal auf 0,8 ne Stunde später sind es dann 0,2 km. Km wurden auch auf dem Laufband angezeigt, warum funktioniert das einfach nicht mehr? Vorher gings. Habe die Fehlerbehebung nach schon ausgeführt nichts. Schade das damit meine verbunden Apps keine Km angezeigt bekommen. Wenn man wenigstens die km die man per Hand einfügen an die verbundenen Apps weiterleiten könnte!

gist: However, it is a little annoying that fit does not do a better job of
text: Fit has done a great job updating itself. However, it is a little annoying that fit does not do a better job of showing sleep tracking breakdown into rem, deep sleep, and light sleep synced from outside apps. Also, I wouldn't mind if you could change the goals a little more like the original or set weekly instead of daily goals and maybe have a 'do 10 heart points today to stay on track for the week' statement. Some other minor complaints, but these are the main ones.

gist: data or widget not syncing or updating
text: Nicht zu empfehlen für eine Synchronisation mit anderen Fit-Apps. Gestern wurden mir 8000 Schritte unterschlagen und generell ist die Übertragung der Schritte eher schlecht. Ich nutze es für das Bonusprogramm meiner Krankenkasse und dachte eigentlich bei "Google" kann man nichts falsch machen...war wohl ein Irrtum. Die Antwort auf diese Rezession ist wohl ein Scherz! Kann ich nicht nachvollziehen...wir gesagt, nicht empfehlenswert.

gist: No ads quick and responsive covers every fitness exercise you could wish for.
text: Love this app. Have tried almost every other similar app I can find and like this the best. No ads quick and responsive covers every fitness exercise you could wish for. Maps and distance are accurate as I have checked against a garmin cycle sat nav. Free and as its free what's not to like except can't find a way to link to social media like other apps do. Best feature is auto record feature so you dont have to remember to set app torecord, as long as you have your phone on you and its switched on it senses your activity and records it for you. Very clever and very handy

gist: Now when I start the activity (for example, walking), only the calories is getting counted
text: I really enjoyed this app for the first couple of days, until the app started having issues in the steps, kms, and pace count. Now when I start the activity (for example, walking), only the calories is getting counted but the rest three counter such as steps, kms, and pace are showing zero. These three do not work at all. I'm sorry I had to give only 2 stars. If there was no problem, I'd have given it a 4 stars.

Eine gute App. Jedoch würde ich mir wünsche das man mit dieser App auch in Verbindung mit Wear OS sein schwimmen tracken lassen kann. Man kann ja schließlich auch andere Sportarten tracken lassen, die im Wasser passieren (z.B. Rudern). Darüber hinaus wäre es toll wenn man seinen Schlaf tracken bzw. Analysieren lassen kann (auch ggf. mit Wear OS). Ansonsten eine wirklich gute App.

gist: Update: erroneous tracking doesn't seem to be an issue anymore.
text: Update: erroneous tracking doesn't seem to be an issue anymore. However as far as weight tracking, it's still not very useful as Fit no longer has a web dashboard and the app is very limited in how it allows you to view data. For example the 3 month view for a January date shows January through March when November through January (last 3 months) would be more useful. Completely unable to slide the time-frames when viewing logs.

gist: The lack of quick selection options in the notification is a massive oversight.
text: This is one of those times when the 'new and improved' version fails to deliver on basic functionality. I've now lost two 30 minute sessions due to the app just doing nothing after ending workout. The lack of quick selection options in the notification is a massive oversight. This app is absolute trash.

Als Orientierung ganz okay und Motivation ist immer gut. Allerdings erkennt die App regelmäßig nicht, wenn ich Rad fahre. Bin ich zu schnell?? Auch Läufe werden nur unzureichend aufgezeichnet. Das geht sicher besser. Dennoch von mir Daumen hoch

Ich habe die App wieder mal installiert um zu sehen ob sie verbessert wurde. NEIN! Sie zählt nachwievor willkürlich Schritte und Kalorien. Bin heute z. B. 1 Stunde, 9500 Schritte und 6,5 km gelaufen. Was sagt die App? 11 Minuten, 900 Schritte und 0,55 km. Ein Witz!! Aber manche Tage zählt sie schon richtig.. Man muss halt diesen Tag erwischen. 😉😕 Mehr wie einen Stern ist sie nicht wert.

gist: data or widget not syncing or updating
text: Keinerlei Synchronisation mehr mit Polar und Withings. Kommt Leute, das kann doch nicht sein, dass das alle 2 Monate zu nem spontanen Disconnect kommt.

gist: I consistently earn far more points from a slow walk than from running the same
text: The step and distance accuracy for running just keeps getting worse. In the latest version, heart points are also being incorrectly calculated. I consistently earn far more points from a slow walk than from running the same time/distance. I think an intern got the sign reversed on the calculation, because I cannot otherwise rationally explain how running for 40 minutes gets 11 points but walking the same time gets 80 points.

gist: Doesn't track activity at all, have uninstalled and reinstalled app, given all permission, linked and
text: Doesn't track activity at all, have uninstalled and reinstalled app, given all permission, linked and unlinked apps, already followed the steps in the help section. Nothing seems to be working. Just randomly stopped tracking activity about a week ago for no reason. Contacted support through the app and still haven't heard anything.

Laut der App habe ich mich seit 4 Tagen nicht 1 Schritt bewegt. Schade. Joggen, mehrstündiges Wandern, Gehen wird nicht aufgezeichnet. Wäre es möglich die AOK App mit einem anderen Tracker zu verknüpfen, hätte ich die G.Fit längst gelöscht. Absolut unbrauchbar.

gist: calorie numbers inaccurate or differ from Apple Health
text: Funktioniert nicht gut mit Radfahren, somit für mich nicht benutzbar. Radtouren werden oft nicht erfasst oder die Zeit stimmt nicht. Außerdem werden Radtouren erzeugt obwohl ich daheim auf der Couch gesessen bin und den ganzen Tag nicht Rad gefahren bin. Auch gibt es Touren mit 0 Kilometern aber einer Zeitangabe z.B. 6 Minuten. Wie kann man eine Fortbewegung mit 0 km/h als Radfahren deklarieren, wenn man sie schon erfassen muss, was auch schon sinnfrei ist.

Warum auch immer wird die Strecke nicht mehr korrekt erfasst. Die Kilometeranzahl stimmt allerdings ist der Streckenverlauf komplett falsch und das obwohl ich das Tracking manuell gestartet habe. Das ging bis vor einiger Zeit noch besser. Desweiteren stimmt die Strecke auch nicht mit der bei Google Maps hinterlegten überein.

Die App wird seit Jahren kaum noch gepflegt. Im Vergleich zu anderen Gesundheit App sehr dürftig. Nur Gewicht und Sport Einheiten Tracking sind mittlerweile zu wenig. Update: bei Rundwege mit dem Fahrrad misst Google die Entfernung zwischen Start und Stop, nicht nicht den zurück gelegten weg. Beispiel für 0,16 km habe ich 65 Minuten gebraucht. Sehr sinnvoll 😉

GARBAGE APP, indeed

gist: calorie numbers inaccurate or differ from Apple Health
text: Wenn ich jede Aktivität in der App selber starten muss... nein danke. Hat sich auch im Laufe der Jahre nichts verbessert. Immer noch sehr ungenau, also nicht zu gebrauchen. Widget ist noch schlimmer.

Zählt Schritte nur teilweise. Oft wird die zurückgelegte Strecke nicht angezeigt. Wie kann das sein? Normalerweise so als App unbrauchbar!!! gist: Steps work for tracking some things, like walking and running, but they do not work
text: They changed the app from tracking minutes exercised to tracking steps, a change I disagree with. Steps work for tracking some things, like walking and running, but they do not work for other forms of exercise, such as bicycling and things where you shouldn't be carrying a phone or other electronic equipment. Please make it possible to choose whether we want to use steps or minutes.

gist: I cannot figure out how to change the stride length.
text: It'll be nice if they ever get it working. Step counter is WAY off. I cannot figure out how to change the stride length. I am a short man with short legs and a 28" stride. Went for a 6 mile walk on a known accurately measured trail. By the time I was at the 4.5 mile mark, it said 6 miles, by the time I got to the 6 mile mark, it clocked me as 7.1 miles. Going back to MapMyFitness. It works. 3 years later, not much improvement. Getting it to connect with different devices is a nightmare

Die App ist wirklich super... Ich finde es aber sehr schade, dass die Funktion Aktivitätsminuten durch Schritte ersetzt wurde. Die Schritte konnte man doch vorher auch ablesen und jeder der das Ziel hatte, mehr Schritte zu laufen, hätte es so auch tun können. Die Aktivitätsminuten waren toll und meine Motivation. Hoffe sehr das diese wiederkommen.

gist: I primarily had goals for my in home yoga work outs and occasionally walking but
text: Extremely upset with the change to the main focus being on steps. I likes the fact that Fit looked at every moment counting. I primarily had goals for my in home yoga work outs and occasionally walking but now it's more difficult to see and track movements. I don't want a step tracker, I want something to track my less step related activities. I get that a lot of people want step trackers but you should at least give us the options to change out the rings to best suit our tracking needs.

gist: data or widget not syncing or updating

Jetzt würde auf Schritte allein umgestellt. Wahnsinniger Verlust an Qualität. Warum nicht dem User die Auswahl geben? Ich werde die App nicht weiter nutzen, wenn das nicht behoben wird. Wirklich schade.

Schade, dass seit dem neusten Update statt der Aktivitätsminuten die Schritte zur persönlichen Zielerreichung herangezogen werden: Während vieler Stunden Fahrradfahren, Schwimmen und den meisten anderen Tätigkeiten zählt die App verständlicherweise keine Schritte. Dadurch ist es nun aber unmöglich die Ziele zu erreichen, da sie sich nun an Schritten orientieren. Äußerst demotivierend. Update: Anstatt 2 Sternen nun quasi 0 - nichtmal das automatische Aufzeichnen von Radtouren geht noch.

Nutze diese App schon lange, aber das letzte Update war und ist richtig blöd! Warum nur noch Schritte und keine Möglichkeit für Aktivitätsminuten? Das geht gar nicht! Das Feedback hier von allen Leuten sollte Ihnen doch wohl reichen

gist: It used to estimate calories and steps, fairly accurately, when you added an activity, but

I think mileage can be off up to 10%. Also, started crashing all the time today. My have to reinstall SportsTracker.

Mir scheint, dass die App keine Daten erfasst, wenn der Starschirm von Android durch eine PIN gesichert ist. Hat jemand Ähnliches beobachtet?

Die App wird immer schlechter. Ständig fehlen Schritte. Die Strecken werden nur bruchhaft bis gar nicht aufgezeichnet. This latest update is garbage. I actually like getting a step count, but I also want accurate distances. Over 5K steps is only 1.38 miles? I don't think so! The app doesn't cou t round trip mileage. Oh, and if you try to edit the journal? The app crashes. Time to look into a better app.
Automatisch erfasste Kilometer werden immer wieder automatisch auf 0 gesetzt - zuerst werden die km korrekt erfasst - nach ein paar Stunden sind die km leer.

B. dass mir 6 statt 8 km angezeigt werden oder 15 statt 19. Das ist sehr ärgerlich. Am GPS kann es nicht liegen. Andere Apps haben durchgehend ein Signal, aber fit zeichnet einfach die Luftlinie ein und misst entsprechend.

text: Oh my god, this new update where it insists on tracking steps is so annoying--like, that's fine as an option for people, but most of my exercise comes from biking, swimming and weight lifting, so no matter how active I am, this app will always declare that I'm failing to meet the goals it's forced me to set. Seit dem letzten Update will die App nicht mehr starten, sie stürzt immer beim Öffnen ab. Cache und Daten löschen bringen nichts. Da ist wohl was schief gelaufen. Edit: das Problem wurde behoben und nun passt alles. Danke!

Optisch ganz gut gemacht. Nur dieses ständige aufpoppen der WHO Meldung stört und es gibt keine Möglichkeit das Fitnessband zu verbinden. Es scheint leider unterschiedliche Versionen von Google Fit zu geben. Auf meiner Fossil SmartWatch der 5. Generation ist es zum Beispiel nicht möglich die Sportart "Schwimmen" zu tracken. Hier muss man auf alternative Apps zurückgreifen. Allerdings funktioniert auch die Übernahme der Daten in Fit nicht. Für mich absolut unverständlich und ein Grund auf Google Fit zu verzichten.

gist: However today my points disappeared and my steps halved!
text: I love this app and have used it for years. Developers listened and got the steps back in addition to move points which was great. However today my points disappeared and my steps halved! I've done 15000 steps, which initially came up along with points only to disappear an hour or so later! This has never happened before. My Google Fit is connected to MyFitness tracker to stay on top of kcal intake etc, so loosing steps is very disruptive! I have send feedback via app. Really hoping for a fix!

Crashes frequently. Same issue across two mobiles! Please fix. Update is not good, as it now seems to be oversimplified at the expense of other things. Editing is poor. If you're after all the bells and whistles, this app is not for you. If you're after basic free logging, fill your boots. 22/06/20 - this is getting worse. This isn't logging distances properly. No web app any more. This is now too dumbed down.

gist: It's worked for a couple of weeks, but now borked again.

gist: wants calories burned focus over heart points

gist: when it works it's fantastic, but it rarely works.

Dafür funktioniert die automatische Erkennung von Aktivitäten inzwischen, wobei die Distanzen und die zurück gelegten Wege nur zur groben Orientierung dienen.

gist: :( The update added one good feature, but removed two.
text: Bring the polygon back! :( The update added one good feature, but removed two. I guess cyclists do not like being forced to switch to steps. Good to see the choice for the beginning of the week. Now just need to bring the good stuff back.

gist: However, this data is useless so far.
text: I use it from the day one and have accumulated a substantial amount of data. However, this data is useless so far. Will be great to have a year-over-year comparison of monthly or weekly results, other metrics in addition to "hearts". Weekly and monthly graphs are not convenient. As an example, how to use data, take a look at "Sleep like Android" app.

Leider zeichnet die App nicht jede Aktivität automatisch auf. Wenn sje wenigstens die Schritte dabei zuverlässig zählen würde, wäre das ja schon etwas. Stattdessen zeichnet die App oft, aber eben nicht immer die Aktivitäten automatisch auf, sodass man es ständig vergisst, bei längeren Läufen die Verfolgung automatisch einzustellen (obwohl es auch dann selten funktioniert).

Nach inzwischen einigen Jahren Nutzung und einer positiven Entwicklung der App, korrigiere ich hiermit meine Bewertung von 2 auf 4 Sterne. Die App funktioniert inzwischen sehr zuverlässig, ohne Abstürze und Hänger, was in der Vergangenheit noch der Fall gewesen ist. Was besonders gut gefällt ist die Akku schonende Hintergrund-Aktivität. Der Schrittzähler funktioniert relativ zuverlässig und das Punktesystem, auch wenn es teilweise sehr unlogisch ist, motiviert einen sich regelmäßig zu bewegen.

gist: This app has over simplified itself to the point of being useless.
text: This app has over simplified itself to the point of being useless. I really want to like it because it seems like it should be better than it is. Stationary activities (treadmill, biking) are always way off. In a 30 minute treadmill run, Fit will show that I have run more than .5 miles more than actually ran. What's worse, there is no way to edit the distance or calibrate the tracker. The limited amount of goals it will track is also disappointing.

gist: Probably the worst health tracking app available.
text: Probably the worst health tracking app available. I think an Excel spreadsheet would be better. It fails at everything it says it's supposed to do. Randomly stops syncing with fitness trackers. They should have kept the web version of fit. At least you could edit your information. Now it's only mobile and the interface is terrible. Plus, there's no information about how they're calculating your points when it does work. Sleep tracking doesn't work at all either. -10 stars! Worst app!!

gist: At least add common ones like waist measures, body fat, calories and nutrition intake.
text: Great app as a central hub to sync among various other health app for workouts and food diary. Meanwhile, it's also not good enough as a central hub cuz the amount of info got synced is just simply not enough. At least add common ones like waist measures, body fat, calories and nutrition intake. This app has so much potential.

Jetzt hat es mal 2 Tage super funktioniert heute habe ich wieder 3000 schritte weniger als auf meiner Fitness App !!!! Sehr schwache Leistung!!!!

text: It doesn't allow you to post your activities on Facebook. It also doesn't allow you to do reporting by month or year. Latest version barely works. It doesnt properly record distances for distance walking. I walked 25km yesterday and google fit only recorded 2 km

Das ich eine seiner mit meinem Kind auf dem Arm durch das Haus laufe und anschließend nur 200 Schritte mehr habe, ist schon demotivierend, aber noch akzeptable, da ich mir Mühe gebe dabei möglichst sanft aufzutreten. Was mich aber wirklich stört: Es passiert häufiger, dass man gezählte Schritte verliert. Gerade hatte ich noch 5900, dann gehe ich etwas weiter und habe nur noch 5500. Sehr frustrierend!

UNBRAUCHBAR!! Alle erforderlichen Zugriffe und Berechtigungen gesetzt (mehrfach kontrolliert)! In den letzten 16 Tagen für die immer gleiche Runde (4,84km, um 40min) genau sechs mal ein brauchbares Ergebnis: ca. 5.600 Schritte. Die anderen Angaben differenzieren zwischen 1.400 und 3.200 Schritten. "Ausreißer" nach unten: 128 Schritte, 70 Schritte und Heute: 5 Schritte !!! Die App gehört auf den Müllhaufen der Technik-Geschichte! Habe seit ein paar Wochen Google fit installiert und musste mehrfach feststellen, dass es s e h r erhebliche Differenzen zwischen real zurückgelegter Strecke / Anzahl Schritte und dem Ergebnis der App gibt. Exemplarisch: 1.242 Schritte für 4,82 km??? Und Selbiges mehrfach in ähnlicher Dimension..... (meist läuft "komoot" mit, was zu der nachweisfähigen Aussage führt...) Resumeé: Google fit ist definitiv NICHT ZU EMPFEHLEN!

gist: Used to be great, but Aug 2018 & later ruined it.
text: Used to be great, but Aug 2018 & later ruined it. It's useless if I can't track my own workout goal. Heart & Move minutes don't help anyone who actually works out! Workout goals per week is such a simple, useful thing that Fit used to have, and then you dropped it. Why?! The widget and wearOS app used to work well. This is not UCD. People need to be able to set their own goals for their own types of workouts and then track against those goals. Basic!

gist: I cannot customise the activities individually and goals.
text: The move minutes resets itself and provides an inaccurate value after reaching the goal. I cannot customise the activities individually and goals. Needs a lot of improvement. Does not connect with Garmin device. Additionally, it misses a lot of steps. I manually counted my steps during my walk, and there was a difference of 25%.

Ihr habt mich quasi über die Jahre vergrault und zu Garmin getrieben. Mach es gut Google Fit. Wir passen nicht mehr zusammen.
